s.en: We can read of things that happened 5,000 years ago in the Near East, where people first learned to write.
s.zh: 我们从书籍中可读到5,000 年前近东发生的事情，那里的人最早学会了写字。

s.en: But there are some parts of the world where even now people cannot write.
s.zh: 但直到现在,世界上有些地方，人们还不会书写。

s.en: The only way that they can preserve their history is to recount it as sagas--legends handed down from one generation to another.
s.zh: 他们保存历史的唯一办法是将历史当作传说讲述，由讲述人一代接一代地将史实描述为传奇故事口传下来。

s.en: These legends are useful because they can tell us something about migrations of people who lived long ago,
s.zh: 这些传说很有用，因为它们可以告诉我们很久以前人们的迁徙，

s.en: but none could write down what they did.
s.zh: 但没有人能写下他们做了什么。

s.en: Anthropologists wondered where the remote ancestors of the Polynesian peoples now living in the Pacific Islands came from.
s.zh: 人类学家想知道现在生活在太平洋岛屿上的波利尼西亚人的祖先来自哪里。

s.en: The sagas of these people explain that some of them came from Indonesia about 2,000 years ago.
s.zh: 这些人的传说解释说，他们中的一些人大约在2000年前来自印度尼西亚。

s.en: But the first people who were like ourselves lived so long ago that even their sagas, if they had any, are forgotten.
s.zh: 但是，与我们相似的第一批人生活在很久以前，即使他们有传奇故事，也被遗忘了。

s.en: So archaeologists have neither history nor legends to help them to find out where the first 'modern men' came from.
s.zh: 因此，考古学家既没有历史也没有传说来帮助他们找出第一批“现代人”来自哪里。

s.en: Fortunately, however, ancient men made tools of stone, especially flint,
s.zh: 然而，幸运的是，古人用石头，尤其是燧石制作了工具，

s.en: because this is easier to shape than other kinds.
s.zh: 因为这比其他种类更容易成形。

s.en: They may also have used wood and skins, but these have rotted away.
s.zh: 他们也可能使用木头和兽皮，但这些都腐烂了。

s.en: Stone does not decay,
s.zh: 石头不会腐烂，

s.en: and so the tools of long ago have remained when even the bones of the men who made them have disappeared without trace.
s.zh: 所以，很久以前的工具保存了下来，而制造这些工具的人的骨头却消失得无影无踪。

q: Why are legends handed down by storytellers useful?
为什么说书人流传下来的传说很有用？

s.en: Why, you may wonder, should spiders be our friends?
s.zh: 你可能会觉得奇怪， 蜘蛛怎么会是我们的朋友呢？

s.en: Because they destroy so many insects,
s.zh: 因为它们能消灭那么多的昆虫，

s.en: and insects include some of the greatest enemies of the human race.
s.zh: 其中包括一些人类的大敌。

s.en: Insects would make it impossible for us to live in the world;
s.zh: 昆虫就会使我们无法在地球上生活下去；

s.en: they would devour all our crops and kill our flocks and herds, if it were not for the protection we get from insect-eating animals.
s.zh: 要不是人类受一些食虫动物的保护，昆虫会吞食我们的全部庄稼，杀死我们的成群的牛羊。

s.en: We owe a lot to the birds and beasts who eat insects but all of them put together kill only a fraction of the number destroyed by spiders.
s.zh: 我们要十分感谢那些吃昆虫的鸟和兽，然而把它们所杀死的昆虫全部加在一起也只相当于蜘蛛所消灭的一小部分。

s.en: Moreover, unlike some of the other insect eaters, spiders never do harm to us or our belongings.
s.zh: 此外，蜘蛛不同于其他食虫动物，它们丝毫不危害我们和我们的财物。

s.en: Spiders are not insects, as many people think, nor even nearly related to them.
s.zh: 许多人认为蜘蛛是昆虫，但它们不是昆虫，甚至与昆虫也没有近亲关系。

s.en: One can tell the difference almost at a glance, for a spider always has eight legs and an insect never more than six.
s.zh: 人们几乎一眼就能看出二者的差异，因为蜘蛛都是 8 条腿，而昆虫的腿从不超过 6 条。

s.en: How many spiders are engaged in this work on our behalf?
s.zh: 有多少蜘蛛在为我们效力呢？

s.en: One authority on spiders made a census of the spiders in a grass field in the south of England,
s.zh: 一位研究蜘蛛的权威对英国南部一块草坪上的蜘蛛作了一次调查，

s.en: and he estimated that there were more than 2,250,000 in one acre;
s.zh: 他估计每英亩草坪里有 225 万多只蜘蛛；

s.en: that is something like 6,000,000 spiders of different kinds on a football pitch.
s.zh: 这就是说，在一个足球场上约有 600 万只不同种类的蜘蛛。

s.en: Spiders are busy for at least half the year in killing insects.
s.zh: 蜘蛛至少有半年在忙于吃昆虫。

s.en: It is impossible to make more than the wildest guess at how many they kill,
s.zh: 它们一年中消灭了多少昆虫，我们简直无法猜测，

s.en: but they are hungry creatures, not content with only three meals a day.
s.zh: 它们是吃不饱的动物，不满意一日三餐。

s.en: It has been estimated that the weight of all the insects destroyed by spiders in Britain in one year would be greater than the total weight of all the human beings in the country.
s.zh: 据估计，在英国蜘蛛一年里所消灭昆虫的重量超过这个国家人口的总重量。

q: How much of each year do spiders spend killing insects?
蜘蛛每年有多少时间用于捕杀昆虫？
q2: T. H. Gillesple Spare that spider from The Listener
T.H.Gillesple 把蜘蛛从《倾听者》中解救出来

s.en: Modern alpinists try to climb mountains by a route which will give them good sport,
s.zh: 现代登山运动员总想找一条能够给他们带来运动乐趣的路线来攀登山峰，

s.en: and the more difficult it is, the more highly it is regarded.
s.zh: 他们认为， 道路愈艰险愈带劲儿。

s.en: In the pioneering days, however, this was not the case at all.
s.zh: 然而，在登山运动的初期，全然不是这种情况。

s.en: The early climbers were looking for the easiest way to the top,
s.zh: 早期登山者所寻找的是通往山顶的最方便的途径，

s.en: because the summit was the prize they sought, especially if it had never been attained before.
s.zh: 因为顶峰特别是前人未曾到过的顶峰 -- 才是他们寻求的目标。

s.en: It is true that during their explorations they often faced difficulties and dangers of the most perilous nature, equipped in a manner which would make a modern climber shudder at the thought,
s.zh: 确实，在探险中他们经常遇到惊心动魄的困难和危险，而他们装备之简陋足以使现代登山者一想起来就胆战心惊，

s.en: but they did not go out of their way to court such excitement.
s.zh: 但是，他们并非故意寻求这种刺激，

s.en: They had a single aim, a solitary goal--the top!
s.zh: 他们只有一个目标，唯一的目标 -- 顶峰！

s.en: It is hard for us to realize nowadays how difficult it was for the pioneers.
s.zh: 我们今天很难想像昔日的登山先驱们是多么艰苦。

s.en: Except for one or two places such as Zermatt and Chamonix, which had rapidly become popular, Alpine villages tended to be impoverished settlements cut off from civilization by the high mountains.
s.zh: 除了泽曼特和夏蒙尼等一两个很快出了名的地方外，阿尔卑斯山山区的小村几乎全是高山环抱、与世隔绝的穷乡僻壤。

s.en: Such inns as there were were generally dirty and flea-ridden;
s.zh: 那里的小客栈一般都很肮脏，而且跳蚤猖獗。

s.en: the food simply local cheese accompanied by bread often twelve months old, all washed down with coarse wine.
s.zh: 食物是当地的干酪和通常存放了一年之久的面包，人们就着劣酒吞下这种食物。

s.en: Often a valley boasted no inn at all,
s.zh: 山谷里常常没有小客栈，

s.en: and climbers found shelter wherever they could--sometimes with the local priest (who was usually as poor as his parishioners), sometimes with shepherds or cheese-makers.
s.zh: 登山者只好随遇而安。有时同当地牧师 （他通常和他的教民一样穷）住在一起，有时同牧羊人或制乳酪的人住在一起。

s.en: Invariably the background was the same: dirt and poverty, and very uncomfortable.
s.zh: 无论住在哪儿，情况都一样：肮脏、贫穷，极其不舒适。

s.en: For men accustomed to eating seven-course dinners and sleeping between fine linen sheets at home, the change to the Alps must have been very hard indeed.
s.zh: 对于过惯了一顿饭吃 7 道菜、睡亚麻细布床单的人来说，变换一下生活环境来到阿尔卑斯山山区，那一定是很艰难的。

q: What was the main objective of early mountain climbers?
早期登山者的主要目标是什么？

s.en: Several cases have been reported in Russia recently of people who can read and detect colours with their fingers, and even see through solid doors and walls.
s.zh: 俄罗斯最近报导了几个事例，有人能用手指看书识字和辨认颜色，甚至能透过厚实的门和墙看到东西。

s.en: One case concerns an eleven-year-old schoolgirl, Vera Petrova, who has normal vision but who can also perceive things with different parts of her skin, and through solid walls.
s.zh: 其中有一例谈到有一个名叫维拉 • 彼托洛娃的11岁学生。她的视力与常人一样，但她还能用皮肤的不同部位辨认东西，甚至看穿坚实的墙壁。

s.en: This ability was first noticed by her father.
s.zh: 是她父亲首先发现她这一功能的。

s.en: One day she came into his office and happened to put her hands on the door of a locked safe.
s.zh: 一天，维拉走进父亲的办公室，偶然把手放在一个锁着的保险柜的门上。

s.en: Suddenly she asked her father why he kept so many old newspapers locked away there,
s.zh: 她突然问父亲为什么把这么多的旧报纸锁在柜子里，

s.en: and even described the way they were done up in bundles.
s.zh: 还说了报纸捆扎的情况。

s.en: Vera's curious talent was brought to the notice of a scientific research institute in the town of Ulyanovsk, near where she lives,
s.zh: 维拉的特异功能引起了她家附近乌里扬诺夫斯克城一个科研单位的注意。

s.en: and in April she was given a series of tests by a special commission of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federal Republic.
s.zh: 4 月里，俄罗斯卫生部一个特别委员会对她进行了一系列的测试。

s.en: During these tests she was able to read a newspaper through an opaque screen and, stranger still, by moving her elbow over a child's game of Lotto she was able to describe the figures and colours printed on it;
s.zh: 在这些测试中，她能隔着不透明的屏幕读报纸。更为奇怪的是，她把肘部在儿童玩的“罗托”纸牌上移动一下，便能说出印在纸牌上的数字和颜色。

s.en: and, in another instance, wearing stockings and slippers, to make out with her foot the outlines and colours of a picture hidden under a carpet.
s.zh: 还有一次，她穿着长筒袜子和拖鞋，能用脚识别出藏在地毯下面的一幅画的轮廓和颜色。

s.en: Other experiments showed that her knees and shoulders had a similar sensitivity.
s.zh: 其他实验表明，她的膝盖和双肩有类似的感觉能力，

s.en: During all these tests Vera was blindfold; and, indeed, except when blindfold she lacked the ability to perceive things with her skin.
s.zh: 在所有这些实验中，维拉的双眼都是蒙着的。如果不蒙上双眼她的皮肤就不再具有识别物体的能力。

s.en: It was also found that although she could perceive things with her fingers this ability ceased the moment her hands were wet.
s.zh: 这是千真万确的。同时还发现，尽管她能用手指识别东西，但她的手一旦弄湿，这种功能便会立即消失。

q: How did Vera disover she had this gift of second sight?
最近俄罗斯报道了几起案例：有些人能用手指识别和感知颜色，甚至能看穿坚固的门和墙壁。
q2: ERIC DE MAUNY Seeing hands from The Listener
埃里克·德·穆尼 看到听众的手

s.en: People are always talking about 'the problem of youth'.
s.zh: 人们总是在谈论“青年问题”。

s.en: If there is one -- which I take leave to doubt -- then it is older people who create it, not the young themselves.
s.zh: 如果这个问题存在的话 -- 请允许我对此持怀疑态度 -- 那么，这个问题是由老年人而不是青年人造成的。

s.en: Let us get down to fundamentals and agree that the young are after all human beings -- people just like their elders.
s.zh: 让我们来认真研究一些基本事实：承认青年人和他们的长辈一样也是人。

s.en: There is only one difference between an old man and a young one: the young man has a glorious future before him and the old one has a splendid past behind him: and maybe that is where the rub is.
s.zh: 老年人和青年人只有一个区别：青年人有光辉灿烂的前景，而老年人的辉煌已成为过去。 问题的症结恐怕就在这里。

s.en: When I was a teenager, I felt that I was just young and uncertain
s.zh: 我十几岁时，总感到自己年轻，有些事拿不准

s.en: -- that I was a new boy in a huge school, and I would have been very pleased to be regarded as something so interesting as a problem.
s.zh: -- 我是一所大学里的一名新生，如果我当时真的被看成像一个问题那样有趣，我会感到很得意的。

s.en: For one thing, being a problem gives you a certain identity,
s.zh: 因为这至少使我得到了某种承认 ，

s.en: and that is one of the things the young are busily engaged in seeking.
s.zh: 这正是年轻人所热衷追求的。

s.en: I find young people exciting.
s.zh: 我觉得年轻人令人振奋。

s.en: They have an air of freedom,
s.zh: 无拘无束，

s.en: and they have not a dreary commitment to mean ambitions or love of comfort.
s.zh: 他们既不追逐卑鄙的名利，也不贪图生活的舒适。

s.en: They are not anxious social climbers, and they have no devotion to material things.
s.zh: 他们不热衷于向上爬，也不一味追求物质享受。

s.en: All this seems to me to link them with life, and the origins of things.
s.zh: 在我看来，所有这些使他们与生命和万物之源联系在了一起。

s.en: It's as if they were, in some sense, cosmic beings in violent and lovely contrast with us suburban creatures.
s.zh: 从某种意义上讲，他们似乎是宇宙人，同我们这些凡夫俗子形成了强烈而鲜明的对照。

s.en: All that is in my mind when I meet a young person. He may be conceited, ill-mannered, presumptuous or fatuous,
s.zh: 每逢我遇到年轻人，脑子里就想到这些年轻人也许狂妄自负，举止无理，傲慢放肆，愚昧无知，

s.en: but I do not turn for protection to dreary clichés about respect for elders -- as if mere age were a reason for respect.
s.zh: 但我不会用应当尊重长者这一套陈词滥调来为我自己辩护，似乎年长就是受人尊敬的理由。

s.en: I accept that we are equals,
s.zh: 我认为我和他们是平等的，

s.en: and I will argue with him, as an equal, if I think he is wrong.
s.zh: 如果我认为他们错了，我就以平等的身份和他们争个明白。

q: How does the writer like to treat young people?
人们总是在谈论‘年轻人的问题’。
q2: FIELDEN HUGHES from Out of the Air, The Listener
《听众》中的菲尔登突然大笑起来

s.en: I am always amazed when I hear people saying that sport creates goodwill between the nations,
s.zh: 我总是惊愕不已，当我听人们说体育运动可创造国家之间的友谊，

s.en: and that if only the common peoples of the world could meet one another at football or cricket,
s.zh: 还说各国民众若在足球场或板球场上交锋，

s.en: they would have no inclination to meet on the battlefield.
s.zh: 就不愿在战场上残杀的时候。

s.en: Even if one didn't know from concrete examples (the 1936 Olympic Games, for instance) that international sporting contests lead to orgies of hatred,
s.zh: 一个人即使不能从具体的事例（例如1936年的奥林匹克运动会）了解到国际运动比赛会导致疯狂的仇恨，

s.en: one could deduce it from general principles.
s.zh: 也可以从常理中推断出结论。

s.en: Nearly all the sports practised nowadays are competitive.
s.zh: 现在开展的体育运动几乎都是竞争性的。

s.en: You play to win, and the game has little meaning unless you do your utmost to win.
s.zh: 参加比赛就是为了取胜。如果不拚命去赢，比赛就没有什么意义了。

s.en: On the village green, where you pick up sides and no feeling of local patriotism is involved,
s.zh: 在乡间的草坪上，当你随意组成两个队，并且不涉及任何地方情绪时，

s.en: it is possible to play simply for the fun and exercise:
s.zh: 那才可能是单纯的为了娱乐和锻炼而进行比赛。

s.en: but as soon as the question of prestige arises,
s.zh: 可是一旦涉及到荣誉问题，

s.en: as soon as you feel that you and some larger unit will be disgraced if you lose,
s.zh: 一旦你想到你和某一团体会因为你输而丢脸时，

s.en: the most savage combative instincts are aroused.
s.zh: 那么最野蛮的争斗天性便会激发起来。

s.en: Anyone who has played even in a school football match knows this.
s.zh: 即使是仅仅参加过学校足球赛的人也有这种体会。

s.en: At the international level, sport is frankly mimic warfare.
s.zh: 在国际比赛中，体育简直是一场模拟战争。

s.en: But the significant thing is not the behaviour of the players but the attitude of the spectators: and, behind the spectators, of the nations who work themselves into furies over these absurd contests,
s.zh: 但是，要紧的还不是运动员的行为，而是观众的态度， 以及观众身后各个国家的态度。面对着这些荒唐的比赛，参赛的各个国家会如痴如狂，

s.en: and seriously believe -- at any rate for short periods — that running, jumping and kicking a ball are tests of national virtue.
s.zh: 甚至煞有介事地相信 — 至少在短期内如此 — 跑跑、跳跳、踢踢球是对一个民族品德素质的检验。

q: How does the writer describe sport at the international level?
作者是如何描述国际层面的体育运动的？

s.en: Not all sounds made by animals serve as language,
s.zh: 动物发出的声音不都是用作语言交际。

s.en: and we have only to turn to that extraordinary discovery of echo-location in bats to see a case in which the voice plays a strictly utilitarian role.
s.zh: 我们只要看一看蝙蝠回声定位这一极不寻常的发现，就可以探究一下声音在什么情况下有绝对的实用价值。

s.en: To get a full appreciation of what this means we must turn first to some recent human inventions.
s.zh: 要透彻理解这句话的意义，我们应先回顾一下人类最近的几项发明。

s.en: Everyone knows that if he shouts in the vicinity of a wall or a mountainside, an echo will come back.
s.zh: 大家都知道，在墙壁或山腰附近发出的喊声，就会听到回声。

s.en: The further off this solid obstruction, the longer time will elapse for the return of the echo.
s.zh: 固体障碍物越远，回声返回所用时间就越长。

s.en: A sound made by tapping on the hull of a ship will be reflected from the sea bottom,
s.zh: 敲打船体所发出的声音会从海底传回来，

s.en: and by measuring the time interval between the taps and the receipt of the echoes,
s.zh: 测出回声间隔的时间，

s.en: the depth of the sea at that point can be calculated.
s.zh: 便可算出该处海洋的深度。

s.en: So was born the echo-sounding apparatus, now in general use in ships.
s.zh: 这样就产生了目前各种船舶上普遍应用的回声探测仪。

s.en: Every solid object will reflect a sound, varying according to the size and nature of the object.
s.zh: 任何固体都反射声音，反射的声音因物体的大小和性质的不同而不同。

s.en: A shoal of fish will do this.
s.zh: 鱼群也反射声音。

s.en: So it is a comparatively simple step from locating the sea bottom to locating a shoal of fish.
s.zh: 从测定海深到测定鱼群，这一进展比较容易。

s.en: With experience, and with improved apparatus,
s.zh: 根据经验和改进了的仪器，

s.en: it is now possible not only to locate a shoal but to tell if it is herring, cod, or other well-known fish, by the pattern of its echo.
s.zh: 不仅能够确定鱼群的位置，而且可以根据鱼群回声的特点分辨出是鲱鱼、鳕鱼，还是其他人们熟悉的鱼。

s.en: It has been found that certain bats emit squeaks and by receiving the echoes,
s.zh: 人们发现，某些蝙蝠能发出尖叫声，

s.en: they can locate and steer clear of obstacles — or locate flying insects on which they feed.
s.zh: 并能通过回声来确定并躲开障碍物，或找到它们赖以为生的昆虫。

s.en: This echo-location in bats is often compared with radar, the principle of which is similar.
s.zh: 蝙蝠这种回声定位常常可与雷达相比较，其原理是相似的。

q: In what way does echo-location in bats play an utilitarian role?
并非所有动物发出的声音都起语言作用；我们只需看看蝙蝠回声定位这一非凡的发现，就能看到一个声音纯粹起实用作用的例子。
q2: MAURICE BURTON Curiosities of animal life
莫里斯·伯顿 对动物生活的好奇心

s.en: Chickens slaughtered in the United States, claim officials in Brussels, are not fit to grace European tables.
s.zh: 布鲁塞尔的官员说，在美国屠宰的鸡不适于用来装点欧洲的餐桌。

s.en: No, say the Americans: our fowl are fine, we simply clean them in a different way.
s.zh: 不，美国人说，我们的家禽很好，只是我们使用了另一种清洗方式。

s.en: These days, it is differences in national regulations, far more than tariffs, that put sand in the wheels of trade between rich countries.
s.zh: 当前，是各国管理条例上的差异，比关税更严重地阻碍了发达国家之间的贸易。

s.en: It is not just farmers who are complaining.
s.zh: 并不仅仅是农民在抱怨。

s.en: An electric razor that meets the European Union's safety standards must be approved by American testers before it can be sold in the United States,
s.zh: 一把符合欧洲联盟安全标准的电动剃须刀必须得到美国检测人员的认可，方可在美国市场上销售；

s.en: and an American-made dialysis machine needs the EU's okay before it hits the market in Europe.
s.zh: 而美国制造的透析仪也要得到欧盟的首肯才能进入欧洲市场。

s.en: As it happens, a razor that is safe in Europe is unlikely to electrocute Americans.
s.zh: 碰巧在欧洲使用安全的剃须刀不大可能使美国人触电身亡，

s.en: So, ask businesses on both sides of the Atlantic, why have two lots of tests where one would do?
s.zh: 因此，大西洋两岸的企业都在问，当一套测试可以解决问题时，为什么需要两套呢？

s.en: Politicians agree, in principle, so America and the EU have been trying to reach a deal which would eliminate the need to double-test many products.
s.zh: 政治家在原则上同意了， 因此，美国和欧洲一直在寻求达成协议，以便为许多产品取消双重检查。

s.en: They hope to finish in time for a trade summit between America and the EU on May 28th.
s.zh: 他们希望尽早达成协议，为5月28日举行的美国和欧洲贸易的最高级会议作准备。

s.en: Although negotiators are optimistic, the details are complex enough that they may be hard-pressed to get a deal at all.
s.zh: 虽然谈判代表持乐观态度，但协议细节如此复杂，他们所面临的困难很可能使他们无法取得一致。

s.en: Why? One difficulty is to construct the agreements.
s.zh: 为什么呢？困难之一是起草这些协议。

s.en: The Americans would happily reach one accord on standards for medical devices and then hammer out different pacts covering, say, electronic goods and drug manufacturing.
s.zh: 美国人很愿意就医疗器械的标准达成一个协议，然后推敲出不同的合同，用以涵盖 — 比如说 — 电子产品和药品的生产。

s.en: The EU -- following fine continental traditions -- wants agreement on general principles, which could be applied to many types of products and perhaps extended to other countries.
s.zh: 欧洲人遵循优良的大陆传统，则希望就普遍的原则取得一致，而这些原则适用于许多不同产品，同时可能延伸到其它国家。

q: What makes trading between rich countries difficult?
是什么让富裕国家之间的贸易变得如此困难呢？

s.en: Alfred the Great acted as his own spy, visiting Danish camps disguised as a minstrel.
s.zh: 阿尔弗雷德大帝曾亲自充当间谍。他扮作吟游歌手到丹麦军队的营地里侦察。

s.en: In those days wandering minstrels were welcome everywhere.
s.zh: 当时，浪迹天涯的吟游歌手到处受欢迎，

s.en: They were not fighting men, and their harp was their passport.
s.zh: 他们不是作战人员，竖琴就是他们的通行证。

s.en: Alfred had learned many of their ballads in his youth, and could vary his programme with acrobatic tricks and simple conjuring.
s.zh: 阿尔弗雷德年轻时学过许多民歌，并能穿插演一些杂技和小魔术使自己的节目多样化。

s.en: While Alfred's little army slowly began to gather at Athelney, the king himself set out to penetrate the camp of Guthrum, the commander of the Danish invaders.
s.zh: 阿尔弗雷德人数不多的军队开始在阿塞尔纳慢慢集结时，他亲自潜入丹麦入侵司令官古瑟罗姆的营地。

s.en: These had settled down for the winter at Chippenham: thither Alfred went.
s.zh: 丹麦军已在切本哈姆扎下营准备过冬，阿尔弗雷德便来到此地。

s.en: He noticed at once that discipline was slack: the Danes had the self-confidence of conquerors, and their security precautions were casual.
s.zh: 他马上发现丹麦军纪律松弛，他们以征服者自居，安全措施马马虎虎。

s.en: They lived well, on the proceeds of raids on neighbouring regions.
s.zh: 他们靠掠夺附近的地区的财物过着舒适的生活。

s.en: There they collected women as well as food and drink, and a life of ease had made them soft.
s.zh: 他们不仅搜刮吃的喝的，而且抢掠妇女，安逸的生活已使丹麦军队变得软弱无力。

s.en: Alfred stayed in the camp a week before he returned to Athelney.
s.zh: 阿尔弗雷德在敌营呆了一个星期后，回到了阿塞尔纳。

s.en: The force there assembled was trivial compared with the Danish horde.
s.zh: 他集结在那里的军队和丹麦大军相比是微不足道的。

s.en: But Alfred had deduced that the Danes were no longer fit for prolonged battle: and that their commissariat had no organization, but depended on irregular raids.
s.zh: 然而，阿尔弗雷德断定，丹麦人已不再适应持久的战争，他们的军需供应处于无组织状态，只是靠临时抢夺来维持。

s.en: So, faced with the Danish advance, Alfred did not risk open battle but harried the enemy.
s.zh: 因此，面对丹麦人的进攻，阿尔弗雷德没有贸然同敌人作战，而是采用骚扰敌人的战术。

s.en: He was constantly on the move, drawing the Danes after him.
s.zh: 他的部队不停地移动，牵着敌人的鼻子，让他们跟着跑。

s.en: His patrols halted the raiding parties: hunger assailed the Danish army.
s.zh: 他派出巡逻队阻止敌人抢劫，因而饥饿威胁着丹麦军队。

s.en: Now Alfred began a long series of skirmishes — and within a month the Danes had surrendered.
s.zh: 这时，阿尔弗雷德发起一连串小规模的进攻，结果不出一个月，丹麦人就投降了。

s.en: The episode could reasonably serve as a unique epic of royal espionage!
s.zh: 这一幕历史可以说是王室谍报活动中最精彩的篇章。

q: What important thing did King Alfred learn when he penetrated the Danish camp of Guthrum?
当阿尔弗雷德国王突袭古思伦的丹麦营地时，他学到了什么重要的东西？

s.en: Technology trends may push Silicon Valley back to the future.
s.zh: 技术的发展趋势有可能把硅谷重新推向未来。

s.en: Carver Mead, a pioneer in integrated circuits and a professor of computer science at the California Institute of Technology, notes there are now work-stations that enable engineers to design, test and produce chips right on their desks, much the way an editor creates a newsletter on a Macintosh.
s.zh: 卡弗 • 米德 — 集成电路的一位先驱，加州理工学院的计算机教授 — 注意到，现在有些计算机工作站使工程技术人员可以在他们的办公桌上设计、试验和生产芯片，就像一位编辑在苹果机上编出一份时事通讯一样。

s.en: As the time and cost of making a chip drop to a few days and a few hundred dollars, engineers may soon be free to let their imaginations soar without being penalized by expensive failures.
s.zh: 由于制造一块芯片的时间已缩短至几天，费用也只有几百美元，因此，工程技术人员可能很快就可充分发挥他们的想像力，而不会因失败而造成经济上的损失。

s.en: Mead predicts that inventors will be able to perfect powerful customized chips over a weekend at the office — spawning a new generation of garage start-ups and giving the U. S. a jump on its foreign rivals in getting new products to market fast.
s.zh: 米德预言发明者可以在办公室用一个周末的时间制造出完美的、功能很强的、按客户需求设计的芯片 — — 造就新一代从车库起家的初创公司，在把产品推向市场方面使美国把它的外国对手们打个措手不及。

s.en: 'We've got more garages with smart people,' Mead observes. 'We really thrive on anarchy.'
s.zh: “我们有更多的车库，那里有许多聪明人，”米德说。“我们确实是靠这种看似混乱状态发展起来的。”

s.en: And on Asians.
s.zh: 靠的是亚洲人。

s.en: Already, orientals and Asian Americans constitute the majority of the engineering staffs at many Valley firms.
s.zh: 硅谷许多公司中工程技术人员的大多数是东方人和亚裔美国人。

s.en: And Chinese, Korean, Filipino and Indian engineers are graduating in droves from California's colleges.
s.zh: 中国、韩国、菲律宾和印度的工程师一批批地从加州的大学毕业。

s.en: As the heads of next-generation start-ups, these Asian innovators can draw on customs and languages to forge tighter links with crucial Pacific Rim markets.
s.zh: 作为新崛起一代的带头人，亚裔发明家可以凭借他们在习惯和语言上的优势，与关键的太平洋沿岸市场建立起更加牢固的联系。

s.en: For instance, Alex Au, a Stanford Ph. D. from Hong Kong, has set up a Taiwan factory to challenge Japan's near lock on the memory-chip market.
s.zh: 比如说，亚历克斯 • 奥，一位来自香港的斯坦福大学博士，已经在台湾建厂，对日本在内存条市场上近似垄断的局面提出了挑战。

s.en: India-born N. Damodar Reddy's tiny California company reopened an AT&T chip plant in Kansas City last spring with financing from the state of Missouri.
s.zh: 印度出生的N • 达莫达 • 雷迪经营的小小的加州公司在堪萨斯城重新启用了美国电话电报公司的一家芯片工厂，并从密苏里州获取了财政上的支持。

s.en: Before it becomes a retirement village, Silicon Valley may prove a classroom for building a global business.
s.zh: 在硅谷变成一个退休村之前，如果你想成立一家世界型的大公司，硅谷就像一个教室一样，你会学到很多。

q: What does the computer industry thrive on apart from anarchy?
科技趋势可能会让硅谷重返未来。
q2: US NEWS AND WORLD REPORT, October 2, 1989
《美国新闻与世界报道》1989年10月2日

s.en: Some old people are oppressed by the fear of death.
s.zh: 有些老年人因为怕死而感到烦恼。

s.en: In the young there is a justification for this feeling.
s.zh: 青年人有这种感觉是情有可原的。

s.en: Young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle may justifiably feel bitter in the thought that they have been cheated of the best things that life has to offer.
s.zh: 有理由害怕自己会死在战场上的年轻人，想到自己被剥夺了生活所能给予的最美好的东西时，感到痛苦，这是可以理解的。

s.en: But in an old man who has known human joys and sorrows, and has achieved whatever work it was in him to do, the fear of death is somewhat abject and ignoble.
s.zh: 可是老年人已经饱尝了人间的甘苦，一切能做的都做了，如果怕死，就有点儿可怜又可鄙。

s.en: The best way to overcome it — so at least it seems to me — is to make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal, until bit by bit the walls of the ego recede, and your life becomes increasingly merged in the universal life.
s.zh: 克服怕死的最好办法 — 至少在我看来是这样 — 就是逐渐使自己的兴趣更加广泛，逐渐摆脱个人狭小的圈子，直到自我的围墙一点一点地倒塌下来，自己的生活慢慢地和整个宇宙的生活融合在一起。

s.en: An individual human existence should be like a river — small at first, narrowly contained within its banks, and rushing passionately past boulders and over waterfalls.
s.zh: 个人的存在应该像一条河流，开始很小，被紧紧地夹在两岸中间，接着热情奔放地冲过巨石，飞下瀑布。

s.en: Gradually the river grows wider, the banks recede, the waters flow more quietly, and in the end, without any visible break, they become merged in the sea, and painlessly lose their individual being.
s.zh: 然后河面渐渐地变宽，两岸后撤，河水流得平缓起来，最后连绵不断地汇入大海，毫无痛苦地失去了自我的存在

s.en: The man who, in old age, can see his life in this way, will not suffer from the fear of death, since the things he cares for will continue.
s.zh: 上了年纪的人这样看待生命，就不会有惧怕死亡的心情了，因为自己关心的一切事件都会继续下去。

s.en: And if, with the decay of vitality, weariness increases, the thought of rest will be not unwelcome.
s.zh: 再者，随着精力的衰退，老年人的疲惫会增长，有长眠的愿望未尝不是一件好事情。

s.en: I should wish to die while still at work, knowing that others will carry on what I can no longer do, and content in the thought that what was possible has been done.
s.zh: 我希望工作到死为止，明白了有人会继续我的未竟事业，想到能做的事都做了，也就坦然了。

q: What, according to the author, is the best way to overcome the fear of death as you get older?
根据作者的观点，随着年龄的增长，克服对死亡的恐惧的最佳方法是什么？

伯特兰·罗素《从记忆中的肖像看如何变老》

s.en: When anyone opens a current account at a bank, he is lending the bank money, repayment of which he may demand at any time, either in cash or by drawing a cheque in favour of another person.
s.zh: 任何人在银行开一个活期账户，就等于把钱借给了银行。这笔钱他可以随时提取，提取的方式可以是取现金，也可以是开一张以他人为收款人的支票。

s.en: Primarily, the banker-customer relationship is that of debtor and creditor — who is which depending on whether the customer's account is in credit or is overdrawn.
s.zh: 银行与储户的关系主要是债务人和债权人的关系。究竟谁是债务人谁是债权人，要看储户是有结余还是透支。

s.en: But, in addition to that basically simple concept, the bank and its customer owe a large number of obligations to one another.
s.zh: 除了这一基本的简单的概念外，银行和储户彼此还需承担大量义务。

s.en: Many of these obligations can give rise to problems and complications but a bank customer, unlike, say, a buyer of goods, cannot complain that the law is loaded against him.
s.zh: 其中许多义务往往引起问题和纠纷。但是储户不能像货物的买主那样来抱怨法律对自己不利。

s.en: The bank must obey its customer's instructions, and not those of anyone else.
s.zh: 银行必须遵照储户的嘱托办事，不能听从其他人的指令。

s.en: When, for example, a customer first opens an account, he instructs the bank to debit his account only in respect of cheques drawn by himself.
s.zh: 比如，储户首次在银行开户时，嘱咐银行他的存款只能凭本人签字的支票来提取。

s.en: He gives the bank specimens of his signature, and there is a very firm rule that the bank has no right or authority to pay out a customer's money on a cheque on which its customer's signature has been forged.
s.zh: 他把自己签名的样本交给银行，对此有一条非常严格的规定：银行没有任何权利或理由凭伪造储户签名的支票付出储户的钱。

s.en: It makes no difference that the forgery may have been a very skillful one: the bank must recognize its customer's signature.
s.zh: 即使伪造得很巧妙，也不能付款，因为银行有责任辨认出其储户的签名。

s.en: For this reason there is no risk to the customer in the practice, adopted by banks, of printing the customer's name on his cheques.
s.zh: 因此，某些银行已采用把储户姓名印在支票上的作法。这种做法对储户毫无风险。

s.en: If this facilitates forgery, it is the bank which will lose, not the customer.
s.zh: 如果因这种作法出现了伪造的话，受损失的将不是储户，而是银行。

q: Why is there no risk to the customer when a bank prints the customer's name on his cheques?
为什么当银行在客户的支票上打印客户的名字时，这对客户来说没有任何风险呢？
q2: --GORDON BARRIE and AUBREY L. DLAMOND The Consumer Society and the Law--
--戈登·巴里与奥布里·L·戴蒙德：消费者社会与法律--

s.en: Beyond two or three days, the world's best weather forecasts are speculative,
s.zh: 超过两三天，世界上最好的天气预报也只能算是推测，

s.en: and beyond six or seven they are worthless.
s.zh: 超过六七天之后，它们就毫无价值了。

s.en: The Butterfly Effect is the reason.
s.zh: 原因就在于“蝴蝶效应”。

s.en: For small pieces of weather--
s.zh: 对于那些微小的、局部天气现象——

s.en: and to a global forecaster, small can mean thunderstorms and blizzards--
s.zh: 对于全球天气预报员来说，“小”可能指雷暴和暴风雪。

s.en: any prediction deteriorates rapidly.
s.zh: 任何预测的准确性都会迅速下降。

s.en: Errors and uncertainties multiply, cascading upward through a chain of turbulent features,
s.zh: 误差和不确定性会成倍增加，通过一连串湍流特征向上扩散，

s.en: from dust devils and squalls up to continent-size eddies that only satellites can see.
s.zh: 从尘旋和小型风暴，到只有卫星才能观测到的、覆盖整个大陆范围的巨大涡旋……

s.en: The modern weather models work with a grid of points of the order of sixty miles apart,
s.zh: 现代天气模型使用的是间距约60英里的网格点，

s.en: and even so, some starting data has to be guessed,
s.zh: 即便如此，一些初始数据仍需推测，

s.en: since ground stations and satellites cannot see everywhere.
s.zh: 因为地面站和卫星无法覆盖所有区域。

s.en: But suppose the earth could be covered with sensors spaced one foot apart,
s.zh: 但是，假设地球表面能够被安装上间距为 1 英尺（约 30 厘米）的传感器，

s.en: rising at one-foot intervals all the way to the top of the atmosphere.
s.zh: 并以1英尺的间隔一直延伸到大气层顶部。

s.en: Suppose every sensor gives perfectly accurate readings of temperature,
s.zh: 假设每个传感器都能提供完全准确的温度、

s.en: pressure, humidity, and any other quantity a meteorologist would want.
s.zh: 压力、湿度，以及气象学家可能需要的任何其他气象参数。

s.en: Precisely at noon an infinitely powerful computer takes all the data and calculates what will happen at each point
s.zh: 正午时分，一台性能无限的计算机采集所有数据，计算各点在
12点01分、12点02分、12点03分等时刻将发生什么。

s.en: The computer will still be unable to predict whether Princeton, New Jersey, will have sun or rain on a day one month away.
s.zh: 计算机仍无法预测一个月后新泽西州普林斯顿是晴天还是雨天。

s.en: At noon the spaces between the sensors will hide fluctuations that the computer will not know about,
s.zh: 正午时分，传感器之间的空隙会隐藏计算机不知道的波动，

s.en: tiny deviations from the average.
s.zh: 这些是相对于平均值的微小偏差。

s.en: By 12.01, those fluctuations will already have created small errors one foot away.
s.zh: 到12点01分，这些波动已经会在1英尺外造成小误差。

s.en: Soon the errors will have multiplied to the ten-foot scale, and so on up to the size of the globe.
s.zh: 很快误差会扩大到10英尺范围，并以此类推，直到覆盖全球。

q: Why do small errors make it impossible to predict the weather system with a high degree of accuracy?
为什么微小的误差会导致无法高精度地预测天气系统呢？

s.en: Two factors weigh heavily against the effectiveness of scientific research in industry.
s.zh: 有两个因素严重阻碍了工业领域科学研究的有效性：

s.en: One is the general atmosphere of secrecy in which it is carried out,
s.zh: 一是进行研究的整体保密氛围；

s.en: the other the lack of freedom of the individual research worker.
s.zh: 另一方面，还存在着个体研究人员缺乏自由的问题。

s.en: In so far as any inquiry is a secret one,
s.zh: 只要任何调查都是保密的（即不对外公开的），

s.en: it naturally limits all those engaged in carrying it out from effective contact with their fellow scientists either in other countries or in universities,
s.zh: 这自然会限制所有参与研究的人员与国外或大学的同行科学家进行有效接触，

s.en: or even, often enough, in other departments of the same firm.
s.zh: 甚至常常连同一公司的其他部门也是如此。

s.en: The degree of secrecy naturally varies considerably.
s.zh: 保密的程度自然会有很大的差异。

s.en: Some of the bigger firms are engaged in researches which are of such general and fundamental nature
s.zh: 一些大公司从事的研究具有普遍性和基础性，

s.en: that it is a positive advantage to them not to keep them secret.
s.zh: 对它们来说，不保密反而更有利，

s.en: Yet a great many processes depending on such research are sought for with complete secrecy until the stage at which patents can be taken out.
s.zh: 然而，许多依赖此类研究的工艺流程在可以申请专利前都完全保密，

s.en: Even more processes are never patented at all but kept as secret processes.
s.zh: 甚至更多的工艺流程根本不申请专利，而是作为秘密工艺保存。

s.en: This applies particularly to chemical industries,
s.zh: 这尤其适用于化学工业领域。

s.en: where chance discoveries play a much larger part than they do in physical and mechanical industries.
s.zh: 在化学工业中，偶然发现的作用比在物理和机械工业中大得多。

s.en: Sometimes the secrecy goes to such an extent that the whole nature of the research cannot be mentioned.
s.zh: 有时保密到了连研究的性质都不能提及的程度。

s.en: Many firms, for instance have great difficulty in obtaining technical or scientific books from libraries
s.zh: 例如，许多公司在从图书馆获取技术类或科学类书籍时遇到了很大的困难。

s.en: because they are unwilling to have their names entered as having taken out such and such a book,
s.zh: 因为不愿让借阅记录显示他们借了某本书，

s.en: for fear the agents of other firms should be able to trace the kind of research they are likely to be undertaking.
s.zh: 生怕其他公司的探子会由此追踪到他们可能在进行的研究。

q: Why is secrecy particularly important in the chemical industries?
为什么在化学工业中，保密性尤为重要？
q2: --J.D. BERNAL The Social Function of Science--

s.en: In the organization of industrial life the influence of the factory upon the physiological and mental state of the workers has been completely neglected.
s.zh: 在工业生活的组织结构中，工厂对工人生理和心理状态的影响完全被忽视了。

s.en: Modern industry is based on the conception of the maximum production at lowest cost,
s.zh: 现代工业建立在“以最低成本实现最大生产”的理念之上。

s.en: in order that an individual or a group of individuals may earn as much money as possible.
s.zh: 这样，个人或某个群体就能赚取尽可能多的钱。

s.en: It has expanded without any idea of the true nature of the human beings who run the machines,
s.zh: 它一直在不断扩张，却对那些操控这些机器的人的真实本质一无所知。

s.en: and without giving any consideration to the effects produced on the individuals and on their descendants by the artificial mode of existence imposed by the factory.
s.zh: 而且，完全没有考虑到工厂所强加的这种人工生活方式对个人及其后代所产生的影响。

s.en: The great cities have been built with no regard for us.
s.zh: 这些伟大的城市是在完全无视我们的存在的情况下建造的。

s.en: The shape and dimensions of the skyscrapers depend entirely on the necessity of obtaining the maximum income per square foot of ground,
s.zh: 摩天大楼的形状和尺寸完全取决于实现“每平方英尺土地带来最高收入”这一目标的需要。

s.en: and of offering to the tenants offices and apartments that please them.
s.zh: 并且为租户提供他们满意的办公室和公寓。

s.en: This caused the construction of gigantic buildings where too large masses of human beings are crowded together.
s.zh: 这导致了巨型建筑物的出现，这些建筑物里挤满了大量的人口。

s.en: Civilized men like such a way of living.
s.zh: 文明人喜欢这样的生活方式。

s.en: While they enjoy the comfort and banal luxury of their dwelling, they do not realize that they are deprived of the necessities of life.
s.zh: 虽然他们享受着住所带来的舒适与平庸的奢华，却没有意识到自己被剥夺了生活必需品。

s.en: The modern city consists of monstrous edifices and of dark, narrow streets full of petrol fumes and toxic gases,
s.zh: 现代城市由巨大的建筑物以及狭窄、昏暗的街道组成；这些街道里弥漫着汽油烟雾和有毒气体。

s.en: torn by the noise of the taxicabs, lorries and buses, and thronged ceaselessly by great crowds.
s.zh: 出租车、卡车和公交车的噪音撕裂着这里的宁静，人群川流不息，络绎不绝。

s.en: Obviously, it has not been planned for the good of its inhabitants.
s.zh: 显然，这一切的规划并非是为了居民们的利益着想。

q: What is the author's main argument about the modern city?
作者关于现代城市的主要观点是什么？

s.en: In the early days of the settlement of Australia, enterprising settlers unwisely introduced the European rabbit.
s.zh: 在澳大利亚殖民初期，一些富有进取心的移民不慎将欧洲野兔引入了该地区。

s.en: This rabbit had no natural enemies in the Antipodes, so that it multiplied with that promiscuous abandon characteristic of rabbits.
s.zh: 这种兔子在澳大利亚没有天敌，因此它们以兔子特有的毫无节制的繁殖力大量滋生。

s.en: It overran a whole continent.
s.zh: 它席卷了整个大陆。

s.en: It caused devastation by burrowing and by devouring the herbage which might have maintained millions of sheep and cattle.
s.zh: 这种生物通过挖掘洞穴以及啃食本可以养活数百万只羊和牛的牧草，造成了严重的破坏。

s.en: Scientists discovered that this particular variety of rabbit (and apparently no other animal) was susceptible to a fatal virus disease, myxomatosis.
s.zh: 科学家发现，这种特定的兔子品种（显然其他动物都没有这种特性）容易感染一种致命的病毒性疾病——黏液瘤病。

s.en: By infecting animals and letting them loose in the burrows, local epidemics of this disease could be created.
s.zh: 通过感染动物并将其放回洞穴，就可以在当地制造这种疾病的流行。

s.en: Later it was found that there was a type of mosquito which acted as the carrier of this disease and passed it on to the rabbits.
s.zh: 后来发现，有一种蚊子是这种疾病的传播媒介，它们将这些病毒传染给了兔子。

s.en: So while the rest of the world was trying to get rid of mosquitoes, Australia was encouraging this one.
s.zh: 当世界上其他国家都在努力消灭蚊子时，澳大利亚却在鼓励这种蚊子繁殖。

s.en: It effectively spread the disease all over the continent and drastically reduced the rabbit population.
s.zh: 它有效地将这种疾病传播到整个大陆，并使兔子数量急剧减少。

s.en: It later became apparent that rabbits were developing a degree of resistance to this disease,
s.zh: 后来发现，兔子对这种疾病逐渐产生了抵抗力。

s.en: so that the rabbit population was unlikely to be completely exterminated.
s.zh: 这样一来，兔子种群就不太可能被彻底消灭了。

s.en: There were hopes, however, that the problem of the rabbit would become manageable.
s.zh: 然而，人们仍抱有希望，认为这个问题最终是可以得到控制的。

s.en: Ironically, Europe, which had bequeathed the rabbit as a pest to Australia, acquired this man-made disease as a pestilence.
s.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，欧洲将兔子这种害兽引入澳大利亚，结果自己却因此染上了这种由人类活动引发的疾病，并将其视为一种瘟疫。

s.en: A French physician decided to get rid of the wild rabbits on his own estate and introduced myxomatosis.
s.zh: 一位法国医生决定清除自己庄园里的野兔，于是引入了黏液瘤病。

s.en: It did not, however, remain within the confines of this estate.
s.zh: 然而，它并没有停留在这片地产的范围内。

s.en: It spread through France, where wild rabbits are not generally regarded as a pest but as a sport and a useful food supply,
s.zh: 它蔓延到法国，在那里野兔通常不被视为害兽，而是作为一种狩猎对象和有用的食物来源。

s.en: and it spread to Britain where wild rabbits are regarded as a pest but where domesticated rabbits,
s.zh: 它又传播到英国，在那里野兔被视为害兽，而家兔

s.en: equally susceptible to the disease, are the basis of a profitable fur industry.
s.zh: 这些动物同样容易感染这种疾病，但它们却是利润丰厚的毛皮产业的基础。

s.en: The question became one of whether Man could control the disease he had invented.
s.zh: 问题变成了：人类是否能够控制自己所发明的这种疾病。

q: What factor helped to spread the disease of myxomatosis?
是什么因素导致了黏液瘤病的传播？
q2: --瑞奇·卡尔德 科学有道理--

s.en: There has long been a superstition among mariners that porpoises will save drowning men by pushing them to the surface,
s.zh: 长期以来，水手们一直有一种迷信：海豚会通过将溺水者推向水面来拯救他们。

s.en: or protect them from sharks by surrounding them in defensive formation.
s.zh: 或者通过形成防御阵型来保护他们免受鲨鱼的攻击。

s.en: Marine Studio biologists have pointed out that, however intelligent they may be,
s.zh: 海洋工作室的生物学家指出，无论它们多么聪明，

s.en: it is probably a mistake to credit dolphins with any motive of life-saving.
s.zh: 将海豚的行为归因于“拯救生命”的动机，很可能是一种错误的看法。

s.en: On the occasions when they have pushed to shore an unconscious human being they have much more likely done it out of curiosity or for sport,
s.zh: 在它们将失去意识的人推向岸边的那些情况下，它们这么做很可能是出于好奇心或为了玩耍，

s.en: as in riding the bow waves of a ship.
s.zh: 就像它们喜欢乘着船头浪一样。

s.en: In 1928 some porpoises were photographed working like beavers to push ashore a waterlogged mattress.
s.zh: 1928年，有人拍到了一些海豚正在像海狸一样辛勤地工作，将一个被水浸透的床垫推上岸。

s.en: If, as has been reported, they have protected humans from sharks,
s.zh: 如果真如报道所说，它们确实保护过人类免受鲨鱼攻击，

s.en: it may have been because curiosity attracted them and because the scent of a possible meal attracted the sharks.
s.zh: 可能是因为好奇心吸引了海豚，而食物的气味吸引了鲨鱼。

s.en: Porpoises and sharks are natural enemies.
s.zh: 海豚和鲨鱼是天生的敌人。

s.en: It is possible that upon such an occasion a battle ensued, with the sharks being driven away or killed.
s.zh: 在这种情况下，很可能会发生一场战斗：鲨鱼们要么被驱赶走，要么被杀死。

s.en: Whether it be bird, fish or beast, the porpoise is intrigued with anything that is alive.
s.zh: 无论是鸟、鱼还是兽，鼠海豚对所有活物都着迷。

s.en: They are constantly after the turtles, who peacefully submit to all sorts of indignities.
s.zh: 它们总是追逐海龟，而海龟则温顺地忍受着各种戏弄。

s.en: One young calf especially enjoyed raising a turtle to the surface with his snout,
s.zh: 有一只小海豚特别喜欢用鼻子把海龟顶到水面，

s.en: and then shoving him across the tank like an aquaplane.
s.zh: 然后像推动水上滑板一样把他推过那个水箱。

s.en: Almost any day a young porpoise may be seen trying to turn a 300-pound sea turtle over by sticking his snout under the edge of his shell and pushing up for dear life.
s.zh: 几乎每天都能看到小海豚试图把一只300磅重的海龟翻个底朝天：它们把鼻子伸到海龟壳边缘，拼尽全力往上顶。

s.en: This is not easy, and may require two porpoises working together.
s.zh: 这并不容易，可能需要两只海豚共同协作才能完成。

s.en: In another game, as the turtle swims across the oceanarium, the first porpoise swoops down from above and butts his shell with his belly.
s.zh: 在另一个游戏中，当海龟游过海洋馆时，第一只海豚从上方俯冲下来，用腹部撞击龟壳。

s.en: This knocks the turtle down several feet.
s.zh: 这一撞把海龟撞下去好几英尺。

s.en: He no sooner recovers his equilibrium than the next porpoise comes along and hits him another crack.
s.zh: 它刚恢复平衡，下一只海豚就过来又撞了一下。

s.en: Eventually the turtle has been butted all the way down to the floor of the tank.
s.zh: 最后海龟被一路撞到了水族箱底部。

s.en: He is now satisfied merely to try to stand up, but as soon as he does so a porpoise knocks him flat.
s.zh: 这时海龟只求能站起来，可刚一站起来，海豚就又把它撞翻了。

s.en: The turtle at last gives up by pulling his feet under his shell and the game is over.
s.zh: 海龟最终放弃，把脚缩进壳里，游戏就此结束。

q: What would you say is the main characteristic of porpoises?
你认为海豚的主要特征是什么？
q2: --RALPH NADING HILL Window in the Sea--

s.en: It is fairly clear that the sleeping period must have some function, and because there is so much of it the function would seem to be important.
s.zh: 很明显，睡眠一定具有某种功能，而且由于这种状态持续的时间很长，因此这种功能必定非常重要。

s.en: Speculations about its nature have been going on for literally thousands of years,
s.zh: 关于睡眠本质的猜测已经持续了数千年之久。

s.en: and one odd finding that makes the problem puzzling is that it looks very much as if sleeping is not simply a matter of giving the body a rest.
s.zh: 一个令人困惑的现象是：睡眠似乎并不仅仅是让身体休息的过程。

s.en: 'Rest', in terms of muscle relaxation and so on, can be achieved by a brief period lying, or even sitting down.
s.zh: 从肌肉放松的角度来看，即使只是短暂地躺下或坐着，也能达到休息的效果。

s.en: The body's tissues are self-repairing and self-restoring to a degree, and function best when more or less continuously active.
s.zh: 人体组织本身具备自我修复和恢复的功能，而且在保持一定程度的活动状态下，其功能才能达到最佳状态。

s.en: In fact a basic amount of movement occurs during sleep which is specifically concerned with preventing muscle inactivity.
s.zh: 事实上，睡眠期间确实会发生一些活动，这些活动专门用于防止肌肉长时间处于静止状态。

s.en: If it is not a question of resting the body, then perhaps it is the brain that needs resting?
s.zh: 如果睡眠的目的不是为了让身体休息，那么或许大脑才是需要休息的对象？

s.en: This might be a plausible hypothesis were it not for two factors.
s.zh: 如果不是有两个因素的话，这或许是一个合理的假设。

s.en: First the electroencephalograph (which is simply a device for recording the electrical activity of the brain by attaching electrodes to the scalp)
s.zh: 首先，脑电图仪（这是一种通过将电极贴在头皮上来记录大脑电活动的简单装置）

s.en: shows that while there is a change in the pattern of activity during sleep,
s.zh: 显示，虽然睡眠期间的活动模式会发生变化，

s.en: there is no evidence that the total amount of activity is any less.
s.zh: 没有证据表明总体活动量有任何减少。

s.en: The second factor is more interesting and more fundamental.
s.zh: 第二个因素更加有趣，也更为根本。

s.en: Some years ago an American psychiatrist named William Dement published experiments dealing with the recording of eye-movements during sleep.
s.zh: 几年前，一位名叫威廉·德门特（William Dement）的美国精神病学家发表了一项研究，该研究记录了人们在睡眠期间的眼球运动情况。

s.en: He showed that the average individual's sleep cycle is punctuated with peculiar bursts of eye-movements, some drifting and slow, others jerky and rapid.
s.zh: 他发现，普通人的睡眠周期中会伴随着一些特殊的眼球运动现象：有些眼球运动较为缓慢、平稳，而另一些则突然、快速地发生。

s.en: People woken during these periods of eye-movements generally reported that they had been dreaming.
s.zh: 在眼球运动期间被唤醒的人通常报告说他们正在做梦。

s.en: When woken at other times they reported no dreams.
s.zh: 在其他时间被唤醒时，他们表示自己没有做任何梦。

s.en: If one group of people were disturbed from their eye-movement sleep for several nights on end,
s.zh: 如果有一组人的眼球运动睡眠（REM sleep）连续几个晚上都被中断，

s.en: and another group were disturbed for an equal period of time but when they were not exhibiting eye-movements,
s.zh: 另一组人在同样长的时间内受到干扰，但干扰时他们并没有表现出眼球运动，

s.en: the first group began to show some personality disorders while the others seemed more or less unaffected.
s.zh: 第一组开始出现一些人格障碍的症状，而其他组则几乎没有受到影响。

s.en: The implications of all this were that it was not the disturbance of sleep that mattered, but the disturbance of dreaming.
s.zh: 所有这些现象表明，重要的不是睡眠受到干扰，而是做梦受到干扰。

q: What is going on when a person experiences rapid eye-movements during sleep?
当人在睡眠中经历快速眼动（REM）时，究竟发生了什么？
q2: --CHRISTOPHER EVANS The stuff of dreams from The Listener--
--克里斯托弗·埃文斯《倾听者》中的梦境--

s.en: How it came about that snakes manufactured poison is a mystery.
s.zh: 蛇是如何制造出毒液的，这至今是个谜。

s.en: Over the periods their saliva, a mild, digestive juice like our own, was converted into a poison that defies analysis even today.
s.zh: 经过漫长的岁月，它们的唾液——一种像我们一样的温和消化液——变成了毒液，这种毒液甚至今天都难以分析。

s.en: It was not forced upon them by the survival competition;
s.zh: 这种毒液的产生并非出于生存竞争的必然；

s.en: they could have caught and lived on prey without using poison, just as the thousands of non-poisonous snakes still do.
s.zh: 它们本可以不使用毒液就捕获猎物并赖以为生，就像现在成千上万的无毒蛇那样。

s.en: Poison to a snake is merely a luxury;
s.zh: 对蛇来说，毒液其实是一种“奢侈品”；

s.en: it enables it to get its food with very little effort, no more effort than one bite.
s.zh: 它让蛇能够毫不费力地捕获猎物，只需轻轻一咬即可。

s.en: And why only snakes?
s.zh: 那么，为什么只有蛇会拥有毒液呢？

s.en: Cats, for instance, would be greatly helped;
s.zh: 以猫为例，毒液对它们来说同样大有帮助：

s.en: no running fights with large, fierce rats or tussles with grown rabbits--just a bite and no more effort needed.
s.zh: 不用与又大又凶的老鼠追逐打斗，也不用和成年兔子扭打——只需咬一口，再不用费力。

s.en: In fact, it would be an assistance to all carnivores though it would be a two-edged weapon when they fought each other.
s.zh: 事实上，这对所有食肉动物来说都是一种帮助；不过当它们互相争斗时，这也会成为一把“双刃剑”（即既有利也有弊）。

s.en: But, of the vertebrates unpredictable Nature selected only snakes (and one lizard).
s.zh: 但是，在脊椎动物中，难以捉摸的大自然只选择了蛇（和一种蜥蜴）。

s.en: One wonders also why Nature, with some snakes concocted poison of such extreme potency.
s.zh: 人们也奇怪，为什么大自然在某些蛇身上调制出如此猛烈的毒药。

s.en: In the conversion of saliva into poison, one might suppose that a fixed process took place. It did not;
s.zh: 在唾液变成毒液的过程中，人们可能会认为有一个固定的过程发生。但事实并非如此；

s.en: some snakes manufactured a poison different in every respect from that of others,
s.zh: 有些蛇产生的毒液在各个方面都与其他蛇产生的毒液不同。

s.en: as different as arsenic is from strychnine, and having different effects.
s.zh: 就像砒霜和马钱子碱不同那样，并且效果也不同。

s.en: One poison acts on the nerves, the other on the blood.
s.zh: 一种毒物作用于神经系统，另一种则作用于血液。

s.en: The makers of the nerve poison include the mambas and the cobras and their venom is called neurotoxic.
s.zh: 制造这种神经毒素的动物包括曼巴蛇和眼镜蛇，它们的毒液被称为神经毒素（neurotoxic venom）。

s.en: Vipers (adders) and rattlesnakes manufacture the blood poison, which is known as haemolytic.
s.zh: 蝰蛇和响尾蛇会分泌一种血液毒素，这种毒素被称为“溶血毒素”（haemolytic toxin）。

s.en: Both poisons are unpleasant, but by far the more unpleasant is the blood poison.
s.zh: 两种毒液都令人不快，但远比神经毒液更令人不快的是血液毒液。

s.en: It is said that the nerve poison is the more primitive of the two, that the blood poison is, so to speak, a newer product from an improved formula.
s.zh: 据说，神经毒液是两者中较原始的一种，而血液毒液，可以这么说，是改良配方后的新产品。

s.en: Be that as it may, the nerve poison does its business with man far more quickly than the blood poison.
s.zh: 尽管如此，这种神经毒素对人体的影响速度要比血液毒素快得多。

s.en: This, however, means nothing.
s.zh: 然而，这毫无意义。

s.en: Snakes did not acquire their poison for use against man but for use against prey such as rats and mice,
s.zh: 蛇之所以拥有毒液，并不是为了用来对付人类，而是为了捕杀老鼠等猎物。

s.en: and the effects on these of viperine poison is almost immediate.
s.zh: 而蝰蛇毒液对这些动物的效果几乎是立竿见影的。

q: What are the two different ways in which snake poison acts?
蛇毒的作用方式主要有哪两种？

lessons.t: William S. Hart and the early 'Western' film
lessons.tz: 威廉.S. 哈特和早期"西部"影片

s.en: William S. Hart was, perhaps, the greatest of all Western stars,
s.zh: 威廉·S.哈特或许是所有西部片明星中最伟大的一位。

s.en: for unlike Gary Cooper and John Wayne he appeared in nothing but Westerns.
s.zh: 与加里·库珀（Gary Cooper）和约翰·韦恩（John Wayne）不同，他只出演过西部片（Westerns）。

s.en: From 1914 to 1924 he was supreme and unchallenged.
s.zh: 从 1914 年到 1924 年，他一直是无可争议的领袖，无人能够与他竞争。

s.en: It was Hart who created the basic formula of the Western film,
s.zh: 正是哈特创造了西部片的基本模式。

s.en: and devised the protagonist he played in every film he made,
s.zh: 并为他出演的每部电影都设计了主角形象，

s.en: the good-bad man, the accidental, noble outlaw,
s.zh: 即亦正亦邪的人，意外成为亡命之徒却品格高尚的人，

s.en: or the honest, but framed cowboy, or the sheriff made suspect by vicious gossip;
s.zh: 或者是那个诚实却被诬陷的牛仔，又或者是那个因恶毒的谣言而受到怀疑的警长……

s.en: in short, the individual in conflict with himself and his frontier environment.
s.zh: 简而言之，这是一个与自己及边疆环境冲突的人。

s.en: Unlike most of his contemporaries in Hollywood,
s.zh: 与好莱坞的大多数同时代人不同，

s.en: Hart actually knew something of the old West.
s.zh: 哈特其实对美国西部历史有所了解。

s.en: He had lived in it as a child when it was already disappearing,
s.zh: 他小时候就生活在那里，那时西部文明已逐渐消逝；

s.en: and his hero was firmly rooted in his memories and experiences,
s.zh: 他的英雄形象深深植根于他的记忆与经历之中，

s.en: and in both the history and the mythology of the vanished frontier,
s.zh: 以及那片消失的边疆的历史与传说之中。

s.en: And although no period or place in American history has been more absurdly romanticized,
s.zh: 尽管美国历史上没有哪个时期或地点被如此荒谬地浪漫化了，

s.en: myth and reality did join hands in at least one arena,
s.zh: 但在至少一点上，神话与现实确实交汇在了一起——

s.en: the conflict between the individual and encroaching civilization.
s.zh: 那就是个人与不断扩张的文明之间的冲突。

s.en: Men accustomed to struggling for survival against the elements and Indians
s.zh: 那些习惯了与自然环境及印第安人抗争以求生存的人们，

s.en: were bewildered by politicians, bankers and businessmen,
s.zh: 却被政客、银行家和商人搞得无所适从；

s.en: and unhorsed by fences, laws and alien taboos.
s.zh: 被围栏、法律和陌生的禁忌拉下马。

s.en: Hart's good-bad man was always an outsider, always one of the disinherited,
s.zh: 哈特笔下的亦正亦邪者永远是局外人，永远是被剥夺继承权的人，

s.en: and if he found it necessary to shoot a sheriff or rob a bank along the way,
s.zh: 如果他觉得有必要开枪打死警长或抢劫银行，他也会这么做。

s.en: his early audiences found it easy to understand and forgive,
s.zh: 他的早期观众很容易理解并原谅他。

s.en: especially when it was Hart who, in the end, overcame the attacking Indians.
s.zh: 尤其是当最终由哈特击败了来犯的印第安人时。

s.en: Audiences in the second decade of the twentieth century
s.zh: 二十世纪第二个十年的观众群体

s.en: found it pleasant to escape to a time when life, though hard, was relatively simple.
s.zh: 觉得逃回到那个虽然艰苦但相对简单的时代是件愉快的事。

s.en: We still do; living in a world in which undeclared aggression, war, hypocrisy,
s.zh: 我们至今仍然如此；生活在一个充满不宣而战的侵略、战争、虚伪、

s.en: chicanery, anarchy and impending immolation are part of our daily lives,
s.zh: 欺诈、混乱以及即将到来的毁灭，都是我们日常生活的一部分。

s.en: we all want a code to live by.
s.zh: 我们都希望有一套可以遵循的准则或规则来指导我们的行为。

威廉·哈特的童年经历是如何为他日后在西部电影中扮演演员角色奠定基础的？

s.en: Why does the idea of progress loom so large in the modern world?
s.zh: 为什么“进步”的概念在现代社会中显得如此重要（或者说，为什么人们对“进步”的追求如此强烈）？

s.en: Surely because progress of a particular kind is actually taking place around us
s.zh: 肯定是因为某种形式的进步正在我们周围实实在在地发生着。

s.en: and is becoming more and more manifest.
s.zh: 而且这种现象正变得越来越明显（或：这种现象正逐渐变得清晰可见）。

s.en: Although mankind has undergone no general improvement in intelligence or morality,
s.zh: 尽管人类的智力或道德水平并没有普遍性的提升，

s.en: it has made extraordinary progress in the accumulation of knowledge.
s.zh: 在知识的积累方面，它取得了非凡的进展。

s.en: Knowledge began to increase as soon as the thoughts of one individual
s.zh: 一旦某个人的思想能够通过语言传达给另一个人，知识就开始增加了。

s.en: could be communicated to another by means of speech.
s.zh: 随着文字的发明，人类社会取得了巨大的进步。

s.en: With the invention of writing, a great advance was made,
s.zh: 这样一来，知识不仅可以被传播，还可以被储存起来。

s.en: for knowledge could then be not only communicated but also stored.
s.zh: 图书馆使教育成为可能，而教育又反过来促进了图书馆的发展（即促进了图书馆资源的丰富与建设）。

s.en: Libraries made education possible, and education in its turn added to libraries:
s.zh: 知识的增长遵循了一种类似于“复利”的规律。

s.en: the growth of knowledge followed a kind of compound interest law,
s.zh: 这一情况因印刷术的发明而得到了极大的促进。

s.en: which was greatly enhanced by the invention of printing.
s.zh: 在科学出现之前，所有这些发展都相对缓慢。

s.en: All this was comparatively slow until, with the coming of science,
s.zh: 节奏突然加快了。

s.en: the tempo was suddenly raised.
s.zh: 于是，知识开始按照系统的计划被逐步积累起来。

s.en: Then knowledge began to be accumulated according to a systematic plan.
s.zh: 起初只是细小的水流，后来逐渐汇聚成了一条小溪；如今，这条小溪已经变成了湍急的急流。

s.en: The trickle became a stream: the stream has now become a torrent.
s.zh: 此外，一旦获得了新的知识，就会立即将其应用于实际中。

s.en: Moreover, as soon as new knowledge is acquired, it is now turned to practical account.
s.zh: 所谓的'现代文明'

s.en: What is called 'modern civilization'
s.zh: 这并不是人类所有天性得到平衡发展的结果。

s.en: is not the result of a balanced development of all man's nature,
s.zh: 而是积累的知识应用于实际生活的结果。

s.en: but of accumulated knowledge applied to practical life.
s.zh: 人类现在面临的问题是：

s.en: The problem now facing humanity is:
s.zh: 这些知识将会被用来做什么呢？

s.en: What is going to be done with all this knowledge?
s.zh: 正如人们经常指出的那样，知识是一把双刃剑。

s.en: As is so often pointed out, knowledge is a two-edged weapon
s.zh: 既可以用于行善，也可以用于作恶。

s.en: which can be used equally for good or evil.
s.zh: 而现在，它被不加区分地用于这两种目的。

s.en: It is now being used indifferently for both.
s.zh: 比如说，还有哪种场景能比这更加荒诞、又充满阴郁的幽默感呢？

s.en: Could any spectacle, for instance, be more grimly whimsical
s.zh: 炮手们利用科学来摧毁人体，

s.en: than that of gunners using science to shatter men's bodies
s.zh: 而近在咫尺的外科医生却用它来修复人体？

s.en: while, close at hand, surgeons use it to restore them?
s.zh: 我们必须非常严肃地问自己一个问题。

s.en: We have to ask ourselves very seriously
s.zh: 如果这种对知识的双重使用，

s.en: what will happen if this twofold use of knowledge,
s.zh: 在其力量不断增强的情况下继续下去，会发生什么？

s.en: with its ever-increasing power, continues.

q: In what two areas have people made no 'progress' at all?
在哪些领域，人们完全没有取得任何进展？

s.en: No two sorts of birds practise quite the same sort of flight;
s.zh: 没有两种鸟类的飞行方式是完全相同的。

s.en: the varieties are infinite; but two classes may be roughly seen.
s.zh: 虽然种类繁多、无穷无尽，但大致上可以分为两类。

s.en: Any ship that crosses the Pacific
s.zh: 任何横渡太平洋的船只

s.en: is accompanied for many days by the smaller albatross,
s.zh: 在许多天里，它都伴随着体型较小的信天翁。

s.en: which may keep company with the vessel for an hour
s.zh: 信天翁可能会与船只结伴一个小时，

s.en: without visible or more than occasional movement of wing.
s.zh: 翅膀没有明显的运动，或者仅有偶尔的轻微摆动。

s.en: The currents of air that the walls of the ship direct upwards,
s.zh: 那些被船体墙壁引导向上的气流……

s.en: as well as in the line of its course,
s.zh: 以及沿着船只航行的方向，

s.en: are enough to give the great bird with its immense wings
s.zh: 足以让这只拥有巨大翅膀的巨鸟

s.en: sufficient sustenance and progress.
s.zh: 获得足够的动力和前进的力量。

s.en: The albatross is the king of the gliders,
s.zh: 信天翁是滑翔鸟类中的“王者”。

s.en: the class of fliers which harness the air to their purpose,
s.zh: 这类飞鸟能驾驭空气来实现飞行目的，

s.en: but must yield to its opposition.
s.zh: 但也不得不屈服于逆风的阻力。

s.en: In the contrary school, the duck is supreme.
s.zh: 而在另一类飞行方式中，鸭子是佼佼者。

s.en: It comes nearer to the engines with which man has 'conquered' the air, as he boasts.
s.zh: 它更接近那些人类用来“征服”天空的飞行器——正如人类所自豪地宣称的那样。

s.en: Ducks, and like them the pigeons, are endowed with steel-like muscles,
s.zh: 鸭子，和鸽子一样，拥有像钢铁一样强健的肌肉。

s.en: that are a good part of the weight of the bird,
s.zh: 这些部分占据了鸟类体重的很大比例。

s.en: and these will ply the short wings with such irresistible power
s.zh: 能以不可抗拒的力量驱动短小的翅膀，

s.en: that they can bore for long distances through an opposing gale
s.zh: 顶着逆风长距离飞行，

s.en: before exhaustion follows.
s.zh: 直到精疲力竭。

s.en: Their humbler followers, such as partridges,
s.zh: 它们那些能力稍逊的同类，比如鹧鸪，

s.en: have a like power of strong propulsion, but soon tire.
s.zh: 它们拥有强大的推进力，但很快就会疲劳。

s.en: You may pick them up in utter exhaustion,
s.zh: 如果海上的风迫使它们长途飞行，

s.en: if wind over the sea has driven them to a long journey.
s.zh: 你甚至可以在它们精疲力竭时把它们捡起来。

s.en: The swallow shares the virtues of both schools in highest measure.
s.zh: 燕子则将这两种飞行方式的优点发挥到了极致。

s.en: It tires not, nor does it boast of its power; but belongs to the air
s.zh: 它不会感到疲劳，也不会夸耀自己的力量，而是属于天空，

s.en: travelling it may be six thousand miles to and from its northern nesting home,
s.zh: 往返北方的筑巢地，行程也许长达六千英里，

s.en: feeding its flown young as it flies, and slipping through a medium
s.zh: 一边飞行一边喂养已经会飞的雏鸟，

s.en: that seems to help its passage even when the wind is adverse.
s.zh: 穿行于似乎能助其前行的空气中，即使风向不利。

s.en: Such birds do us good,
s.zh: 这样的鸟类对我们大有裨益，

s.en: though we no longer take omens from their flight on this side and that;
s.zh: 尽管我们不再从它们忽东忽西的飞行中解读预兆了；

s.en: and even the most superstitious villagers no longer take off their hats to the magpie and wish it good-morning.
s.zh: 就连最迷信的村民，也不会再向喜鹊脱帽道早安了。

q: What are the two main types of bird flight described by the author?
作者描述了哪两种主要的鸟类飞行方式？
q2: --威廉·比奇·托马斯《乡下人的信条》--

s.en: A young man sees a sunset and,
s.zh: 一个年轻人看到了日落，

s.en: unable to understand or to express the emotion that it rouses in him,
s.zh: 无法理解这种情感在他心中所引发的反应，也无法表达出自己所感受到的情绪。

s.en: concludes that it must be the gateway to a world that lies beyond.
s.zh: 得出结论：这一定是通往另一个未知世界的入口。

s.en: It is difficult for any of us in moments of intense aesthetic experience
s.zh: 在那些充满强烈审美体验的时刻，我们任何人都很难抗拒这样一种想法：

s.en: to resist the suggestion that we are catching a glimpse of a light
s.zh: 我们似乎瞥见了某种光芒，

s.en: that shines down to us from a different realm of existence, different and,
s.zh: 那种光芒是从另一个存在领域照射到我们这里的；那个领域与我们截然不同……

s.en: because the experience is intensely moving, in some way higher.
s.zh: 因为这种体验非常令人感动，从某种意义上来说，它的价值甚至更高（即这种体验带来的意义或影响更为深远）。

s.en: And, though the gleams blind and dazzle, yet do they convey a hint of beauty and serenity
s.zh: 尽管那些光芒刺眼、令人眩目，但它们依然透露出一种美丽与宁静的气息。

s.en: greater than we have known or imagined. Greater too than we can describe;
s.zh: 比我们以往所知道或想象的都要伟大；同时也超出了我们的描述能力。

s.en: for language, which was invented to convey the meanings of this world
s.zh: 因为语言是为了传达这个世界的意义而创造的，

s.en: cannot readily be fitted to the uses of another.
s.zh: 所以它很难用来表达另一个世界的意义。

s.en: That all great art has this power of suggesting a world beyond is undeniable.
s.zh: 不可否认，一切伟大的艺术都有这种暗示超越尘世的世界的力量。

s.en: In some moods, nature shares it.
s.zh: 在某些心境下，大自然也具有这种力量。

s.en: There is no sky in June so blue that it does not point forward to a bluer,
s.zh: 六月的蓝天再蓝，也会让人向往更蓝的天空；

s.en: no sunset so beautiful that it does not waken the vision of a greater beauty,
s.zh: 日落再美，也会唤起人们对更美之景的想象，

s.en: a vision which passes before it is fully glimpsed,
s.zh: 这种幻景还未被充分看清便消逝，

s.en: and in passing leaves an indefinable longing and regret.
s.zh: 只留下一种难以言喻的渴望与遗憾。

s.en: But, if this world is not merely a bad joke,
s.zh: 但是，如果这个世界不仅仅是一个糟糕的玩笑，

s.en: life a vulgar flare amid the cool radiance of the stars,
s.zh: 如果生命不是在星辰冷冽光芒中的短暂闪光，

s.en: and existence an empty laugh braying across the mysteries;
s.zh: 如果存在不是对那些神秘事物的徒劳嘲笑……

s.en: if these intimations of a something behind and beyond
s.zh: 如果这些关于世界背后、超越尘世的某种存在的暗示，

s.en: are not evil humour born of indigestion,
s.zh: 不是消化不良引起的恶劣情绪，

s.en: or whimsies sent by the devil to mock and madden us, if, in a word,
s.zh: 也不是魔鬼派来嘲笑和折磨我们的奇想——

s.en: beauty means something, yet we must not seek to interpret the meaning.
s.zh: 总之，如果美确有某种意义，我们也不应试图解释这种意义。

s.en: If we glimpse the unutterable, it is unwise to try to utter it,
s.zh: 如果我们瞥见了那不可言说之物，试图言说它是不明智的，

s.en: nor should we seek to invest with significance that which we cannot grasp.
s.zh: 我们也不应该试图赋予那些我们无法理解的事物以意义。

s.en: Beauty in terms of our human meanings is meaningless.
s.zh: 用人类的意义来衡量，美是没有意义的。

q: What do glimpses of beauty, either in nature or art, often suggest to the human mind?
无论是自然界中的美景，还是艺术作品中的美感，它们往往能给人类的心灵带来怎样的启示呢？

s.en: Many people in industry and the Services,
s.zh: 工业界和军队中许多人，

s.en: who have practical experience of noise,
s.zh: 具有接触噪音的实际经验，

s.en: regard any investigation of this question as a waste of time;
s.zh: 认为对这个问题进行任何调查都是浪费时间；

s.en: they are not prepared even to admit the possibility that noise affects people.
s.zh: 他们甚至不愿意承认“噪音会影响人们”这一可能性。

s.en: On the other hand,
s.zh: 另一方面，

s.en: those who dislike noise will sometimes use most inadequate evidence
s.zh: 那些不喜欢噪音的人，有时会使用非常不充分的证据

s.en: to support their pleas for a quieter society.
s.zh: 以支持他们关于营造一个更加宁静社会的诉求。

s.en: This is a pity, because noise abatement really is a good cause,
s.zh: 这真是太遗憾了，因为减少噪音确实是一个非常有益的事业（或：减少噪音是一件很有意义的事情）。

s.en: and it is likely to be discredited if it gets to be associated with bad science.
s.zh: 如果这种理论或方法与糟糕的科学实践（即不严谨、不科学的研究方法）联系在一起，它很可能会被人们质疑或否定（即失去可信度）。

s.en: One allegation often made is that noise produces mental illness.
s.zh: 一个常见的指控是：噪音会导致精神疾病。

s.en: A recent article in a weekly newspaper, for instance,
s.zh: 例如，最近一家周刊上发表了一篇文章……

s.en: was headed with a striking illustration of a lady in a state of considerable distress,
s.zh: 文章的标题配有一幅引人注目的插图，描绘了一位极度痛苦的女士

s.en: with the caption 'She was yet another victim, reduced to a screaming wreck'.
s.zh: 配文写道：“她只是又一个受害者，被折磨成了一个只会尖叫的废人”。

s.en: On turning eagerly to the text, one learns that the lady was a typist
s.zh: 当人们急切地阅读这段文字时，会发现那位女士原来是一名打字员。

s.en: who found the sound of office typewriters worried her more and more
s.zh: 她发现办公室打字机的声音让她越来越焦虑

s.en: until eventually she had to go into a mental hospital.
s.zh: 直到最后，她不得不被送进精神病院。

s.en: Now the snag in this sort of anecdote is of course that one cannot distinguish cause and effect.
s.zh: 当然，这类轶事的一个问题在于人们无法区分其中的因果关系（即哪些事件是原因，哪些是结果）。

s.en: Was the noise a cause of the illness,
s.zh: 这种噪音是导致疾病的原因吗？

s.en: or were the complaints about noise merely a symptom?
s.zh: 还是说，那些关于噪音的投诉只是一种症状？

s.en: Another patient might equally well complain
s.zh: 另一个病人也可能抱怨，

s.en: that her neighbours were combining to slander her and persecute her,
s.zh: 说她的邻居们联合起来诽谤她、迫害她

s.en: and yet one might be cautious about believing this statement.
s.zh: 然而，人们或许会对这一说法持谨慎态度（即不太相信它）。

s.en: What is needed in the case of noise is a study of large numbers of people living under noisy conditions,
s.zh: 在噪声环境下，我们需要对大量生活在嘈杂环境中的人进行研究。

s.en: to discover whether they are mentally ill more often than other people are.
s.zh: 为了查明他们是否比普通人更容易患上精神疾病。

s.en: Some time ago the United States Navy, for instance,
s.zh: 例如，不久前美国海军就……

s.en: examined a very large number of men working on aircraft carriers:
s.zh: 对大量在航空母舰上工作的男性进行了检查。

s.en: the study was known as Project Anehin.
s.zh: 这项研究被称为“Project Anehin”。

s.en: It can be unpleasant to live even several miles from an aerodrome;
s.zh: 即使住在离机场几英里远的地方，也可能很不愉快；

s.en: if you think what it must be like to share the deck of a ship with several squadrons of jet aircraft,
s.zh: 如果你想象一下：与几支喷气式飞机中队共享同一艘船的甲板，那会是什么样子……

s.en: you will realize that a modern navy is a good place to study noise.
s.zh: 你会发现，现代海军是一个研究噪声问题的理想场所。

s.en: But neither psychiatric interviews nor objective tests
s.zh: 但无论是精神病学访谈还是客观测试

s.en: were able to show any effects upon these American sailors.
s.zh: 都未能显示对这些美国水手有任何影响。

s.en: This result merely confirms earlier American and British studies:
s.zh: 这一结果仅仅证实了此前美国和英国的研究结果而已。

s.en: if there is any effect of noise upon mental health,
s.zh: 如果噪音对心理健康有任何影响的话……

s.en: it must be so small that present methods of psychiatric diagnosis cannot find it.
s.zh: 它一定非常微小，以至于现有的精神疾病诊断方法无法检测到它。

s.en: That does not prove that it does not exist; but it does mean
s.zh: 这并不能证明该事物根本不存在；不过这确实意味着……

s.en: that noise is less dangerous than, say being brought up in an orphanage
s.zh: 它一定比，比如说在孤儿院长大，要安全得多

s.en: --which really is a mental health hazard.
s.zh: ——那才真正是精神健康的危害。

q: What conclusion does the author draw about noise and health in this piece?
作者在这篇文章中关于“噪音与健康”得出了什么结论？

lessons.t: The past life of the earth

s.en: It is animals and plants which lived in or near water whose remains are most likely to be preserved,
s.zh: 最有可能被保存下来的，是那些生活在水中或水边的动植物的遗骸。

s.en: for one of the necessary conditions of preservation is quick burial,
s.zh: 其中一个必要的保存条件就是迅速掩埋。

s.en: and it is only in the seas and rivers, and sometimes lakes,
s.zh: 而只有在海洋、河流中，有时也在湖泊里，

s.en: where mud and silt have been continuously deposited,
s.zh: 在那些泥沙不断沉积的地方……

s.en: that bodies and the like can be rapidly covered over and preserved.
s.zh: 尸体等物才能被迅速覆盖并保存下来。

s.en: But even in the most favourable circumstances
s.zh: 但即使在最有利的情况下

s.en: only a small fraction of the creatures that die are preserved in this way
s.zh: 只有极少数死亡的生物能够以这种方式被保存下来。

s.en: before decay sets in or, even more likely, before scavengers eat them.
s.zh: 在腐烂开始之前，或者更可能的是，在食腐动物吃掉它们之前。

s.en: After all, all living creatures live by feeding on something else,
s.zh: 毕竟，所有生物都是通过摄取其他物质来维持生存的。

s.en: whether it be plant or animal, dead or alive,
s.zh: 无论是植物还是动物，无论是死的还是活的……

s.en: and it is only by chance that such a fate is avoided.
s.zh: 只有碰巧才能避免这样的命运。

s.en: The remains of plants and animals that lived on land are much more rarely preserved,
s.zh: 生活在陆地上的植物和动物的遗骸被保存下来的情况要少得多。

s.en: for there is seldom anything to cover them over.
s.zh: 因为很少有东西能将它们覆盖起来。

s.en: When you think of the innumerable birds that one sees flying about,
s.zh: 当你想到那些在空中飞舞的无数鸟类时……

s.en: not to mention the equally numerous small animals like field mice and voles which you do not see,
s.zh: 更不用说那些同样数量众多但你看不到的小动物，比如田鼠等小型啮齿动物。

s.en: it is very rarely that one comes across a dead body, except, of course, on the roads.
s.zh: 人们很少能碰到动物的尸体，当然，路上除外。

s.en: They decompose and are quickly destroyed by the weather or eaten by some other creature.
s.zh: 它们会腐烂，很快被风化或被其他动物吃掉。

s.en: It is almost always due to some very special circumstances that traces of land animals survive,
s.zh: 几乎总是由于一些非常特殊的情况，陆地动物的痕迹才能得以保存下来。

s.en: as by falling into inaccessible caves, or into an ice crevasse,
s.zh: 比如掉进无法进入的洞穴里，或者掉进冰裂隙里。

s.en: like the Siberian mammoths,
s.zh: 就像西伯利亚猛犸象一样……

s.en: when the whole animal is sometimes preserved, as in a refrigerator.
s.zh: 有时整个动物会像在冰箱里一样被保存下来。

s.en: This is what happened to the famous Beresovka mammoth which was found preserved and in good condition.
s.zh: 这就是著名的贝列索夫卡猛犸象的遭遇：它被发现时保存完好，状态极佳。

s.en: In his mouth were the remains of fir trees--the last meal that he had before he fell into the crevasse and broke his back.
s.zh: 它嘴里还残留着冷杉树枝——那是它掉进冰缝摔断背前的最后一餐。

s.en: The mammoth has now been restored in the Palaeontological Museum in St. Petersburg.
s.zh: 这头猛犸象现已被修复并陈列在圣彼得堡的古生物博物馆中。

s.en: Other animals were trapped in tar pits, like the elephants, sabre-toothed cats,
s.zh: 还有些动物陷进了沥青坑，比如大象、剑齿虎

s.en: and numerous other creatures that are found at Rancho la Brea, which is now just a suburb of Los Angeles.
s.zh: 以及在兰乔拉布雷亚发现的众多其他生物，那里如今只是洛杉矶的一个郊区。

s.en: Apparently what happened was that water collected on these tar pits
s.zh: 显然，发生的情况是水在这些沥青坑中积聚了。

s.en: and the bigger animals like the elephants ventured out on to the apparently firm surface to drink,
s.zh: 那些体型较大的动物，比如大象，便冒险走到了那片看起来非常坚固的地面上去喝水。

s.en: and were promptly bogged in the tar.
s.zh: 结果立刻陷进了沥青里。

s.en: And then, when they were dead, the carnivores,
s.zh: 然后，当它们死去之后，那些肉食动物……

s.en: like the sabretoothed cats and the giant wolves,
s.zh: 就像剑齿虎和巨型狼一样……

s.en: came out to feed and suffered exactly the same fate.
s.zh: 它们出来觅食，结果遭遇了完全相同的命运。

s.en: There are also endless numbers of birds in the tar as well.
s.zh: 沥青里还有数不清的鸟类的遗骸。

q: What is the main condition for the preservation of the remains of any living creature?
保存任何生物遗骸的主要条件是什么？

s.en: What happened to the 'Vasa' almost immediately after she was launched?
s.zh: “瓦萨号”在下水后几乎立刻就发生了什么？

s.en: From the seventeenth-century empire of Sweden,
s.zh: 从十七世纪的瑞典帝国，

s.en: the story of a galleon that sank at the start of her maiden voyage in 1628 must be one of the strangest tales of the sea.
s.zh: 这艘加莱昂帆船的故事堪称海洋史上最离奇的传说之一：它在1628年首次航行时便沉没了。

s.en: For nearly three and a half centuries she lay at the bottom of Stockholm harbour until her discovery in 1956.
s.zh: 在将近三个半世纪的时间里，这艘船一直沉躺在斯德哥尔摩港的底部，直到1956年才被人发现。

s.en: This was the Vasa, royal flagship of the great imperial fleet.
s.zh: 这艘船是“瓦萨号”（Vasa），属于那个伟大帝国舰队的皇家旗舰。

s.en: King Gustavus Adolphus 'The Northern Hurricane',
s.zh: 古斯塔夫·阿道夫国王，被称为“北方飓风”……

s.en: then at the height of his military success in the Thirty Years' War,
s.zh: 就在他在“三十年战争”中取得军事胜利的巅峰时期，

s.en: had dictated her measurements and armament.
s.zh: 亲自规定了她的尺寸和武器装备。

s.en: Triple gun-decks mounted sixty-four bronze cannon.
s.zh: 三层甲板上共安装了六十四门青铜大炮。

s.en: She was intended to play a leading role in the growing might of Sweden.
s.zh: 她本应在瑞典日益增长的国力中扮演重要角色。

s.en: As she was prepared for her maiden voyage on August 10, 1628, Stockholm was in a ferment.
s.zh: 1628年8月10日，当这艘船准备首航时，斯德哥尔摩一片沸腾。

s.en: From the Skeppsbron and surrounding islands
s.zh: 从斯凯普斯布隆（Skeppsbron）和周围的岛屿上，

s.en: the people watched this thing of beauty begin to spread her sails and catch the wind.
s.zh: 人们看着这艘美丽的船开始扬起帆，迎风启航。

s.en: They had laboured for three years to produce this floating work of art;
s.zh: 他们花了三年时间才完成这件浮动的艺术品。

s.en: she was more richly carved and ornamented than any previous ship.
s.zh: 它的雕刻和装饰比以往任何一艘船都要精美、复杂得多。

s.en: The high stern castle was a riot of carved gods, demons, knights, kings, warriors,
s.zh: 高耸的船尾城堡上雕刻着神祇、恶魔、骑士、国王、武士，

s.en: mermaids, cherubs; and zoomorphic animal shapes ablaze with red and gold and blue,
s.zh: 美人鱼、小天使，以及那些被红色、金色和蓝色装饰得绚丽多彩的动物形状……

s.en: symbols of courage, power, and cruelty,
s.zh: 象征着勇气、力量与残酷的符号……

s.en: were portrayed to stir the imaginations of the superstitious sailors of the day.
s.zh: 这些雕刻旨在激发当时迷信水手的想象力。

s.en: Then the cannons of the anchored warships thundered a salute to which the Vasa fired in reply.
s.zh: 随后，停泊在港口的战舰们鸣响了礼炮，以示敬意；作为回应，瓦萨号（Vasa）也开炮回敬了。

s.en: As she emerged from her drifting cloud of gun smoke with the water churned to foam beneath her bow,
s.zh: 当她从那弥漫着枪炮烟雾的云层中走出来时，船头下方的水面已经泛起了层层泡沫……

s.en: her flags flying, pennants waving, sails filling in the breeze,
s.zh: 她的旗帜高高飘扬，小旗子随风摆动，船帆在微风中轻轻鼓动……

s.en: and the red and gold of her superstructure ablaze with colour,
s.zh: 上层建筑的红色和金色熠熠生辉，

s.en: she presented a more majestic spectacle than Stockholmers had ever seen before.
s.zh: 她呈现出斯德哥尔摩市民从未见过的壮丽景象。

s.en: All gun-ports were open and the muzzles peeped wickedly from them.
s.zh: 所有炮窗都敞开着，炮口从中邪恶地探出。

s.en: As the wind freshened there came a sudden squall and the ship made a strange movement, listing to port.
s.zh: 随着风势的增强，突然刮起了一阵狂风，船只也出现了异常的摇晃——它向左舷倾斜了过去。

s.en: The Ordnance officer ordered all the port cannon to be heaved to starboard
s.zh: 军械官命令将所有左舷炮移到右舷

s.en: to counteract the list but the steepening angle of the decks increased.
s.zh: 以抵消倾斜，但甲板的倾斜角度却越来越大。

s.en: Then the sound of rumbling thunder reached the watchers on the shore,
s.zh: 接着，轰隆的雷声传到了岸边观望的人们耳边。

s.en: as cargo, ballast, ammunition and 400 people went sliding and crashing down to the port side of the steeply listing ship.
s.zh: 货物、压舱物、弹药和400人滑落并撞向严重倾斜的船的左舷。

s.en: The lower gun-ports were now below water and the inrush sealed the ship's fate.
s.zh: 船上的下层炮口此时已经浸没在水中，海水涌入船内，注定了这艘船的毁灭。

s.en: In that first glorious hour, the mighty Vasa, which was intended to rule the Baltic,
s.zh: 在光荣的第一个小时里，这艘本应称霸波罗的海的巨舰“瓦萨号”

s.en: sank with all flags flying--in the harbour of her birth.
s.zh: 它带着所有的旗帜，在自己出生的港口沉没了。

q: The 'Vasa'
“瓦萨号”
q2: --ROY SAUNGERS The Raising of the' Vasa 'from The Listener--

s.en: This is a sceptical age,
s.zh: 这是一个充满怀疑的时代。

s.en: but although our faith in many of the things in which our forefathers fervently believed has weakened,
s.zh: 尽管我们对祖先们坚信的许多事物的信心已经减弱，

s.en: our confidence in the curative properties of the bottle of medicine remains the same as theirs.
s.zh: 但我们对药物疗效的信任却依然与他们一样坚定。

s.en: This modern faith in medicines is proved by the fact
s.zh: 这种对药物的现代信仰，从卫生服务部门的年度药品开支不断攀升至天文数字这一事实中得到了证明，

s.en: that the annual drug bill of the Health Services is mounting to astronomical figures
s.zh: 而且目前这种趋势还没有停止的迹象。

s.en: and shows no signs at present of ceasing to rise.
s.zh: 大多数前往医院门诊部就诊的患者认为，

s.en: The majority of the patients attending the medical out-patients departments of our hospitals feel that
s.zh: 除非他们能带回家

s.en: they have not received adequate treatment unless they are able to carry home with them
s.zh: 一瓶药、一盒药片或一小罐药膏这样实实在在的药物，

s.en: some tangible remedy in the shape of a bottle of medicine,
s.zh: 否则就觉得自己没有得到充分的治疗。

s.en: a box of pills, or a small jar of ointment,
s.zh: 负责该科室的医生也非常乐意满足他们的这些要求。

s.en: and the doctor in charge of the department is only too ready to provide them with these requirements.
s.zh: 没有比给患者他们所要的东西更快打发他们的方法了。

s.en: There is no quicker method of disposing of patients than by giving them what they are asking for,
s.zh: 而且由于卫生系统中的大多数医生都工作过度

s.en: and since most medical men in the Health Services are overworked
s.zh: 因此，他们几乎没有时间去提供那些耗时且不太受重视的建议——比如关于饮食方面的建议。

s.en: and have little time for offering time-consuming and little-appreciated advice on such subjects as diet,
s.zh: 正确的生活方式，以及摒弃不良习惯的必要性等等。

s.en: right living, and the need for abandoning bad habits etc.,
s.zh: 他们几乎总能得到所要求的药水、药片和药膏。

s.en: the bottle, the box, and the jar are almost always granted them.
s.zh: 并不是只有那些无知或受教育程度低的人才会对药瓶（或药物）抱有如此大的信任（或依赖）。

s.en: Nor is it only the ignorant and ill-educated person who has such faith in the bottle of medicine.
s.zh: 据记载，当托马斯·卡莱尔得知他的朋友亨利·泰勒生病了之后……

s.en: It is recounted of Thomas Carlyle that when he heard of the illness of his friend, Henry Taylor,
s.zh: 他立刻动身去拜访他了。

s.en: he went off immediately to visit him,
s.zh: 口袋里还装着一瓶剩下的药，这瓶药原本是给卡莱尔夫人开的，用于治疗她的小毛病。

s.en: carrying with him in his pocket what remained of a bottle of medicine formerly prescribed for an indisposition of Mrs. Carlyle's.
s.zh: 卡莱尔完全不知道自己口袋里的瓶子里装着什么。

s.en: Carlyle was entirely ignorant of what the bottle in his pocket contained,
s.zh: 关于他的朋友所患疾病的性质……

s.en: of the nature of the illness from which his friend was suffering,
s.zh: 以及他妻子之前得了什么病。

s.en: and of what had previously been wrong with his wife,
s.zh: 但是，一种在某种疾病治疗中效果非常好的药物，肯定也会对另一种疾病产生同样的治疗效果。

s.en: but a medicine that had worked so well in one form of illness would surely be of equal benefit in another,
s.zh: 并且因为想到自己能为朋友提供帮助而感到欣慰（或：感到安慰）。

s.en: and comforted by the thought of the help he was bringing to his friend,
s.zh: 他急忙赶往亨利·泰勒的家中。

s.en: he hastened to Henry Taylor's house.
s.zh: 历史没有记载他的朋友是否接受了他的医疗帮助，但很可能接受了。

s.en: History does not relate whether his friend accepted his medical help, but in all probability he did.
s.zh: 吃药的最大好处是它对服药者没有任何要求，

s.en: The great advantage of taking medicine is that it makes no demands on the taker
s.zh: 除了暂时忍受一下难吃的味道之外。

s.en: beyond that of putting up for a moment with a disgusting taste,
s.zh: 而这正是所有患者对医生所要求的：能够得到治疗，同时自己不必承受任何不便或麻烦。

s.en: and that is what all patients demand of their doctors--to be cured at no inconvenience to themselves.

q: What are patients looking for when they visit the doctor?
患者去看医生时，他们在寻找什么？

s.en: Many strange new means of transport have been developed in our century,
s.zh: 在我们这个世纪，许多新型的、奇特的交通工具被开发出来了。

s.en: the strangest of them being perhaps the hovercraft.
s.zh: 其中最奇怪的，或许要数那艘气垫船了。

s.en: In 1953, a former electronics engineer in his fifties, Christopher Cockerell,
s.zh: 1953年，一位五十多岁的前电子工程师克里斯托弗·科克雷尔（Christopher Cockerell）……

s.en: who had turned to boat-building on the Norfolk Broads,
s.zh: 他后来转而在诺福克湖区从事造船业，

s.en: suggested an idea on which he had been working for many years to the British Government and industrial circles.
s.zh: 他向英国政府和工业界提出了一项自己多年来一直在研究的想法。

s.en: It was the idea of supporting a craft on a 'pad', or cushion, of low-pressure air, ringed with a curtain of higher pressure air.
s.zh: 这个想法的核心在于：利用一层低压空气作为“垫子”或“支撑层”来托住某个物体（比如飞行器），而该低压空气层则被一层高压空气所包围。

s.en: Ever since, people have had difficulty in deciding whether the craft should be ranged among ships, planes,
s.zh: 从那以后，人们就一直难以确定这种交通工具应该被归类为船舶、飞机中的哪一类。

s.en: or land vehicles--for it is something in between a boat and an aircraft.
s.zh: 或者陆地交通工具——因为它介于船和飞机之间。

s.en: As a shipbuilder, Cockerell was trying to find a solution to the problem of the wave resistance which wastes a good deal of a surface ship's power and limits its speed.
s.zh: 作为一名造船工程师，科克雷尔一直在努力寻找解决船舶波浪阻力问题的方法。波浪阻力会浪费船舶大量动力，并限制其航行速度。

s.en: His answer was to lift the vessel out of the water by making it ride on a cushion of air, no more than one or two feet thick.
s.zh: 他的解决方案是让船漂浮在一片空气“垫层”上，这片空气垫层的厚度不超过一两英尺。

s.en: This is done by a great number of ring-shaped air jets on the bottom of the craft.
s.zh: 这是通过气垫船底部大量环形喷气装置来实现的。

s.en: It 'flies', therefore, but it cannot fly higher--its action depends on the surface, water or ground, over which it rides.
s.zh: 因此，它确实能够“飞行”，但它无法飞得更高；它的运动方式取决于它所依附的表面——无论是水面还是地面。

s.en: The first tests on the Solent in 1959 caused a sensation.
s.zh: 1959年，在索伦特海峡进行的首次试验引起了轰动。

s.en: The hovercraft travelled first over the water, then mounted the beach, climbed up the dunes, and sat down on a road.
s.zh: 气垫船先在水面上行驶，然后驶上了沙滩，接着爬上了沙丘，最后停在了道路上。

s.en: Later it crossed the Channel, riding smoothly over the waves, which presented no problem.
s.zh: 后来，它穿过了英吉利海峡，平稳地掠过海浪——整个过程没有任何问题。

s.en: Since that time, various types of hovercraft have appeared and taken up regular service.
s.zh: 从那时起，各种类型的气垫船相继问世，并开始被广泛使用（即投入日常运营）。

s.en: The hovercraft is particularly useful in large areas with poor communications such as Africa or Australia;
s.zh: 气垫船在交通不便的广大地区（如非洲或澳大利亚）特别有用。

s.en: it can become a 'flying fruit-bowl', carrying bananas from the plantations to the ports;
s.zh: 它可以变成一个“会飞的果盘”，负责将香蕉从种植园运送到港口。

s.en: giant hovercraft liners could span the Atlantic;
s.zh: 巨大的气垫船客轮或许能够横渡大西洋。

s.en: and the railway of the future may well be the 'hovertrain',
s.zh: 未来的铁路很可能会是“悬浮列车”。

s.en: riding on its air cushion over a single rail, which it never touches, at speeds, up to 300 m.p.h.--the possibilities appear unlimited.
s.zh: 这种装置依靠空气垫在单根轨道上行驶，且从未与轨道接触；其行驶速度可达到每小时300英里。由此看来，它的应用可能性似乎是无限的。
