气垫船在运动时是“骑”在什么上面的呢？
q2: --EGON LARSEN The Pegasus Book of Inventors--

s.en: Our knowledge of the oceans a hundred years ago was confined to the two-dimensional shape of the sea surface
s.zh: 一百年前，我们对海洋的了解仅限于海面的二维形态。

s.en: and the hazards of navigation presented by the irregularities in depth of the shallow water close to the land.
s.zh: 以及由于靠近陆地的浅水区水深不均匀所带来的航行危险。

s.en: The open sea was deep and mysterious,
s.zh: 广阔的海洋深邃而神秘。

s.en: and anyone who gave more than a passing thought to the bottom confines of the oceans probably assumed that the sea-bed was flat.
s.zh: 任何稍微思考过海洋底部情况的人，很可能都认为海床是平坦的。

s.en: Sir James Clark Ross had obtained a sounding of over 2,400 fathoms in 1839,
s.zh: 詹姆斯·克拉克·罗斯爵士在1839年测得水深超过了2,400英寻（约4,389米）。

s.en: but it was not until 1869, when H.M.S. Porcupine was put at the disposal of the Royal Society for several cruises
s.zh: 但直到 1869 年，“H.M.S. Porcupine”号才被交由皇家学会使用，用于多次科学考察航行。

s.en: that a series of deep soundings was obtained in the Atlantic and the first samples were collected by dredging the bottom.
s.zh: 在大西洋进行了一系列深海探测，并通过挖掘海底的方式采集到了首批样本。

s.en: Shortly after this the famous H.M.S. Challenger expedition established the study of the sea-floor
s.zh: 不久之后，著名的H.M.S.挑战者号探险队开始了对海底的研究工作。

s.en: as a subject worthy of the most qualified physicists and geologists.
s.zh: 一个值得最顶尖物理学家和地质学家研究的课题。

s.en: A burst of activity associated with the laying of submarine cables
s.zh: 与铺设海底电缆相关的一系列活动迅速展开。

s.en: soon confirmed the Challenger's observation that many parts of the ocean were two to three miles deep,
s.zh: 很快证实了挑战者的观察结果：海洋的许多区域深度在两到三英里之间。

s.en: and the existence of underwater features of considerable magnitude.
s.zh: 以及水下存在一些规模相当大的地质结构（或地貌特征）。

s.en: Today, enough soundings are available to enable a relief map of the Atlantic to be drawn
s.zh: 如今，我们已经收集到了足够多的数据，可以绘制出大西洋的海底地形图（即“海底 relief map”）。

s.en: and we know something of the great variety of the sea bed's topography.
s.zh: 我们对海底地形的多样性也有所了解。

s.en: Since the sea covers the greater part of the earth's surface,
s.zh: 由于海洋覆盖了地球表面的大部分区域，

s.en: it is quite reasonable to regard the sea floor as the basic form of the crust of the earth,
s.zh: 将海底视为地球地壳的基本构成部分，这是完全合理的。

s.en: with superimposed upon it the continents,
s.zh: 大陆叠加其上，

s.en: together with the islands and other features of the oceans.
s.zh: 连同海洋中的岛屿以及其他地形特征一起。

s.en: The continents form rugged tablelands which stand nearly three miles above the floor of the open ocean.
s.zh: 这些大陆形成了崎岖的高原地带，其高度几乎比开阔海域的海底高出三英里（约4.8公里）。

s.en: From the shore line, out to a distance which may be anywhere from a few miles to a few hundred miles,
s.zh: 从海岸线开始，延伸到距离海岸几英里到几百英里的范围内……

s.en: runs the gentle slope of the continental shelf, geologically part of the continents.
s.zh: 沿着大陆架的平缓坡度延伸；从地质学角度来看，大陆架属于大陆的一部分。

s.en: The real dividing line between continents and oceans occurs at the foot of a steeper slope.
s.zh: 实际上，大陆与海洋之间的分界线位于一个更陡峭的斜坡的底部。

s.en: This continental slope usually starts at a place somewhere near the 100-fathom mark
s.zh: 这个大陆坡通常始于水深约100英寻（约183米）的位置。

s.en: and in the course of a few hundred miles reaches the true ocean floor at 2,500-3,500 fathoms.
s.zh: 在延伸数百英里后，它最终抵达真正的海底，那里的水深为2,500至3,500英寻（约4,572至6,400米）。

s.en: The slope averages about 1 in 30, but contains steep,
s.zh: 坡度的平均比例约为1:30（即每水平延伸30单位，垂直下降1单位），但其中也包含陡峭的、

s.en: probably vertical, cliffs, and gentle sediment-covered terraces,
s.zh: 可能是垂直的悬崖，以及被松软沉积物覆盖的缓坡地形。

s.en: and near its lower reaches there is a long tailing-off which is almost certainly the result of
s.zh: 在其下端附近，有一段逐渐变缓的延伸带，这几乎可以肯定是

s.en: material transported out to deep water after being eroded from the continental masses.
s.zh: 从大陆侵蚀下来并被输送到深水区的物质堆积的结果。

q: How did people probably imagine the sea-floor before it was investigated?
在人们开始对海底进行探索之前，他们可能是如何想象海底的样子的呢？

s.en: Appreciation of sculpture depends upon the ability to respond to form in 3 dimensions.
s.zh: 对雕塑的欣赏，取决于人们能否理解和回应三维空间中的形态（即雕塑的立体结构与形态特征）。

s.en: That is perhaps why sculpture has been described as the most difficult of all arts;
s.zh: 也许正因为如此，雕塑才被人们称为所有艺术形式中最难掌握的一种。

s.en: certainly it is more difficult than the arts which involve appreciation of flat forms, shape in only two dimensions.
s.zh: 当然，这比那些只需要欣赏二维平面形状的艺术形式要困难得多。

s.en: Many more people are 'form-blind' than colour-blind.
s.zh: 有'形式盲'的人比有色盲的人多得多。

s.en: The child learning to see, first distinguishes only two-dimensional shape; it cannot judge distances, depths.
s.zh: 正在学习观察事物的孩子最初只能识别二维的形状；他们还无法判断距离或物体的深度。

s.en: Later, for its personal safety and practical needs, it has to develop (partly by means of touch) the ability to judge roughly 3-dimensional distances.
s.zh: 后来，为了自身安全和实际需要，它必须（部分通过触觉）培养出大致判断三维距离的能力。

s.en: But having satisfied the requirements of practical necessity, most people go no further.
s.zh: 然而，在满足了实际需求之后，大多数人就不会再进一步去追求更高的目标了。

s.en: Though they may attain considerable accuracy in the perception of flat form,
s.zh: 尽管他们在识别平面形状方面可以达到相当高的准确度，

s.en: they do not make the further intellectual and emotional effort needed to comprehend form in its full spatial existence.
s.zh: 他们没有付出进一步的智力与情感努力，去全面理解“形式”在其空间存在中的本质（即形式在三维空间中的具体表现方式）。

s.en: This is what the sculptor must do.
s.zh: 这就是雕塑家必须做的事情。

s.en: He must strive continually to think of and use, form in its full spatial completeness.
s.zh: 他必须不断努力去思考和运用形式在空间中的完整性。

s.en: He gets the solid shape as it were, inside his head--he thinks of it, whatever its size, as if he were holding it completely enclosed in the hollow of his hand.
s.zh: 他在脑海中清晰地想象出那个物体的形状；无论这个物体的实际大小如何，他都仿佛能够将其完全握在手中一样。

s.en: He mentally visualizes a complex form from all round itself;
s.zh: 他在脑海中从各个角度想象出一个复杂的形体；

s.en: he knows while he looks at one side what the other side is like; he identifies himself with its centre of gravity, its mass, its weight;
s.zh: 他看着一面时就知道另一面是什么样子；他体会其重心、质量和重量。

s.en: he realizes its volume as the space that the shape displaces in the air.
s.zh: 他认识到这个物体的“体积”，其实就是该物体在空气中占据的空间（即该物体将空气“挤开”后所形成的空间）。

s.en: And the sensitive observer of sculpture must also learn to feel shape simply as shape, not as description or reminiscence.
s.zh: 对于雕塑而言，敏锐的观察者也必须学会纯粹地将形状视为形状本身来感知它，而不是将其视为某种描述或回忆的象征。

s.en: He must, for example, perceive an egg as a simple single solid shape quite apart from its significance as food,
s.zh: 例如，他必须将鸡蛋仅仅视为一个简单的、独立的固体形状，而忽略其作为食物的意义。

s.en: or from the literary idea that it will become a bird.
s.zh: 也不把它看作会变成鸟的文学意象。

s.en: And so with solids such as a shell, a nut, a plum, a pear, a tadpole, a mushroom,
s.zh: 同样，对于贝壳、坚果、李子、梨、蝌蚪、蘑菇等固体，

s.en: a mountain peak, a kidney, a carrot, a tree-trunk, a bird, a bud, a lark, a ladybird, a bulrush, a bone.
s.zh: 山峰、肾脏、胡萝卜、树干、鸟、花蕾、云雀、瓢虫、香蒲、骨头。

s.en: From these he can go on to appreciate more complex forms or combinations of several forms.
s.zh: 从这些出发，他可以进而欣赏更复杂的形式或多种形式的组合。

q: What do you have to be able to do to appreciate sculpture?
要真正欣赏雕塑，你需要具备哪些条件或能力呢？

s.en: In his own lifetime Galileo was the centre of violent controversy, but the scientific dust has long since settled,
s.zh: 在伽利略有生之年，他一直是激烈争议的焦点；然而，那些科学上的争论早已平息，尘埃也已落定。

s.en: and today we can see even his famous clash with the Inquisition in something like its proper perspective.
s.zh: 今天，我们终于能够以更加客观的角度来看待他那场著名的与宗教裁判所的冲突了。

s.en: But, in contrast, it is only in modern times that Galileo has become a problem child for historians of science.
s.zh: 然而，相比之下，直到现代，伽利略才成为科学史学家们眼中的一个麻烦人物。

s.en: The old view of Galileo was delightfully uncomplicated.
s.zh: 人们对伽利略的看法过去非常简单明了（即：人们过去对伽利略的看法非常直接、容易理解）。

s.en: He was, above all, a man who experimented:
s.zh: 他首先是一个喜欢进行实验的人。

s.en: who despised the prejudice and book learning of the Aristotelians,
s.zh: 他鄙视亚里士多德学派的偏见和迂腐的书本知识，

s.en: who put his questions to nature instead of to the ancients, and who drew his conclusions fearlessly.
s.zh: 他把问题提给大自然而不是古人，并勇敢地得出结论。

s.en: He had been the first to turn a telescope to the sky,
s.zh: 他是第一个将望远镜对准天空的人。

s.en: and he had seen there evidence enough to overthrow Aristotle and Ptolemy together.
s.zh: 他看到了足够的证据，足以推翻亚里士多德和托勒密的理论。

s.en: He was the man who climbed the Leaning Tower of Pisa and dropped various weights from the top,
s.zh: 他就是那个爬上比萨斜塔并从塔顶扔下各种重物的人。

s.en: who rolled balls down inclined planes, and then generalized the results of his many experiments into the famous law of free fall.
s.zh: 他让球体沿斜面滚下，然后将众多实验结果归纳成著名的自由落体定律。

s.en: But a closer study of the evidence,
s.zh: 但是，对证据进行更仔细的研究之后……

s.en: supported by a deeper sense of the period, and particularly by a new consciousness of the philosophical undercurrents in the scientific revolution,
s.zh: 这种研究建立在对那个时代更深刻的理解之上，特别是对科学革命中哲学暗流的全新认识。

s.en: has profoundly modified this view of Galileo.
s.zh: 这极大地改变了人们对伽利略的看法。

s.en: Today, although the old Galileo lives on in many popular writings, among historians of science a new and more sophisticated picture has emerged.
s.zh: 如今，尽管老伽利略的形象仍然存在于许多通俗的文学作品中，但在科学史学家们看来，关于他的新观点和更复杂的认识已经逐渐形成。

s.en: At the same time our sympathy for Galileo's opponents has grown somewhat.
s.zh: 与此同时，我们对伽利略的反对者的同情心也有所增加。

s.en: His telescopic observations are justly immortal;
s.zh: 他的望远镜观测成果当之无愧地被载入史册，永垂不朽。

s.en: they aroused great interest at the time,
s.zh: 它们在当时引起了极大的兴趣。

s.en: they had important theoretical consequences,
s.zh: 它们具有重要的理论意义，

s.en: and they provided a striking demonstration of the potentialities hidden in instruments and apparatus.
s.zh: 它们生动地展示了仪器和设备中蕴藏的巨大潜力。

s.en: But can we blame those who looked and failed to see what Galileo saw,
s.zh: 但是，我们能责怪那些明明有机会却未能看到伽利略所发现的东西的人吗？

s.en: if we remember that to use a telescope at the limit of its powers calls for long experience and intimate familiarity with one's instrument?
s.zh: 如果我们记得：把一台望远镜的性能发挥到极限，就需要具备丰富的使用经验，并且对这台仪器有非常深入的了解（即对其工作原理、操作方法等了如指掌）的话……

s.en: Was the philosopher who refused to look through Galileo's telescope more culpable than those who alleged
s.zh: 那位拒绝通过伽利略的望远镜观察的哲学家，难道比那些声称

s.en: that the spiral nebulae observed with Lord Rosse's great telescope in the 1840s were scratches left by the grinder?
s.zh: 罗斯勋爵在19世纪40年代用大型望远镜观测到的螺旋星云只是镜片磨制者留下的划痕的人，更应受到责备吗？

s.en: We can perhaps forgive those who said the moons of Jupiter were produced by Galileo's spyglass if we recall that in his day,
s.zh: 如果我们记得在他那个时代，和几个世纪前一样，曲面玻璃是流行的造假工具，产生的不是真相而是幻象，那么我们或许可以原谅那些说木星的卫星是伽利略的望远镜造出来的人。

s.en: as for centuries before, curved glass was the popular contrivance for producing not truth but illusion, untruth;
s.zh: 因为如果单片曲面玻璃就会扭曲自然，那么双片曲面玻璃造成的扭曲岂不更严重？

s.en: and if a single curved glass would distort nature, how much more would a pair of them?

q: What has modified our traditional view of Galileo in recent times?
近年来，是什么改变了我们对伽利略的传统看法？
q2: --MICHAEL HOSKIN Galileo Reborn from The Listener--
--迈克尔·霍斯金·伽利略从《倾听者》中重生--

s.en: Education is one of the key words of our time.
s.zh: “教育”是我们这个时代的核心关键词之一。

s.en: A man without an education, many of us believe,
s.zh: 我们中的许多人认为，一个没有受过教育的人……

s.en: is an unfortunate victim of adverse circumstances, deprived of one of the greatest twentieth-century opportunities.
s.zh: 是恶劣环境的不幸受害者，被剥夺了20世纪最伟大的机遇之一。

s.en: Convinced of the importance of education, modern states 'invest' in institutions of learning to get back 'interest'
s.zh: 确信教育的重要性，现代国家‘投资’于教育机构，以‘利息’的形式

s.en: in the form of a large group of enlightened young men and women who are potential leaders.
s.zh: 收回一群有教养的青年男女，他们是潜在的领导者。

s.en: Education, with its cycles of instruction so carefully worked out,
s.zh: 教育，其教学流程都是经过精心设计的……

s.en: punctuated by textbooks--those purchasable wells of wisdom--what would civilization be like without its benefits?
s.zh: 被教科书——那些可以购买的智慧之井——所点缀，如果没有它的好处，文明会是什么样子？

s.en: So much is certain: that we would have doctors and preachers,
s.zh: 有几点是确定的：我们一定会拥有医生和传教士。

s.en: lawyers and defendants, marriages and births--but our spiritual outlook would be different.
s.zh: 律师和被告，婚姻和出生——但我们的精神面貌会有所不同。

s.en: We would lay less stress on 'facts and figures' and more on a good memory,
s.zh: 我们会减少对“事实和数据”的依赖，而更加重视良好的记忆力。

s.en: on applied psychology, and on the capacity of a man to get along with his fellow-citizens.
s.zh: 应用心理学，以及一个人与同胞相处的能力。

s.en: If our educational system were fashioned after its bookless past we would have the most democratic form of 'college' imaginable.
s.zh: 如果我们的教育体系模仿其无书籍的过去，我们会有可以想象的最民主的‘大学’形式。

s.en: Among tribal people all knowledge inherited by tradition is shared by all;
s.zh: 在部落社会中，所有通过传统传承下来的知识都是大家共同拥有的。

s.en: it is taught to every member of the tribe so that in this respect everybody is equally equipped for life.
s.zh: 它被传授给部落的每个成员，因此在这方面每个人都同样为生活做好了准备。

s.en: It is the ideal condition of the 'equal start' which only our most progressive forms of modern education try to regain.
s.zh: 这是‘平等起步’的理想条件，只有我们最进步的现代教育形式才试图重新获得。

s.en: In primitive cultures the obligation to seek and to receive the traditional instruction is binding to all.
s.zh: 在原始文化中，寻求并接受传统教诲的义务对所有人都是具有约束力的。

s.en: There are no 'illiterates' --if the term can be applied to peoples without a script--while our own compulsory school attendance became law in Germany in 1642,
s.zh: 没有‘文盲’——如果这个词可以适用于没有文字的民族——而我们的义务教育在1642年成为德国的法律，

s.en: in France in 1806, and in England in 1876 and is still nonexistent in a number of 'civilized' nations.
s.zh: 1806年在法国，1876年在英国，而在许多‘文明’国家仍然不存在。

s.en: This shows how long it was before we deemed it necessary to make sure
s.zh: 这表明过了多久我们才认为有必要确保

s.en: that all our children could share in the knowledge accumulated by the 'happy few' during the past centuries.
s.zh: 我们所有的孩子都能分享过去几个世纪里‘少数幸运儿’积累的知识。

s.en: Education in the wilderness is not a matter of monetary means.
s.zh: 荒野中的教育不是金钱手段的问题。

s.en: All are entitled to an equal start.
s.zh: 每个人都应该拥有平等的起点。

s.en: There is none of the hurry which, in our society, often hampers the full development of a growing personality.
s.zh: 没有那种在我们社会中常常阻碍成长个性全面发展的匆忙。

s.en: There, a child grows up under the everpresent attention of his parents;
s.zh: 在那里，一个孩子在父母无时无刻不在的关注下长大。

s.en: therefore the jungles and the savannahs know of no 'juvenile delinquency'.
s.zh: 因此，丛林和热带草原不知道有‘少年犯罪’。

s.en: No necessity of making a living away from home results in neglect of children, and no father is confronted with his inability to 'buy' an education for his child.
s.zh: 没有离家谋生的必要导致对孩子的忽视，也没有父亲面对自己无力为孩子‘购买’教育的困境。

q: Why is education democratic in bookless tribal societies?
为什么在没有书籍的部落社会中，教育是民主的？
q2: --JULIUS E. LIPS The Origin of Things--
--朱利厄斯·利普斯《事物的起源》--

s.en: Parents are often upset when their children praise the homes of their friends and regard it as a slur on their own cooking, or cleaning, or furniture,
s.zh: 当孩子们夸赞朋友家的环境时，父母往往会感到不满，他们认为这种行为是对自己烹饪水平、清洁工作或家具质量的贬低。

s.en: and often are foolish enough to let the adolescents see that they are annoyed.
s.zh: 他们常常犯愚蠢的错误，让青少年察觉到他们其实很恼火（或：他们总是犯傻，以至于让青少年看出来他们很生气）。

s.en: They may even accuse them of disloyalty, or make some spiteful remark about the friends' parents.
s.zh: 他们甚至可能会指责孩子不忠，或者对那些朋友的父母说一些刻薄的话。

s.en: Such a loss of dignity and descent into childish behaviour on the part of the adults deeply shocks the adolescents,
s.zh: 成年人这种丧失尊严、行为变得幼稚的现象，令青少年们感到极为震惊。

s.en: and makes them resolve that in future they will not talk to their parents about the places or people they visit.
s.zh: 这让他们决定：以后不会再和父母谈论自己去过的地方或遇到的人。

s.en: Before very long the parents will be complaining that the child is so secretive and never tells them anything,
s.zh: 用不了多久，父母们就会开始抱怨孩子太保密了，从不跟他们透露任何事情。

s.en: but they seldom realize that they have brought this on themselves.
s.zh: 但他们很少意识到，这一切其实都是他们自己造成的。

s.en: Disillusionment with the parents,
s.zh: 无论父母作为父母或作为个体有多么优秀和称职，孩子对他们的失望在某种程度上都是不可避免的。

s.en: however good and adequate they may be both as parents and as individuals, is to some degree inevitable.
s.zh: 大多数孩子对他们的父母都有着非常高的期望（或：对父母有着非常美好的想象）。

s.en: Most children have such a high ideal of their parents,
s.zh: 除非父母本身的表现令人不满意，否则这种理想很难经得起现实的评估。

s.en: unless the parents themselves have been unsatisfactory, that it can hardly hope to stand up to a realistic evaluation.
s.zh: 如果父母意识到他们的孩子通常对自己的人格以及他们的“绝对正确性”抱有多大的信任，他们一定会感到非常惊讶和深受感动。

s.en: Parents would be greatly surprised and deeply touched if they realized how much belief their children usually have in their character and infallibility,
s.zh: 以及这种信念对一个孩子来说意味着什么。

s.en: and how much this faith means to a child.
s.zh: 如果父母能够预料到青少年会有这样的反应……

s.en: If parents were prepared for this adolescent reaction,
s.zh: 并意识到这正是孩子正在成长的一个迹象

s.en: and realized that it was a sign that the child was growing up
s.zh: 同时培养出宝贵的观察能力和独立判断力。

s.en: and developing valuable powers of observation and independent judgment,
s.zh: 他们就不会受到那么大的伤害；因此，也不会因为感到怨恨和抗拒而让孩子与他们产生对立情绪。

s.en: they would not be so hurt, and therefore would not drive the child into opposition by resenting and resisting it.
s.zh: 这个青少年，对真诚充满热情……

s.en: The adolescent, with his passion for sincerity,
s.zh: 总是尊重那些承认自己犯错或无知的父母。

s.en: always respects a parent who admits that he is wrong, or ignorant,
s.zh: 甚至承认自己行为不公平或不公正。

s.en: or even that he has been unfair or unjust.
s.zh: 孩子无法原谅的是：如果孩子知道父母的这些过错是事实，父母却拒绝承认。

s.en: What the child cannot forgive is the parents' refusal to admit these charges if the child knows them to be true.
s.zh: 维多利亚时代的父母认为，通过采取一种不合理的专断态度可以维护自己的尊严；但实际上，他们根本没有做到这一点。

s.en: Victorian parents believed that they kept their dignity by retreating behind an unreasoning authoritarian attitude; in fact they did nothing of the kind,
s.zh: 但那时孩子们都太胆小了，不敢说出自己的真实感受。

s.en: but children were then too cowed to let them know how they really felt.
s.zh: 如今，我们往往走向另一个极端。

s.en: Today we tend to go to the other extreme,
s.zh: 但总体来说，这种态度对孩子的成长以及父母的心理状态都有益处（即更健康）。

s.en: but on the whole this is a healthier attitude both for the child and the parent.
s.zh: 无论此刻的现实有多么痛苦，直面现实总是更为明智、也更安全的选择。

s.en: It is always wiser and safer to face up to reality, however painful it may be at the moment.

q: What do adolescents respect in parents?
青少年在父母身上尊重什么？

s.en: The Moon is likely to become the industrial hub of the Solar System supplying the rocket fuels for its ships,
s.zh: 月球很可能会成为太阳系的工业中心，为宇宙飞船提供所需的火箭燃料。

s.en: easily obtainable from the lunar rocks in the form of liquid oxygen.
s.zh: 这种物质可以从月球岩石中轻易提取出来，其形式为液态氧。

s.en: The reason lies in its gravity.
s.zh: 原因在于它的重力。

s.en: Because the Moon has only an eightieth of the Earth's mass,
s.zh: 因为月球的质量只有地球的八十分之一，

s.en: it requires 97% less energy
s.zh: 从月球到地球轨道（长达二十五万英里）所需的能量，比从地球表面进入轨道（二百英里）所需的能量要少97%！

s.en: to travel the quarter of a million miles from the Moon to Earth-orbit than the 200 mile-journey from Earth's surface into orbit!
s.zh: 这听起来可能令人难以置信，但这个结论是很容易计算出来的。

s.en: This may sound fantastic, but it is easily calculated.
s.zh: 要乘坐火箭逃离地球，必须以每秒七英里的速度飞行。

s.en: To escape from the Earth in a rocket, one must travel at seven miles per second.
s.zh: 从月球出发所需的相应速度仅为每秒1.5英里。

s.en: The comparable speed from the Moon is only 1.5 miles per second.
s.zh: 因为月球表面的重力只有地球的六分之一（还记得阿波罗宇航员在月球上行走时是多么轻松自如吗？）

s.en: Because the gravity on the Moon's surface is only a sixth of Earth's (remember how easily the Apollo astronauts bounded along),
s.zh: 在月球上，将物体加速到每秒1.5英里所需的能量要比在地球上少得多。

s.en: it takes much less energy to accelerate to that 1.5mps than it does on Earth.
s.zh: 月球居民在太空中旅行的费用，将仅为他们的地球表亲进行类似旅程所需费用的3%。

s.en: Moon dwellers will be able to fly in space at only three percent of the cost of similar journeys by their terrestrial cousins.
s.zh: 阿瑟·C·克拉克曾提出一个观点：一个革命性的想法通常会经历三个阶段：

s.en: Arthur C.Clark once suggested a revolutionary idea passes through three phases:
s.zh: 1. “这不可能——别浪费我的时间了。”

s.en: 1.  'It's impossible--don't waste my time.'
s.zh: 2. “这是可能的，但并不值得去做。”

s.en: 2.  'It's possible, but not worth doing.'
s.zh: 3. “我一直都说这是个好主意。”

s.en: 3.  'I said it was a good idea all along.'
s.zh: 当有相当数量的人能够在太空中永久居住时，将火星（一个距离地球比月球远160倍的天体）殖民化的想法，将果断地从第二阶段进入第三阶段。

s.en: The idea of colonising Mars--a world 160 times more distant than the Moon--will move decisively from the second phase to the third,
s.zh: 火星对那些渴望踏上太空之旅的人来说，具有难以抗拒的吸引力。

s.en: when a significant number of people are living permanently in space.
s.zh: 美国、俄罗斯和欧洲都有许多热衷者——其中许多是严肃资深的科学家，他们梦想着将人类送上火星。

s.en: Mars has an extraordinary fascination for would-be voyagers.
s.zh: 他们的目标是可以理解的。

s.en: America, Russia and Europe are filled with enthusiasts--many of them serious and senior scientists who dream of sending people to it.
s.zh: 它是太阳系中与地球最为相似的行星。

s.en: Their aim is understandable.
s.zh: 这是一个遍布红色沙质沙漠的世界（因此它被称为“红色星球”）。

s.en: It is the one world in the Solar System that is most like the Earth.
s.zh: 万里无云的天空、猛烈的沙尘暴、比大峡谷还要宽阔的峡谷，以及至少有一座高度超过珠穆朗玛峰两倍的山峰。

s.en: It is a world of red sandy deserts (hence its name--the Red Planet),
s.zh: 这似乎非常适合用于定居。

s.en: cloudless skies, savage sandstorms, chasms wider than the Grand Canyon and at least one mountain more than twice as tall as Everest.
It seems ideal for settlement.

q: When will it be possible for us to think seriously about colonising Mars?
我们什么时候才能真正认真地考虑在火星上建立殖民地呢？

s.en: If a nation is essentially disunited, it is left to the government to hold it together.
s.zh: 如果一个国家本质上处于分裂状态，那么维持国家的统一就只能依靠政府的力量了。

s.en: This increases the expense of government, and reduces correspondingly the amount of economic resources that could be used for developing the country.
s.zh: 这增加了政府的开支，相应地减少了可用于国家发展的经济资源。

s.en: And it should not be forgotten how small those resources are in a poor and backward country.
s.zh: 而且我们不应忘记：在这样一个贫穷且落后的国家里，这些资源是多么的匮乏（或者说，这些资源的数量是多么的有限）。

s.en: Where the cost of government is high, resources for development are correspondingly low.
s.zh: 在政府开支较高的地方，用于发展的资源相应地也会减少。

s.en: This may be illustrated by comparing the position of a nation with that of a private business enterprise.
s.zh: 这可以通过将一个国家的地位与一家私营企业的地位进行比较来说明。

s.en: An enterprise has to incur certain costs and expenses in order to stay in business.
s.zh: 企业必须承担一定的成本和开支，才能维持自身的运营。

s.en: For our purposes, we are concerned only with one kind of cost--the cost of managing and administering the business.
s.zh: 就我们的目的而言，我们只关注一种成本——即管理和运营企业的成本。

s.en: Such administrative overheads in a business are analogous to the cost of government in a nation.
s.zh: 在企业中，这些行政开销就相当于一个国家中的政府开支。

s.en: The administrative overheads of a business are low to the extent that everyone working in the business
s.zh: 企业的行政开支之所以低，是因为企业里的每一位员工

s.en: can be trusted to behave in a way that best promotes the interests of the firm.
s.zh: 可以信赖他们会以最有利于公司利益的方式行事。

s.en: If they can each be trusted to take such responsibilities,
s.zh: 如果他们每个人都能被信任去承担这样的责任的话……

s.en: and to exercise such initiative as falls within their sphere, then administrative overheads will be low.
s.zh: 如果他们能够在自己的职责范围内主动采取行动，那么行政成本将会很低。

s.en: It will be low because it will be necessary to have only one man looking after each job without having another man to check upon what he is doing,
s.zh: 行政成本之所以会很低，是因为每项工作只需要一个人负责，而不需要另一个人去监督他

s.en: keep him in line, and report on him to someone else.
s.zh: 让他遵守规定，并向其他人汇报他的表现。

s.en: But if no one can be trusted to act in a loyal and responsible manner towards his job,
s.zh: 但如果没有人能够被信任以忠诚和负责任的态度对待自己的工作的话……

s.en: then the business will require armies of administrators, checkers and foremen and administrative overheads will rise correspondingly.
s.zh: 那么，企业将需要大量的管理人员、审核人员以及工头；相应的，管理成本也会随之增加。

s.en: As administrative overheads rise, so the earnings of the business after meeting the expense of administration, will fall;
s.zh: 随着行政开支的增加，企业在扣除行政费用后的净利润也会相应下降。

s.en: and the business will have less money to distribute as dividends or invest directly in its future progress and development.
s.zh: 这样一来，企业可用于分配作为股息的资金，以及用于直接投资其未来发展与进步的资金，都会减少。

s.en: It is precisely the same with a nation.
s.zh: 对于一个国家来说，情况也是如此。

s.en: To the extent that the people can be relied on to behave in a loyal and responsible manner,
s.zh: 在人们能够被信赖、会以忠诚和负责任的方式行事的前提下，

s.en: the government does not require armies of police and civil servants to keep them in order.
s.zh: 政府并不需要大量的警察和公务员来维持社会秩序。

s.en: But if a nation is disunited, the government cannot be sure that the actions of the people will be in the interests of the nation;
s.zh: 但是，如果一个国家处于分裂状态，政府就无法确保人民的行为会符合国家的利益。

s.en: and it will have to watch, check, and control the people accordingly.
s.zh: 它将不得不监视、检查和控制人民

s.en: A disunited nation therefore has to incur unduly high costs of government.
s.zh: 因此，一个分裂的国家不得不承担过高额的政府开支。

q: What's the most important factor, both in government or business, for keeping running costs low?
在政府或企业中，保持运营成本处于较低水平的最重要因素是什么？
q2: --雷蒙德·弗罗斯特 《落后的社会》--

s.en: At the age of twelve years, the human body is at its most vigorous.
s.zh: 在十二岁的时候，人体正处于最旺盛的发育阶段。

s.en: It has yet to reach its full size and strength, and its owner his or her full intelligence: but at this age the likelihood of death is least.
s.zh: 它还没有达到自己的最大体型和最强壮的状态，其主人也尚未发挥出全部智力；不过在这个阶段，死亡的风险是最小的。

s.en: Earlier, we were infants and young children, and consequently more vulnerable;
s.zh: 早些时候，我们还是婴儿和幼儿，因此更加脆弱。

s.en: later, we shall undergo a progressive loss of our vigour and resistance which, though imperceptible at first,
s.zh: 后来，我们的体力和抵抗力会逐渐减弱；虽然这种变化起初并不明显，但最终会变得显而易见。

s.en: will finally become so steep that we can live no longer,
s.zh: 最终，情况会变得如此糟糕，以至于我们再也无法生存下去了。

s.en: however well we look after ourselves, and however well society, and our doctors, look after us.
s.zh: 无论我们自己多么注重保养身体，无论社会和医生为我们提供了多么优质的医疗服务，情况依然可能不尽如人意。

s.en: This decline in vigour with the passing of time is called ageing.
s.zh: 这种随着时间推移而逐渐减弱的能力或活力，被称为“衰老”。

s.en: It is one of the most unpleasant discoveries which we all make that we must decline in this way, that if we escape wars,
s.zh: 我们都会发现一件极不愉快的事：我们必定会这样衰退；即使躲过战争、

s.en: accidents and diseases we shall eventually 'die of old age', and that this happens at a rate which differs little from person to person,
s.zh: 事故和疾病，最终也会“老死”，而衰退的速度因人而异的差别很小。

s.en: so that there are heavy odds in favour of our dying between the ages of 65 and 80.
s.zh: 因此，我们在 65 到 80 岁之间死亡的概率非常高。

s.en: Some of us will die sooner, a few will live longer -- on into a ninth or tenth decade.
s.zh: 我们中的一些人会早逝，而另一些人则会活得更长，能活到八十多岁或九十多岁。

s.en: But the chances are against it,
s.zh: 但是，这种可能性非常小。

s.en: and there is a virtual limit on how long we can hope to remain alive, however lucky and robust we are.
s.zh: 无论我们多么幸运、身体多么强健，我们的生命都存在一个客观的、无法超越的极限。

s.en: Normal people tend to forget this process unless and until they are reminded of it.
s.zh: 普通人往往会忘记这个过程，除非有人提醒他们。

s.en: We are so familiar with the fact that man ages, that people have for years assumed that the process of losing vigour with time,
s.zh: 我们非常清楚人类会衰老这一事实；多年来，人们一直认为随着时间的推移，人体会逐渐失去活力。

s.en: of becoming more likely to die the older we get, was something self-evident
s.zh: 随着年龄的增长，死亡风险增加这一事实是显而易见的。

s.en: like the cooling of a hot kettle or the wearing-out of a pair of shoes.
s.zh: 就像热水壶冷却下来，或者一双鞋子被穿破一样。

s.en: They have also assumed that all animals,
s.zh: 他们还假设所有的动物……

s.en: and probably other organisms such as trees, or even the universe itself, must in the nature of things 'wear out'.
s.zh: 很可能其他生物，甚至整个宇宙本身，按照自然规律也都会“逐渐磨损”或衰败。

s.en: Most animals we commonly observe do in fact age as we do,
s.zh: 我们日常生活中观察到的大多数动物确实会像我们一样衰老。

s.en: if given the chance to live long enough;
s.zh: 如果有机会活得足够长的话……

s.en: and mechanical systems like a wound watch, or the sun,
s.zh: 以及像上了发条的手表或太阳这样的机械系统。

s.en: do in fact run out of energy in accordance with the second law of thermodynamics (whether the whole universe does so is a moot point at present).
s.zh: 根据热力学第二定律，能量确实会逐渐耗尽（至于整个宇宙是否如此，目前仍有争议）。

s.en: But these are not analogous to what happens when man ages.
s.zh: 但这些情况与人类衰老过程中的变化并不相似。

s.en: A run-down watch is still a watch and can be rewound.
s.zh: 一块发条走完的手表仍然是手表，可以重新上发条。

s.en: An old watch, by contrast, becomes so worn and unreliable that it eventually is not worth mending.
s.zh: 相比之下，一块旧手表会因为长时间的使用而变得非常破旧、不可靠，最终甚至不值得修理了。

s.en: But a watch could never repair itself--it does not consist of living parts, only of metal, which wears away by friction.
s.zh: 但是，手表永远无法自我修复——它并没有任何“活的”部件，只由金属构成，而金属会因摩擦而逐渐磨损。

s.en: We could, at one time, repair ourselves--well enough, at least, to overcome all but the most instantly fatal illnesses and accidents.
s.zh: 曾经，我们能够自我修复——至少能够修复到足以克服除那些瞬间致命的疾病和意外之外的所有伤害的程度。

s.en: Between twelve and eighty years we gradually lose this power;
s.zh: 在十二岁到八十岁之间，我们逐渐失去了这种能力。

s.en: an illness which at 12 would knock us over, at 80 can knock us out, and into our grave.
s.zh: 一种疾病：在12岁时就可能让我们倒下，而在80岁时则可能让我们彻底失去生命，直接送我们进坟墓。

s.en: If we could stay as vigorous as we are at twelve,
s.zh: 如果我们能保持十二岁时那样的活力和精力……

s.en: it would take about 700 years for half of us to die, and another 700 for the survivors to be reduced by half again.
s.zh: 大约需要700年的时间，我们中的一半人会死去；再过700年，剩下的幸存者数量又会减少一半。

q: What is one of the most unpleasant discoveries we make about ourselves as we get older?
随着年龄的增长，关于我们自己，我们会发现哪些最令人不快的真相（或事实）呢？

s.en: Contamination of water supplies is usually due to poor sanitation close to water sources,
s.zh: 水源的污染通常是由于水源附近卫生条件差所导致的。

s.en: sewage disposal into the sources themselves, leakage of sewage into distribution systems or contamination with industrial or farm waste.
s.zh: 污水被直接排放到水源中；污水泄漏到供水系统中；或者水源被工业或农业废弃物污染。

s.en: Even if a piped water supply is safe at its source, it is not always safe by the time it reaches the tap.
s.zh: 即使管道输送的自来水在源头是安全的，但在到达水龙头时也不一定还是安全的。

s.en: Intermittent tap-water supplies should be regarded as particularly suspect.
s.zh: 间歇性的自来水供应应被视为特别可疑。

s.en: Travellers on short trips to areas with water supplies of uncertain quality
s.zh: 前往水质不稳定的地区的短途旅行者

s.en: should avoid drinking tap-water, or untreated water from any other source.
s.zh: 应避免饮用自来水或来自其他任何来源的未经处理的水。

s.en: It is best to keep to hot drinks, bottled or canned drinks of well-known brand names—international standards of water treatment are usually followed at bottling plants.
s.zh: 最好选择热饮，或者选择知名品牌生产的瓶装或罐装饮料。这些饮料的生产工厂通常采用国际标准的水处理工艺。

s.en: Carbonated drinks are acidic, and slightly safer.
s.zh: 碳酸饮料是酸性的，因此稍微安全一些。

s.en: Make sure that all bottles are opened in your presence, and that their rims are clean and dry.
s.zh: 请确保所有瓶子都在你的监督下被打开，并且瓶口的边缘保持干净、干燥的状态。

s.en: Boiling is always a good way of treating water.
s.zh: 煮沸始终是处理水的一种有效方法。

s.en: Some hotels supply boiled water on request and this can be used for drinking, or for brushing teeth.
s.zh: 有些酒店会根据客人的要求提供煮沸的水，这种水可以用来饮用或刷牙。

s.en: Portable boiling elements that can boil small quantities of water are useful when the right voltage of electricity is available.
s.zh: 在有合适电压的情况下，能烧开少量水的便携式煮水器很有用。

s.en: Refuse politely any cold drink from an unknown source.
s.zh: 应礼貌地拒绝任何来源不明的冷饮。

s.en: Ice is only as safe as the water from which it is made,
s.zh: 冰的安全性取决于制作它的水。

s.en: and should not be put in drinks unless it is known to be safe.
s.zh: 除非确定它是安全的，否则不应该将其添加到饮料中。

s.en: Drinks can be cooled by placing them on ice rather than adding ice to them.
s.zh: 饮料可以通过将其放在冰块上来冷却，而不是在饮料中加入冰块。

s.en: Alcohol may be a medical disinfectant, but should not be relied upon to sterilize water.
s.zh: 酒精虽然可以用作医疗消毒剂，但不应依赖它来对水进行杀菌处理。

s.en: Ethanol is more effective at a concentration of 50-70 percent;
s.zh: 乙醇在浓度为50%至70%时效果更佳。

s.en: below 20 per cent, its bactericidal action is negligible.
s.zh: 当其浓度低于20%时，其杀菌效果几乎可以忽略不计。

s.en: Spirits labelled 95 proof contain only about 47 per cent alcohol.
s.zh: 标有95 proof的烈酒只含约47%的酒精。

s.en: Beware of methylated alcohol,
s.zh: 要警惕变性酒精，

s.en: which is very poisonous and should never be added to drinking water.
s.zh: 这种物质具有很强的毒性，绝对不能被添加到饮用水中。

s.en: If no other safe water supply can be obtained,
s.zh: 如果无法获得其他安全的水源，

s.en: tap water that is too hot to touch can be left to cool and is generally safe to drink.
s.zh: 烫得无法触摸的自来水可以放凉后饮用，通常是安全的。

s.en: Those planning a trip to remote areas, or intending to live in countries where drinking water is not readily available,
s.zh: 那些计划前往偏远地区旅行，或者打算生活在饮用水不易获得的国家的人，

s.en: should know about the various possible methods for making water safe.
s.zh: 应该了解各种使水变得安全的方法。

q: What does this text describe?
这段文字描述了什么？

s.en: I have known very few writers,
s.zh: 我认识的作家其实很少。

s.en: but those I have known and whom I respect, confess at once that they have little idea where they are going when they first set pen to paper.
s.zh: 但我认识且尊敬的人们都会坦承：当他们第一次拿起笔开始写作时，其实对自己要写什么、想要表达什么几乎一无所知（或者说，他们根本不知道自己该往哪个方向去写）。

s.en: They have a character, perhaps two;
s.zh: 他们心中有一个人物，也许是两个人物。

s.en: they are in that condition of eager discomfort which passes for inspiration; all admit radical changes of destination once the journey has begun;
s.zh: 他们处于一种急切不安的状态，这种状态被当作灵感；所有人都承认，一旦旅程开始，目的地就会发生根本性的变化。

s.en: one, to my certain knowledge, spent nine months on a novel about Kashmir,
s.zh: 据我所知，有一个人花了九个月的时间来创作一部关于克什米尔的小说。

s.en: then reset the whole thing in the Scottish Highlands.
s.zh: 然后把整个故事的背景改到了苏格兰高地。

s.en: I never heard of anyone making a 'skeleton', as we were taught at school.
s.zh: 我从未听说过有人会像我们在学校学的那样先列提纲。

s.en: In the breaking and remaking, in the timing, interweaving, beginning afresh,
s.zh: 在不断的拆解和重组、在安排时序和交织情节、在重新开始的过程中，

s.en: the writer comes to discern things in his material which were not consciously in his mind when he began.
s.zh: 作者在处理材料时，会发现一些自己开始写作时并未刻意考虑过的细节或元素。

s.en: This organic process, often leading to moments of extraordinary self-discovery, is of an indescribable fascination.
s.zh: 这个自然发生的过程常常会带来令人惊叹的自我发现时刻，其魅力实在难以用语言形容。

s.en: A blurred image appears; he adds a brushstroke and another and it is gone
s.zh: 一个模糊的形象出现了；他添上一笔，又添上一笔，它就消失了

s.en: but something was there, and he will not rest till he has captured it.
s.zh: 但那里确实有什么东西；他不会罢休，直到抓住它为止。

s.en: Sometimes the yeast within a writer outlives a book he has written.
s.zh: 有时候，一个作家内心深处的“创造力”（或“灵感之源”）会比他写出的任何作品都更加持久、更加充满生命力。

s.en: I have heard of writers who read nothing but their own books;
s.zh: 我听说过有些作家，他们只读自己写的书。

s.en: like adolescents they stand before the mirror,
s.zh: 就像青少年一样，他们站在镜子前……

s.en: and still cannot fathom the exact outline of the vision before them.
s.zh: 却仍然无法看清眼前这个构想的确切轮廓。

s.en: For the same reason, writers talk interminably about their own books,
s.zh: 出于同样的原因，作家们总是滔滔不绝地谈论自己的作品。

s.en: winkling out hidden meanings, super-imposing new ones,
s.zh: 揭示隐藏的含义，同时叠加新的意义……

s.en: begging response from those around them.
s.zh: 恳求周围的人做出回应。

s.en: Of course a writer doing this is misunderstood: he might as well try to explain a crime or a love affair.
s.zh: 当然，这样的作家总是会被误解；他们其实就像是在试图解释一件犯罪行为或一段爱情故事一样——这两者都是极其复杂、难以用语言完全表达的事情。

s.en: He is also, incidentally, an unforgivable bore.
s.zh: 顺便说一下，他也是一个极其无趣、让人难以忍受的人。

s.en: This temptation to cover the distance between himself and the reader,
s.zh: 这种想要缩短自己与读者之间距离的诱惑

s.en: to study his image in the sight of those who do not know him, can be his undoing: he has begun to write to please.
s.zh: 这种想在陌生人眼中审视自己形象的渴望，可能毁了他：他已经开始为取悦而写作了。

s.en: A young English writer made the pertinent observation a year or two back
s.zh: 一两年前，一位年轻的英国作家提出了一个中肯的见解

s.en: that the talent goes into the first draft, and the art into the drafts that follow.
s.zh: 也就是说，才华体现在最初的草稿中，而艺术性则体现在后续的修改稿中。

s.en: For this reason also the writer, like any other artist,
s.zh: 正因如此，这位作家和其他艺术家一样，

s.en: has no resting place, no crowd or movement in which he may take comfort,
s.zh: 没有安身之所，没有可以让他获得慰藉的群体或运动

s.en: no judgment from outside which can replace the judgment from within.
s.zh: 没有任何外界的评判能取代内心的评判。

s.en: A writer makes order out of the anarchy of his heart;
s.zh: 作家从自己内心中的混乱与无序中创造出秩序。

s.en: he submits himself to a more ruthless discipline than any critic dreamed of,
s.zh: 他自我约束的严格程度，超出了任何批评者所能想象的。

s.en: and when he flirts with fame, he is taking time off from living with himself,
s.zh: 当他追逐名利时，他其实是在暂时中断与自我相处的时光

s.en: from the search for what his world contains at its inmost point.
s.zh: 中断对探索自己世界最核心内容的追求。

q: How do professional writers ignore what they were taught at school about writing?
专业作家是如何忽视他们在学校里学到的写作知识的呢？
q2: JOHN LE CARRÉ What Every Writer Wants from Harper's
约翰·勒CARRÉ 每个作家都想从哈泼斯得到什么

s.en: Waves are the children of the struggle between ocean and atmosphere, the ongoing signatures of infinity.
s.zh: 海浪是海洋与大气相互作用的产物，是永恒不息的印记。

s.en: Rays from the sun excite and energize the atmosphere of the earth, awakening it to flow, to movement, to rhythm, to life.
s.zh: 太阳的光线激发并赋予地球大气层能量，使其开始流动、运动、产生节奏，并充满生机。

s.en: The wind then speaks the message of the sun to the sea
s.zh: 然后，风将太阳的信息传递给了大海。

s.en: and the sea transmits it on through waves--an ancient, exquisite, powerful message.
s.zh: 海水通过海浪将这一信息传递出去——一条古老而精美的、充满力量的信息。

s.en: These ocean waves are among the earth's most complicated natural phenomena.
s.zh: 这些海浪是地球上最复杂的自然现象之一。

s.en: The basic features include a crest (the highest point of the wave),
s.zh: 基本特征包括波峰（即波浪的最高点）。

s.en: a trough (the lowest point), a height (the vertical distance from the trough to the crest),
s.zh: 波谷（即最低点），波高（即从波谷到波峰的垂直距离），

s.en: a wave length (the horizontal distance between two wave crests),
s.zh: 波长（即两个波峰之间的水平距离）

s.en: and a period (which is the time it takes a wave crest to travel one wave length).
s.zh: 以及周期（即波峰传播一个波长所需的时间）。

s.en: Although an ocean wave gives the impression of a wall of water moving in your direction,
s.zh: 虽然海浪看起来像是一堵朝你方向涌来的水墙，

s.en: in actuality waves move through the water leaving the water about where it was.
s.zh: 实际上，波浪在水中传播时，水本身基本停留在原处。

s.en: If the water was moving with the wave,
s.zh: 如果水是随着波浪一起运动的……

s.en: the ocean and everything on it would be racing in to the shore with obviously catastrophic results.
s.zh: 海洋以及其中的一切都会被冲向海岸，这显然会造成灾难性的后果。

s.en: An ocean wave passing through deep water causes a particle on the surface to move in a roughly circular orbit,
s.zh: 当海浪穿过深水区域时，水面上的一个颗粒会沿着近似圆形的轨道运动。

s.en: drawing the particle first towards the advancing wave, then up into the wave,
s.zh: 首先将粒子吸引向前进的波浪，然后使其向上融入到波浪中。

s.en: then forward with it and then--as the wave leaves the particles behind--back to its starting point again.
s.zh: 然后随波浪前进，最后——当波浪离开粒子后——粒子又回到起点。

s.en: From birth to maturity to death, a wave is subject to the same laws as any other 'living' thing.
s.zh: 从诞生到成熟再到消亡，海浪也遵循着与其他'生命体'相同的规律。

s.en: For a time it assumes a miraculous individuality that, in the end, is reabsorbed into the great ocean of life.
s.zh: 在一段时间内，它展现出一种仿佛奇迹般的独特性；然而最终，这种独特性还是被重新融入了浩瀚的生命之海中。

s.en: The undulating waves of the open sea are generated by three natural causes:
s.zh: 开阔海域中那些起伏的波浪是由三种自然原因形成的：

s.en: wind, earth movements or tremors, and the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun.
s.zh: 风、地壳运动或震动，以及月球和太阳的引力。

s.en: Once waves have been generated,
s.zh: 一旦海浪被生成

s.en: gravity is the force that drives them in a continual attempt to restore the ocean surface to a flat plain.
s.zh: 重力是驱动波浪的力量，它不断试图使海面恢复平坦。

q: What false impression does an ocean wave convey to the observer?
海浪会给观察者留下什么样的错误印象呢？

s.en: Two main techniques have been used for training elephants, which we may call respectively the tough and the gentle.
s.zh: 训练大象主要采用了两种方法，我们可以分别将它们称为“强硬型”方法与“温和型”方法。

s.en: The former method simply consists of setting an elephant to work and beating him until he does what is expected of him.
s.zh: 前一种方法很简单：就是让大象开始工作，然后不断地鞭打它，直到它按照要求去做为止。

s.en: Apart from any moral considerations this is a stupid method of training,
s.zh: 抛开任何道德方面的考虑不谈，这种训练方法实在愚蠢至极。

s.en: for it produces a resentful animal who at a later stage may well turn man-killer.
s.zh: 因为这会造就一只心怀怨恨的动物，而这种动物在未来很可能会变成杀人凶手。

s.en: The gentle method requires more patience in the early stages,
s.zh: 这种温和的方法在初期需要更多的耐心。

s.en: but produces a cheerful good-tempered elephant who will give many years of loyal service.
s.zh: 不过，最终会诞生出一头性格开朗、脾气温和的大象，它将为我们提供多年忠诚的服务。

s.en: The first essential in elephant training is to assign to the animal a single mahout who will be entirely responsible for the job.
s.zh: 在大象训练中，首要的一点就是为每头大象指定一名专门的驯象师，这名驯象师将完全负责大象的训练工作。

s.en: Elephants like to have one master just as dogs do, and are capable of a considerable degree of personal affection.
s.zh: 大象和狗一样，也需要一个主人，并且能够表现出相当程度的个人情感。

s.en: There are even stories of half-trained elephant calves who have refused to feed and pined to death
s.zh: 甚至还有这样的故事：那些只接受过部分训练的小象会拒绝进食，最终因思念而憔悴而死。

s.en: when by some unavoidable circumstance they have been deprived of their own trainer.
s.zh: 当由于某些不可避免的情况，它们失去了自己的驯象师时……

s.en: Such extreme cases must probably be taken with a grain of salt,
s.zh: 对于这类极端案例，我们或许应该持保留态度。

s.en: but they do underline the general principle that the relationship between elephant and mahout is the key to successful training.
s.zh: 但他们确实强调了这样一个基本原则：大象与驯象师之间的关系是成功训练大象的关键。

s.en: The most economical age to capture an elephant for training is between 15 and 20 years,
s.zh: 捕捉大象进行训练最经济的年龄是在15到20岁之间，

s.en: for it is then almost ready to undertake heavy work and can begin to earn its keep straight away.
s.zh: 因为那时它已经差不多准备好承担繁重的工作了，可以立即开始挣回自己的饲养成本。

s.en: But animals of this age do not easily become subservient to man, and a very firm hand must be employed in the early stages.
s.zh: 但是这个年龄段的动物并不容易屈服于人类，在初期阶段，必须采取非常强硬的手段。

s.en: The captive elephant, still roped to a tree,
s.zh: 那头被囚禁的大象仍然被绳子拴在树上……

s.en: plunges and screams every time a man approaches, and for several days will probably refuse all food through anger and fear.
s.zh: 每当有人靠近时，它就会惊慌失措、尖叫不已；出于愤怒和恐惧，它可能会连续几天拒绝进食。

s.en: Sometimes a tame elephant is tethered nearby to give the wild one confidence,
s.zh: 有时候，人们会把一头驯服的大象拴在附近，以此来让野生的大象感到安心（或有安全感）。

s.en: and in most cases the captive gradually quietens down and begins to accept its food.
s.zh: 在大多数情况下，被捕获的大象会逐渐安静下来，并开始接受食物。

s.en: The next stage is to get the elephant to the training establishment,
s.zh: 下一个步骤是将大象送到训练机构去。

s.en: a ticklish business which is achieved with the aid of two tame elephants roped to the captive on either side.
s.zh: 这是一项棘手的工作，需要借助两头驯服的大象来完成，它们被绳子拴在被捕获大象的两侧。

s.en: When several elephants are being trained at one time,
s.zh: 当同时有多头大象正在接受训练时，

s.en: it is customary for the new arrival to be placed between the stalls of two captives whose training is already well advanced.
s.zh: 按照惯例，新来的大象会被安排在两头训练已有相当进展的被捕获大象的围栏之间。

s.en: It is then left completely undisturbed with plenty of food and water
s.zh: 之后，它就被完全不受打扰地留下，周围有充足的食物和水。

s.en: so that it can absorb the atmosphere of its new home and see that nothing particularly alarming is happening to its companions.
s.zh: 这样它就能适应新家的氛围，并看到它的同伴们没有遇到任何特别令人惊慌的事情。

s.en: When it is eating normally, its own training begins.
s.zh: 当它开始正常进食时，它自己的训练就开始了。

s.en: The trainer stands in front of the elephant holding a long stick with a sharp metal point.
s.zh: 驯象师站在大象面前，手中拿着一根带有锋利金属尖端的长棍。

s.en: Two assistants, mounted on tame elephants, control the captive from either side,
s.zh: 两名助手骑在驯服的大象背上，从两侧控制着被捕获的大象，

s.en: while others rub their hands over his skin to the accompaniment of a monotonous and soothing chant.
s.zh: 而其他人则一边重复着单调而舒缓的吟唱，一边用手抚摸它的皮肤。

s.en: This is supposed to induce pleasurable sensations in the elephant,
s.zh: 这应该是为了给大象带来愉悦的感觉。

s.en: and its effects are reinforced by the use of endearing epithets,
s.zh: 其效果通过使用那些亲切、可爱的称呼（或称谓）得到了进一步的强化。

s.en: such as 'ho! my son', or 'ho! my father', or 'my mother', according to the age and sex of the captive.
s.zh: 例如“嗬！我的儿子”或“嗬！我的父亲”，或者“我的母亲”——这些称呼会根据被捕获大象的年龄和性别来决定。

s.en: The elephant is not immediately susceptible to such blandishments, however, and usually lashes fiercely with its trunk in all directions.
s.zh: 然而，大象并不会立刻被这些花言巧语所打动；它通常会用鼻子猛烈地朝四面八方挥打。

s.en: These movements are controlled by the trainer with the metal-pointed stick,
s.zh: 这些动作由驯象师用带金属尖的棍子来控制，

s.en: and the trunk eventually becomes so sore that the elephant curls it up and seldom afterwards uses it for offensive purposes.
s.zh: 最终，大象的鼻子会变得非常疼痛；因此大象会将其蜷缩起来，之后也很少再使用它的鼻子来进行攻击性动作。

q: At what point does the training of a captive wild elephant begin?
圈养野生大象的训练是从什么时候开始的呢？

s.en: An earthquake comes like a thief in the night, without warning.
s.zh: 地震就像夜间的小偷一样，毫无预兆地突然降临。

s.en: It was necessary, therefore, to invent instruments that neither slumbered nor slept.
s.zh: 因此，有必要发明那些既不会打盹也不会睡觉的仪器。

s.en: Some devices were quite simple.
s.zh: 有些设备的设计非常简单。

s.en: One, for instance, consisted of rods of various lengths and thicknesses which would stand up on end like ninepins.
s.zh: 例如，其中有一个装置由长度和厚度各不相同的杆子组成；这些杆子可以像九柱戏（ninepins）中的柱子一样竖立起来。

s.en: When a shock came, it shook the rigid table upon which these stood.
s.zh: 当震动来临时，它震动了这些杆子所放置的坚硬桌子。

s.en: If it were gentle, only the more unstable rods fell.
s.zh: 如果震动轻微，只有较不稳定的杆子会倒下。

s.en: If it were severe, they all fell.
s.zh: 如果震动剧烈，它们就全部倒下。

s.en: Thus the rods, by falling, and by the direction in which they fell,
s.zh: 因此，这些杆子通过倒下以及倒下的方向，

s.en: recorded for the slumbering scientist the strength of a shock that was too weak to waken him,
s.zh: 为那位正在沉睡的科学家记录下了那次冲击的强度——不过那次冲击实在太微弱了，根本无法将他唤醒。

s.en: and the direction from which it came.
s.zh: 以及它来自的方向。

s.en: But instruments far more delicate than that were needed if any really serious advance was to be made.
s.zh: 但是，如果要取得真正重大的进展，就需要使用比那些仪器更加精密的设备。

s.en: The ideal to be aimed at was to devise an instrument that could record with a pen on paper,
s.zh: 理想的目标是设计出一种能用笔在纸上记录的仪器，

s.en: the movements of the ground or of the table as the quake passed by.
s.zh: 记录地震经过时地面或桌子的运动。

s.en: While I write my pen moves, but the paper keeps still.
s.zh: 当我写字时，笔在动，但纸却静止不动。

s.en: With practice, no doubt, I could in time learn to write by holding the pen still while the paper moved.
s.zh: 毫无疑问，通过练习，我最终能学会保持笔不动而让纸动来写字。

s.en: That sounds a silly suggestion,
s.zh: 那听起来真是个愚蠢的建议。

s.en: but that was precisely the idea adopted in some of the early instruments (seismometers) for recording earthquake waves.
s.zh: 但这正是某些早期地震仪在记录地震波时所采用的设计理念。

s.en: But when table, penholder and paper are all moving, how is it possible to write legibly?
s.zh: 但是当桌子、笔架和纸张都在移动时，怎么可能还能写出清晰可读的文字呢？

s.en: The key to a solution of that problem lay in an everyday observation.
s.zh: 解决那个问题的关键在于一个日常的观察结果。

s.en: Why does a person standing in a bus or train tend to fall when a sudden start is made?
s.zh: 为什么当公交车或火车突然启动时，站在上面的人容易摔倒呢？

s.en: It is because his feet move on, but his head stays still.
s.zh: 这是因为他的脚向前移动，而头部却保持静止。

s.en: A simple experiment will help us a little further.
s.zh: 一个简单的实验能帮助我们进一步理解这个原理。

s.en: Tie a heavy weight at the end of a long piece of string.
s.zh: 在一段较长的绳子末端系上一个重物。

s.en: With the hand held high in the air, hold the string so that the weight nearly touches the ground.
s.zh: 将绳子高高举过头顶，使重物几乎触碰到地面。

s.en: Now move the hand to and fro and around but not up and down.
s.zh: 现在让手前后左右移动，但不要上下移动。

s.en: It will be found that the weight moves but slightly or not at all.
s.zh: 你会发现重物几乎不动，或者只轻微移动。

s.en: Imagine a pen attached to the weight in such a way that its point rests upon a piece of paper on the floor.
s.zh: 想象一下，有一支笔被固定在重物上，其笔尖接触着地面上的一张纸。

s.en: Imagine an earthquake shock shaking the floor, the paper, you and your hand.
s.zh: 再想象一场地震，地震使地面、纸张以及你的手都在震动。

s.en: In the midst of all this movement, the weight and the pen would be still.
s.zh: 在所有这些运动中，重物和笔会保持静止。

s.en: But as the paper moved from side to side under the pen point, its movement would be recorded in ink upon its surface.
s.zh: 但当纸张在笔尖下左右移动时，它的运动就会以墨迹记录在纸面上。

s.en: It was upon this principle that the first instruments were made, but the paper was wrapped round a drum which rotated slowly.
s.zh: 最早的测量仪器就是基于这个原理制造的——只不过当时的纸张是缠绕在一个缓慢旋转的鼓上的。

s.en: As long as all was still, the pen drew a straight line,
s.zh: 当一切保持静止时，笔会画出一条直线；

s.en: but while the drum was being shaken, the line that the pen was drawing wriggled from side to side.
s.zh: 但当鼓被震动时，笔所画的线就会左右摆动。

s.en: The apparatus thus described, however,
s.zh: 然而，上面描述的装置

s.en: records only the horizontal component of the wave movement, which is, in fact, much more complicated.
s.zh: 只能记录波动的水平分量，而实际上波动要复杂得多。

s.en: If we could actually see the path described by a particle,
s.zh: 如果我们能真的看到粒子所描绘的路径，

s.en: such as a sand grain in the rock,
s.zh: 就像岩石中的一粒沙子一样……

s.en: it would be more like that of a bluebottle buzzing round the room; it would be up and down, to and fro and from side to side.
s.zh: 它会更像一只绿头苍蝇在房间里嗡嗡飞舞：上下、前后、左右地移动。

s.en: Instruments have been devised and can be so placed that all three elements can be recorded in different graphs.
s.zh: 已经设计出可以适当放置的仪器，从而能将这三个要素记录在不同的图表上。

s.en: When the instrument is situated at more than 700 miles from the earthquake centre,
s.zh: 当该仪器距离地震中心超过700英里时，

s.en: the graphic record shows three waves arriving one after the other at short intervals.
s.zh: 图纸上会显示出三列波以较短的时间间隔相继到达。

s.en: The first records the arrival of longitudinal vibrations.
s.zh: 第一列波记录了纵向振动的到达。

s.en: The second marks the arrival of transverse vibrations which travel more slowly and arrive several minutes after the first.
s.zh: 第二列波标志着横向振动的到达；这些振动传播较慢，在第一列波到达几分钟后才传来。

s.en: These two have travelled through the earth.
s.zh: 这两列波已经穿过地球。

s.en: It was from the study of these that so much was learnt about the interior of the earth.
s.zh: 正是通过研究这两列波，人类才对地球内部有了如此多的了解。

s.en: The third, or main wave is the slowest and has travelled round the earth through the surface rocks.
s.zh: 第三列波即主波传播最慢，它是通过地表岩石环绕地球传播的。

q: What does a pen have to do to record on paper the vibrations generated by an earthquake?
一支笔要如何才能在纸上记录下地震产生的震动呢？

s.en: We must conclude from the work of those who have studied the origin of life,
s.zh: 我们必须从那些研究生命起源的科学家们的研究成果中得出结论。

s.en: that given a planet only approximately like our own, life is almost certain to start.
s.zh: 只要有一颗行星的条件与我们的地球大致相似，生命几乎必然会诞生。

s.en: Of all the planets in our solar system, we are now pretty certain the Earth is the only one on which life can survive.
s.zh: 在我们太阳系中的所有行星中，我们现在可以相当确定：地球是唯一一个适合生命生存的星球。

s.en: Mars is too dry and poor in oxygen, Venus far too hot, and so is Mercury,
s.zh: 火星太干燥且氧气含量极低；金星的温度过高；水星的情况也是如此。

s.en: and the outer planets have temperatures near absolute zero and hydrogen-dominated atmospheres.
s.zh: 外行星的温度接近绝对零度，其大气层主要由氢气构成。

s.en: But other suns, stars as the astronomers call them, are bound to have planets like our own, and as the number of stars in the universe is so vast,
s.zh: 但是其他恒星（正如天文学家所称的那样）肯定也拥有像我们地球这样的行星，而且由于宇宙中的恒星数量如此庞大，

s.en: this possibility becomes virtual certainty.
s.zh: 这种可能性几乎变成了必然的事实。

s.en: There are one hundred thousand million stars in our own Milky Way alone,
s.zh: 仅在我们自己的银河系中，就有一千亿颗恒星，

s.en: and then there are three thousand million other milky ways or galaxies, in the universe,
s.zh: 此外，宇宙中还有三十亿个类似的银河系或星系。

s.en: so the number of stars that we know exist is now estimated at about 300 million million million.
s.zh: 因此，目前已知的恒星数量估计约为3×10²⁰颗。

s.en: Although perhaps only 1 percent of the life that has started somewhere will develop into highly complex and intelligent patterns,
s.zh: 尽管在所有生命起源中，可能只有1%的生命会发展成高度复杂且具有智能的形态，

s.en: so vast is the number of planets, that intelligent life is bound to be a natural part of the universe.
s.zh: 行星的数量如此之多，以至于智慧生命必定是宇宙中自然存在的一部分。

s.en: If then we are so certain that other intelligent life exists in the universe, why have we had no visitors from outer space yet?
s.zh: 如果我们确信宇宙中存在其他智慧生命，那么为什么至今还没有来自外太空的访客呢？

s.en: First of all, they may have come to this planet of ours thousands or millions of years ago,
s.zh: 首先，他们可能早在几千甚至几百万年前就来到了我们的这个星球上。

s.en: and found our then prevailing primitive state completely uninteresting to their own advanced knowledge.
s.zh: 他们发现我们当时所处的原始状态，与他们自己所拥有的先进知识相比，完全毫无吸引力（或者说：他们认为我们的原始状态极其乏味、毫无价值）。

s.en: Professor Ronald Bracewell, a leading American radio astronomer,
s.zh: 罗纳德·布雷斯韦尔教授是美国著名的射电天文学家。

s.en: argued in Nature that such a superior civilization, on a visit to our own solar system,
s.zh: 在《自然》杂志上论证说，这样一个高度发达的文明在造访我们的太阳系时，

s.en: may have left an automatic messenger behind to await the possible awakening of an advanced civilization.
s.zh: 它可能留下了一种自动信息传递系统，等待着某个先进文明的觉醒。

s.en: Such a messenger, receiving our radio and television signals,
s.zh: 这样的“信使”能够接收我们的无线电和电视信号。

s.en: might well re-transmit them back to its home-planet,
s.zh: 很可能会将这些信息重新传回它的母星。

s.en: although what impression any other civilization would thus get from us is best left unsaid.
s.zh: 不过，其他文明对我们会有怎样的印象，最好还是不要去说了。

s.en: But here we come up against the most difficult of all obstacles to contact with people on other planets
s.zh: 但在这里，我们遇到了与其他星球上的智慧生命建立联系时所面临的最大障碍。

s.en: -- the astronomical distances which separate us.
s.zh: ——那些将我们分隔开的天文距离。

s.en: As a reasonable guess, they might, on an average, be 100 light years away.
s.zh: 作为一个合理的猜测，它们平均可能距离我们大约100光年。

s.en: (A light year is the distance which light travels at 186,000 miles per second in one year, namely 6 million million miles.)
s.zh: （一光年是指光以每秒186,000英里的速度在一年内所行进的距离，即6万亿英里。）

s.en: Radio waves also travel at the speed of light,
s.zh: 无线电波的传播速度也与光速相同。

s.en: and assuming such an automatic messenger picked up our first broadcasts of the 1920's,
s.zh: 假设这样的自动通讯系统能够接收到我们20世纪20年代的首批广播信号的话……

s.en: the message to its home planet is barely halfway there.
s.zh: 那么这条信息传到它的母星才走了一半的路程。

s.en: Similarly, our own present primitive chemical rockets,
s.zh: 同样地，我们目前使用的原始化学火箭，

s.en: though good enough to orbit men, have no chance of transporting us to the nearest other star,
s.zh: 虽然这些飞船的性能已经足够好，可以载人进入太空轨道，但它们根本无法将我们送到离我们最近的另一颗恒星。

s.en: four light years away, let alone distances of tens or hundreds of light years.
s.zh: 而最近的恒星离我们也有4光年远，更不用说数十或数百光年的距离了。

s.en: Fortunately, there is a 'uniquely rational way' for us to communicate with other intelligent beings,
s.zh: 幸运的是，我们有一种“独特而理性的方式”来与其他智慧生物进行交流。

s.en: as Walter Sullivan has put it in his excellent book,
s.zh: 正如沃尔特·沙利文在其佳作

s.en: We Are not Alone.
s.zh: 《我们并不孤单》中所说。

s.en: This depends on the precise radio frequency of the 21-cm wavelength, or 1420 megacycles per second.
s.zh: 这取决于21厘米波长的精确无线电频率，即每秒1420兆周。

s.en: It is the natural frequency of emission of the hydrogen atoms in space and was discovered by us in 1951;
s.zh: 这是太空中氢原子的自然辐射频率，由我们在1951年发现；

s.en: it must be known to any kind of radio astronomer in the universe.
s.zh: 宇宙中任何射电天文学家都应该知道这个频率。

s.en: Once the existence of this wave-length had been discovered,
s.zh: 一旦这种波长的存在被确认，

s.en: it was not long before its use as the uniquely recognizable broadcasting frequency for interstellar communication was suggested.
s.zh: 人们很快便提出了将其作为星际通信的独特识别频率的想法。

s.en: Without something of this kind,
s.zh: 如果没有这样的频率，

s.en: searching for intelligences on other planets would be like trying to meet a friend in London without a pre-arranged rendezvous
s.zh: 在其它行星上寻找智慧生命就如同在伦敦与朋友见面时没有事先约定，

s.en: and absurdly wandering the streets in the hope of a chance encounter.
s.zh: 只能荒唐地在街头游荡，希望能偶然碰上一样。

q: What does the 'uniquely rational way' for us to communicate with other intelligent beings in space depend on?
我们与太空中其他智慧生物进行交流的“独特且理性的方式”究竟取决于什么呢？
q2: --ANTHONY MICHAELIS Are There Strangers in Space? from The Weekend Telegraph--
--安东尼·迈克尔 太空中有陌生人吗？ 来自《周末电讯报》--

s.en: Custom has not commonly been regarded as a subject of any great moment.
s.zh: 习俗通常不被认为是多么重要的研究课题。

s.en: The inner workings of our own brains we feel to be uniquely worthy of investigation,
s.zh: 我们觉得自己大脑的内部运作机制是特别值得研究的对象。

s.en: but custom, we have a way of thinking, is behaviour at its most commonplace.
s.zh: 而对于习俗，我们往往认为它只是最普通不过的行为。

s.en: As a matter of fact, it is the other way around.
s.zh: 事实上，情况恰恰相反。

s.en: Traditional custom, taken the world over,
s.zh: 纵观全世界，传统习俗是一整套细致的行为，

s.en: is a mass of detailed behaviour more astonishing than what any one person can ever evolve in individual actions,
s.zh: 比任何个人通过个体行动所能创造出来的都更令人惊讶，

s.en: no matter how aberrant.
s.zh: 无论这些行为多么反常（或离谱）。

s.en: Yet that is a rather trivial aspect of the matter.
s.zh: 然而，这其实只是问题中一个相当微不足道的方面罢了。

s.en: The fact of first-rate importance is the predominant role that custom plays in experience and in belief,
s.zh: 最重要的一点是：在人们的体验和信念中，习俗起着主导性的作用。

s.en: and the very great varieties it may manifest.
s.zh: 以及它可能展现出的极其多样的形式。

s.en: No man ever looks at the world with pristine eyes.
s.zh: 没有人能够以纯粹、未受污染的眼光来看待这个世界；

s.en: He sees it edited by a definite set of customs and institutions and ways of thinking.
s.zh: 他所看到的世界总是被特定的习俗、制度以及思维方式所塑造的。

s.en: Even in his philosophical probings he cannot go behind these stereotypes;
s.zh: 即使在哲学探索中，他也无法超越这些刻板印象；

s.en: his very concepts of the true and the false will still have reference to his particular traditional customs.
s.zh: 他对“真实”与“虚假”的概念依然会受到自己所属传统习俗的影响。

s.en: John Dewey has said in all seriousness that the part played by custom in shaping the behaviour of the individual,
s.zh: 约翰·杜威曾严肃地指出：习俗在塑造个人行为方面所起的作用，

s.en: as against any way in which he can affect traditional custom,
s.zh: 与个人试图改变传统习俗的能力相比，

s.en: is as the proportion of the total vocabulary of his mother tongue
s.zh: 就如同一个人母语的全部词汇量，

s.en: against those words of his own baby talk that are taken up into the vernacular of his family.
s.zh: 与他婴儿时期说出的、被纳入家庭日常用语的那几个词语之间的比例一样悬殊。

s.en: When one seriously studies the social orders that have had the opportunity to develop autonomously,
s.zh: 当人们认真研究那些有机会自主发展的社会秩序时，

s.en: the figure becomes no more than an exact and matter-of-fact observation.
s.zh: 这个比喻便不过是准确而客观的观察了。

s.en: The life history of the individual is first and foremost an accommodation
s.zh: 个人的生命历程，归根结底，就是一种适应过程。

s.en: to the patterns and standards traditionally handed down in his community.
s.zh: 遵循他所在社区中传统上流传下来的模式和标准。

s.en: From the moment of his birth,
s.zh: 从他出生的那一刻起，

s.en: the customs into which he is born shape his experience and behaviour.
s.zh: 他出生所处的风俗习惯塑造了他的经历和行为方式。

s.en: By the time he can talk, he is the little creature of his culture,
s.zh: 等到他能够说话的时候，他就已经完全融入了自己所处文化的圈子中，成为了那个文化环境中的“小成员”了。

s.en: and by the time he is grown and able to take part in its activities,
s.zh: 等到他长大到可以参与这些活动的时候……

s.en: its habits are his habits, its beliefs his beliefs, its impossibilities his impossibilities.
s.zh: 它的习惯就是他的习惯，它的信念就是他的信念，它所认为的不可能之事，也就是他所认为的不可能之事。

s.en: Every child that is born into his group will share them with him,
s.zh: 每个出生在这个群体中的孩子都会与他分享这些东西。

s.en: and no child born into one on the opposite side of the globe can ever achieve the thousandth part.
s.zh: 而任何一个出生在地球另一端的孩子，甚至不可能学到这些习俗的千分之一。

s.en: There is no social problem it is more incumbent upon us to understand than this of the role of custom.
s.zh: 没有哪个社会问题比“习俗的作用”更值得我们去深入了解的了。

s.en: Until we are intelligent as to its laws and varieties,
s.zh: 在我们弄清习俗的规律及其多样性之前，

s.en: the main complicating facts of human life must remain unintelligible.
s.zh: 人类生活中那些最复杂、最难以理解的因素，或许永远都无法被我们完全弄清楚。

s.en: The study of custom can be profitable only after certain preliminary propositions have been accepted,
s.zh: 只有接受某些基本前提之后，对习俗的研究才会有收获。

s.en: and some of these propositions have been violently opposed.
s.zh: 其中一些提议遭到了强烈的反对。

s.en: In the first place, any scientific study requires that there be no
s.zh: 首先，任何科学研究都要求，

s.en: preferential weighting of one or another of the items in the series it selects for its consideration.
s.zh: 对所选作考察对象的一组事物中的任何一项，都不应有所偏重。

s.en: In all the less controversial fields, like the study of cacti or termites or the nature of nebulae,
s.zh: 在所有争议较少的领域中，比如对仙人掌、白蚁的研究，或者对星云本质的探索，

s.en: the necessary method of study is to group the relevant material and to take note of all possible variant forms and conditions.
s.zh: 必要的学习方法是：将相关的学习材料整理成组，并记录下所有可能存在的变体形式和各种条件。

s.en: In this way, we have learned all that we know of the laws of astronomy, or of the habits of the social insects, let us say.
s.zh: 通过这种方式，我们了解了所有关于天文学定律的知识，或者比如说，关于社会性昆虫习性的知识。

s.en: It is only in the study of man himself that the major social sciences
s.zh: 唯独在研究人类自身时，主要的社会科学

s.en: have substituted the study of one local variation, that of Western civilization.
s.zh: 却用对一种地方性变体——西方文明——的研究，替代了这种全面考察的方法。

s.en: Anthropology was by definition impossible,
s.zh: 只要我们与原始人、

s.en: as long as these distinctions between ourselves and the primitive,
s.zh: 与野蛮人、与异教徒之间的这些区别观念，

s.en: ourselves and the barbarian, ourselves and the pagan, held sway over people's minds.
s.zh: 仍然支配着人们的思想，人类学按其定义就不可能成立。

s.en: It was necessary first to arrive at that degree of sophistication
s.zh: 首先，人们必须达到这样的认识水平：

s.en: where we no longer set our own belief against our neighbour's superstition.
s.zh: 不再把自己的信仰与邻人的所谓迷信区别对待。

s.en: It was necessary to recognize that these institutions which are based on the same premises, let us say the supernatural,
s.zh: 我们必须认识到：那些基于相同前提——比如超自然信念——的制度，

s.en: must be considered together, our own among the rest.
s.zh: 都应该被一并考虑——包括我们自己的信仰在内。

q: What influences us from the moment of birth?
从我们出生的那一刻起，有哪些因素在影响着我们呢？

s.en: In man's early days, competition with other creatures must have been critical.
s.zh: 在人类早期，与其他生物的竞争肯定至关重要。

s.en: But this phase of our development is now finished.
s.zh: 但我们发展的这个阶段现在已经结束了。

s.en: Indeed, we lack practice and experience nowadays in dealing with primitive conditions.
s.zh: 确实，如今我们在应对恶劣环境时缺乏相应的实践经验和能力。

s.en: I am sure that, without modern weapons,
s.zh: 我确信，如果没有现代武器的话，

s.en: I would make a very poor show of disputing the ownership of a cave with a bear, and in this I do not think that I stand alone.
s.zh: 如果我要和一只熊争论某个洞穴的所有权，那我肯定会表现得非常愚蠢。而且，我认为不止我一个人会有这种想法。

s.en: The last creature to compete with man was the mosquito.
s.zh: 最后一种与人类竞争的生物是蚊子。

s.en: But even the mosquito has been subdued by attention to drainage and by chemical sprays.
s.zh: 不过，就连蚊子也因为人们对排水系统的重视以及化学喷雾的使用而得到了控制。

s.en: Competition between ourselves, person against person, community against community, still persists, however; and it is as fierce as it ever was.
s.zh: 然而，人与人之间的竞争，社区之间的对立与冲突依然存在，而且依然和以往一样激烈。

s.en: But the competition of man against man is not the simple process envisioned in biology.
s.zh: 但是人与人之间的竞争，并不是生物学中所描述的那种简单的过程。

s.en: It is not a simple competition for a fixed amount of food determined by the physical environment,
s.zh: 这并不是为争夺由自然环境所决定的固定数量的食物而进行的简单竞争，

s.en: because the environment that determines our evolution is no longer essentially physical.
s.zh: 因为决定我们进化的环境已经不再是纯粹的物理环境。

s.en: Our environment is chiefly conditioned by the things we believe.
s.zh: 我们的环境在很大程度上是由我们的信念所塑造的。

s.en: Morocco and California are bits of the Earth in very similar latitudes,
s.zh: 摩洛哥和加利福尼亚都位于相似的纬度线上。

s.en: both on the west coasts of continents with similar climates, and probably with rather similar natural resources.
s.zh: 它们都位于各大洲的西海岸，拥有相似的气候条件，以及可能相当相似的自然资源。

s.en: Yet their present development is wholly different,
s.zh: 然而，他们目前的发展状况却完全不同。

s.en: not so much because of different people even,
s.zh: 其实，这并不完全是因为人与人之间的差异……

s.en: but because of the different thoughts that exist in the minds of their inhabitants.
s.zh: 但是，由于这些地方居民的思维方式各不相同，情况就变得复杂了。

s.en: This is the point I wish to emphasize.
s.zh: 这就是我想强调的重点。

s.en: The most important factor in our environment is the state of our own minds.
s.zh: 我们环境中最重要的因素，就是我们自己心理的状态。

s.en: It is well known that where the white man has invaded a primitive culture,
s.zh: 众所周知，每当白人侵入原始文化时，

s.en: the most destructive effects have come not from physical weapons but from ideas.
s.zh: 最具破坏性的影响并非来自物理武器，而是来自思想。

s.en: Ideas are dangerous.
s.zh: 想法是危险的。

s.en: The Holy Office knew this full well when it caused heretics to be burned in days gone by.
s.zh: 在过去的岁月里，当宗教裁判所将异端分子处以火刑时，他们对此再清楚不过了。

s.en: Indeed, the concept of free speech only exists in our modern society because when you are inside a community,
s.zh: 的确，言论自由这一概念之所以能存在于现代社会，是因为当人们身处一个社群时，

s.en: you are conditioned by the conventions of the community to such a degree that it is very difficult to conceive of anything really destructive.
s.zh: 你深受社区习俗的影响，以至于很难想象任何真正具有破坏性的行为或事物。

s.en: It is only someone looking on from outside that can inject the dangerous thoughts.
s.zh: 只有那些从外部观察的人，才有可能灌输那些危险的思想。

s.en: I do not doubt that it would be possible to inject ideas into the modern world that would utterly destroy us.
s.zh: 我毫不怀疑，将某些有害的思想引入现代社会是完全可能的；这些思想很可能会对我们造成毁灭性的影响。

s.en: I would like to give you an example, but fortunately I cannot do so.
s.zh: 我想给你举个例子，但幸运的是，我无法做到这一点。

s.en: Perhaps it will suffice to mention the nuclear bomb.
s.zh: 或许只需提到核弹就足够了。

s.en: Imagine the effect on a reasonably advanced technological society,
s.zh: 想象一下这对一个技术相当先进的社会会产生什么样的影响吧。

s.en: one that still does not possess the bomb, of making it aware of the possibility, of supplying sufficient details to enable the thing to be constructed.
s.zh: 假如这个社会尚未拥有核弹，而有人使它意识到制造核弹的可能，并提供足以造出核弹的详细资料，会产生怎样的影响。

s.en: 20 or 30 pages of information handed to any of the major world powers around the year 1925,
s.zh: 大约在1925年，如果有任何世界大国收到这样20到30页的信息资料的话……

s.en: would have been sufficient to change the course of world history.
s.zh: 这本足以改变世界历史的进程。

s.en: It is a strange thought, but I believe a correct one,
s.zh: 这是个奇怪的想法，但我相信它是正确的。

s.en: that twenty or thirty pages of ideas and information would be capable of turning the present-day world upside down, or even destroying it.
s.zh: 那些二十到三十页的内容有可能彻底改变当今的世界，甚至将其摧毁。

s.en: I have often tried to conceive of what those pages might contain,
s.zh: 我经常试图想象那些页面上可能包含些什么内容。

s.en: but of course I cannot do so because I am a prisoner of the present-day world, just as all of you are.
s.zh: 但当然，我无法做到这一点——因为我就像你们所有人一样，是这个现代社会的“囚徒”。

s.en: We cannot think outside the particular patterns that our brains are conditioned to, or,
s.zh: 我们无法跳出大脑所习惯的特定思维模式来进行思考。

s.en: to be more accurate we can think only a very little way outside and then only if we are very original.
s.zh: 更准确地说，我们只能稍微超出常规思维的范围去思考；而且只有当我们真正具备创新性时，才能做到这一点。

q: What is the most influential factor in any human society?
在任何人类社会中，最具影响力的因素是什么？

s.en: A gifted American psychologist has said, 'Worry is a spasm of the emotion;
s.zh: 一位才华横溢的美国心理学家曾说过：“忧虑其实是一种情绪的突然发作。”

s.en: the mind catches hold of something and will not let it go.'
s.zh: “人的思维一旦抓住了某个想法或概念，就会紧紧不放。”

s.en: It is useless to argue with the mind in this condition.
s.zh: 在这种状态下，试图用道理说服自己的头脑是没有用的。

s.en: The stronger the will, the more futile the task.
s.zh: 意志越坚强，这项任务就越显得徒劳无功。

s.en: One can only gently insinuate something else into its convulsive grasp.
s.zh: 人们只能小心翼翼地、慢慢地将其他东西引入它那“抽搐般”的、难以控制的掌控之中。

s.en: And if this something else is rightly chosen, if it is really attended by the illumination of another field of interest,
s.zh: 那么，如果这个“其他的东西”被正确地选中了，如果它确实能带来另一个兴趣领域的启迪，

s.en: gradually, and often quite swiftly, the old undue grip relaxes and the process of recuperation and repair begins.
s.zh: 慢慢地，而且往往速度相当快，那些旧有的、不必要的束缚就会逐渐消失，身体开始恢复和修复的过程。

s.en: The cultivation of a hobby and new forms of interest is therefore a policy of the first importance to a public man.
s.zh: 因此，培养个人爱好和新的兴趣爱好对于一位公众人物来说是一项至关重要的政策。

s.en: But this is not a business that can be undertaken in a day or swiftly improvised by a mere command of the will.
s.zh: 但这并不是一项能够在一天内完成、或者仅仅通过一时的意志力就能迅速解决的事情。

s.en: The growth of alternative mental interests is a long process.
s.zh: 培养其他类型的兴趣爱好是一个漫长的过程。

s.en: The seeds must be carefully chosen; they must fall on good ground;
s.zh: 种子必须经过精心挑选；它们必须被种在肥沃的土壤里。

s.en: they must be sedulously tended, if the vivifying fruits are to be at hand when needed.
s.zh: 如果想要在需要时立即获得那些能够带来活力的成果，就必须对这些事物进行精心照料。

s.en: To be really happy and really safe, one ought to have at least two or three hobbies, and they must all be real.
s.zh: 要想真正获得幸福和安全感，一个人至少应该有两到三个爱好，而且这些爱好都必须是真实存在的。

s.en: It is no use starting late in life to say: 'I will take an interest in this or that.'
s.zh: 人生晚些时候才开始说“我想对这件事或那件事产生兴趣”，也是无济于事的。

s.en: Such an attempt only aggravates the strain of mental effort.
s.zh: 这样的尝试只会加剧精神上的压力。

s.en: A man may acquire great knowledge of topics unconnected with his daily work, and yet get hardly any benefit or relief.
s.zh: 一个人可能会在那些与他的日常工作无关的领域获得丰富的知识，但却几乎无法从中获得任何实际的好处或帮助。

s.en: It is no use doing what you like; you have got to like what you do.
s.zh: 光做自己喜欢的事情是没有用的；你必须真正喜欢自己所做的事情。

s.en: Broadly speaking, human beings may be divided into three classes:
s.zh: 广义上讲，人类可以分为三类：

s.en: those who are toiled to death, those who are worried to death, and those who are bored to death.
s.zh: 那些累死的人，那些担心死的人，以及那些无聊死的人。

s.en: It is no use offering the manual labourer,
s.zh: 让经过一周辛苦劳动、已经筋疲力尽的体力劳动者，

s.en: tired out with a hard week's sweat and effort the chance of playing a game of football or baseball on Saturday afternoon.
s.zh: 在星期六下午去踢足球或打棒球，是没有用的。

s.en: It is no use inviting the politician or the professional or business man, who has been working or worrying about serious things for six days,
s.zh: 邀请那位政客、专业人士或商人是没有用的——他们已经连续六天都在处理一些严肃、重要的事务了，根本无暇顾及其他事情。

s.en: to work or worry about trifling things at the weekend.
s.zh: 在周末的时候，就别去忙那些琐碎的事情了，也别为此烦恼了。

s.en: As for the unfortunate people who can command everything they want,
s.zh: 至于那些不幸的人——他们虽然能够随心所欲地支配一切，

s.en: who can gratify every caprice and lay their hands on almost every object of desire--for them a new pleasure, a new excitement is only an additional satiation.
s.zh: 那些能够满足自己所有的任性欲望、几乎可以得到任何想要的东西的人，对他们来说，新的快乐或新的刺激只不过使他们更加厌腻罢了。

s.en: In vain they rush frantically round from place to place, trying to escape from avenging boredom by mere clatter and motion.
s.zh: 他们徒劳地四处奔忙，试图通过制造噪音和动作来逃避那种令人痛苦的、无意义的无聊感。

s.en: For them discipline in one form or another is the most hopeful path.
s.zh: 对他们来说，无论以何种形式存在，自我约束都是摆脱无聊最有希望的途径。

s.en: It may also be said that rational, industrious, useful human beings are divided into two classes:
s.zh: 也可以这样说：那些理性、勤奋且有用的人被分成了两个阶层。

s.en: first, those whose work is work and whose pleasure is pleasure;
s.zh: 首先，那些将工作视为工作、将娱乐视为娱乐的人；

s.en: and secondly, those whose work and pleasure are one.
s.zh: 其次，那些将工作与个人乐趣融为一体的人。

s.en: Of these the former are the majority. They have their compensations.
s.zh: 其中，前者占大多数。它们也有自己的优势。

s.en: The long hours in the office or the factory bring with them as their reward,
s.zh: 在办公室或工厂长时间工作所带来的“回报”是……

s.en: not only the means of sustenance, but a keen appetite for pleasure even in its simplest and most modest forms.
s.zh: 人们不仅需要维持生计的手段，同时也渴望享受各种乐趣——哪怕这些乐趣是最简单、最朴素的。

s.en: But Fortune's favoured children belong to the second class.
s.zh: 但那些得到命运眷顾的幸运儿属于第二类。

s.en: Their life is a natural harmony.
s.zh: 他们的生活充满了和谐与宁静。

s.en: For them the working hours are never long enough.
s.zh: 对他们来说，工作时间永远都不够长；每一天都像节日一样美好。

s.en: Each day is a holiday, and ordinary holidays, when they come, are grudged as enforced interruptions in an absorbing vocation.
s.zh: 然而，当普通的假期到来时，他们却会将其视为对这份令人着迷的工作的打扰，因而感到不满。

s.en: Yet to both classes, the need of an alternative outlook, of a change of atmosphere, of a diversion of effort, is essential.
s.zh: 其实，对于这两个阶层的人来说，都需要一种不同的生活方式、一种能够改变氛围、转移注意力的方式。

s.en: Indeed, it may well be that those whose work is their pleasure are those who most need the means of banishing it at intervals from their minds.
s.zh: 事实上，那些将工作视为乐趣的人，或许正是最需要偶尔将工作从脑海中暂时抛开的人。

q: Who, according to the author, are 'Fortune's favoured children'?
根据作者的观点，谁是《财富》杂志所青睐的“宠儿”呢？
q2: ——温斯顿·丘吉尔 《绘画作为一种消遣》——

s.en: Economy is one powerful motive for camping,
s.zh: 经济因素是人们选择露营的一个重要原因。

s.en: since after the initial outlay upon equipment, or through hiring it, the total expense can be far less than the cost of hotels.
s.zh: 因为在购买了设备或租用设备之后，总花费可能远低于住酒店的费用。

s.en: But, contrary to a popular assumption, it is far from being the only one, or even the greatest.
s.zh: 但是，与普遍的看法相反，这远非唯一的动机，甚至也不是最主要的动机。

s.en: The man who manoeuvres carelessly into his 20 pounds' worth of space at one of Europe's myriad permanent sites may find himself bumping a Bentley.
s.zh: 在欧洲众多永久性露营地中，那个开车时不小心驶入自己花20英镑租来的营位的人，可能会发现自己撞上了一辆宾利。

s.en: More likely, Ford Escort will be hub to hub with Renault or Mercedes, but rarely with bicycles made for two.
s.zh: 更有可能的是，福特Escort会与雷诺或奔驰并排停放，但很少会与双人自行车并排。

s.en: That the equipment of modern camping becomes yearly more sophisticated is an entertaining paradox for the cynic,
s.zh: 对于那些持悲观态度的人来说，现代露营装备逐年变得越来越先进，这确实是一个颇具讽刺意味的矛盾现象。

s.en: a brighter promise for the hopeful traveller who has sworn to get away from it all.
s.zh: 对于那些渴望逃离现实、追求自由生活的旅行者来说，这无疑是一个更加光明的希望。

s.en: It also provides--and some student sociologist might care to base his thesis upon the phenomenon--an escape of another kind.
s.zh: 它还提供了一种不同的“逃避方式”；一些研究社会现象的学生或许会想以此作为自己论文的写作基础。

s.en: The modern traveller is often a man who dislikes the Splendide and the Bellavista,
s.zh: 现代旅行者往往不喜欢那些名为'辉煌'或'美景'的豪华酒店，

s.en: not because he cannot afford, or shuns their material comforts, but because he is afraid of them.
s.zh: 不是因为他买不起这些物质上的享受，也不是因为他拒绝它们，而是因为他害怕它们。

s.en: Affluent he may be, but he is by no means sure what to tip the doorman or the chambermaid.
s.zh: 尽管他很富有，但他仍然不知道该给门卫或客房服务员多少小费才合适。

s.en: Master in his own house he has little idea of when to say boo to a hotel manager.
s.zh: 在自己家里他或许很自在，但在酒店里，他完全不知道该如何与经理打交道。

s.en: From all such fears camping releases him.
s.zh: 面对所有这些恐惧，露营反而让他感到解脱。

s.en: Granted, a snobbery of camping itself, based upon equipment and techniques, already exists;
s.zh: 诚然，基于所使用的装备和技术，露营本身就带有一种“优越感”或“傲慢的态度”。

s.en: but it is of a kind that, if he meets it, he can readily understand and deal with.
s.zh: 不过，这种情况属于他能够轻易理解并妥善处理的类型。

s.en: There is no superior 'they' in the shape of managements and hotel hierarchies to darken his holiday days.
s.zh: 没有管理层和酒店等级制度中那些高高在上的'他们'来破坏他的假期心情。

s.en: To such motives, yet another must be added.
s.zh: 除了这些动机之外，还必须再加上另一个动机。

s.en: The contemporary phenomenon of car worship is to be explained not least by the sense of independence and freedom that ownership entails.
s.zh: 当代社会中对汽车的崇拜现象，很大程度上可以归因于汽车所有权所带来的独立感和自由感。

s.en: To this pleasure camping gives an exquisite refinement.
s.zh: 露营使这种独立自由的乐趣更加美妙。

s.en: From one's own front door to home or foreign hills or sands and back again, everything is to hand.
s.zh: 从自己家中的前门出发，无论是前往国内的山丘、沙漠，还是国外，无论走到哪里，一切所需的东西都唾手可得。

s.en: Not only are the means of arriving at the holiday paradise entirely within one's own command and keeping,
s.zh: 不仅前往这个度假天堂的方式完全由自己掌控，

s.en: but the means of escape from holiday hell (if the beach proves too crowded, the local weather too inclement)
s.zh: 而且，逃离“假期地狱”的手段——如果海滩过于拥挤、当地天气过于恶劣——

s.en: are there, outside--or, as likely, part of--the tent.
s.zh: 这些逃离'假期地狱'的手段就在帐篷外——或者很可能就是帐篷的一部分。

s.en: Idealists have objected to the practice of camping, as to the package tour,
s.zh: 理想主义者反对露营这种活动，也同样反对跟团旅游。

s.en: that the traveller abroad thereby denies himself the opportunity of getting to know the people of the country visited.
s.zh: 这意味着出国旅行的游客就失去了了解所访问国家人民的机会。

s.en: Insularity and self-containment, it is argued, go hand in hand.
s.zh: 有人认为，孤立主义与自我封闭是密不可分的。

s.en: The opinion does not survive experience of a popular Continental camping place.
s.zh: 这种观点在人们实际体验了那处热门的欧洲大陆露营地之后就被推翻了。

s.en: Holiday hotels tend to cater for one nationality of visitors especially, sometimes exclusively.
s.zh: 假日酒店通常主要服务于某一特定国籍的游客，有时甚至只接待该国籍的客人。

s.en: Camping sites, by contrast, are highly cosmopolitan.
s.zh: 相比之下，露营地具有很强的国际性。

s.en: Granted, a preponderance of Germans is a characteristic that seems common to most Mediterranean sites;
s.zh: 诚然，德国人的数量占多数似乎是大多数地中海地区共有的特征；

s.en: but as yet there is no overwhelmingly specialized patronage.
s.zh: 但到目前为止还没有出现压倒性的特定国籍客人。

s.en: Notices forbidding the open-air drying of clothes,
s.zh: 禁止户外晾晒衣物的告示，

s.en: or the use of water points for car washing,
s.zh: 禁止用水龙头洗车的告示，

s.en: or those inviting 'our camping friends' to a dance or a boat trip are printed not only in French or Italian or Spanish, but also in English, German and Dutch.
s.zh: 那些邀请“我们的露营伙伴”参加舞会或乘船旅行的邀请函，不仅用法语、意大利语和西班牙语印刷，还用英语、德语和荷兰语印刷。

s.en: At meal times the odour of sauerkraut vies with that of garlic.
s.zh: 用餐时，酸菜的味道与大蒜的味道交织在一起，令人难以忽视。

s.en: The Frenchman's breakfast coffee competes with the Englishman's bacon and eggs.
s.zh: 法国人的早餐咖啡与英国人的培根和鸡蛋形成了鲜明对比。

s.en: Whether the remarkable growth of organized camping means the eventual death of the more independent kind is hard to say.
s.zh: 很难说，有组织的露营活动的迅速发展是否意味着那些更加独立、自由式的露营方式的最终消亡。

s.en: Municipalities naturally want to secure the campers' site fees and other custom.
s.zh: 市政当局自然希望确保能收到露营者的场地费和其他消费。

s.en: Police are wary of itinerants who cannot be traced to a recognized camp boundary or to four walls.
s.zh: 警方对那些无法被追踪到任何已知营地范围或固定住所的流动人员保持警惕。

s.en: But most probably it will all depend upon campers themselves: how many heath fires they cause; how much litter they leave;
s.zh: 但很可能一切都取决于露营者自己：他们引发了多少野火；他们留下了多少垃圾；

s.en: in short, whether or not they wholly alienate landowners and those who live in the countryside.
s.zh: 简而言之，取决于他们是否会让土地所有者和乡村居民彻底厌恶他们。

s.en: Only good scouting is likely to preserve the freedoms so dear to the heart of the eternal Boy Scout.
s.zh: 只有良好的露营行为规范才可能保住那些永恒童子军心中珍视的自由。

s.en: There is no shortage of tipsters around offering 'get-rich-quick' opportunities.
s.zh: 到处都有那些提供“快速致富”机会的所谓投资顾问。

s.en: But if you are a serious private investor, leave the Las Vegas mentality to those with money to fritter.
s.zh: 但如果你是一位认真的私人投资者，那就把那种“拉斯维加斯式”的赌博心态留给那些有钱挥霍的人吧。

s.en: The serious investor needs a proper 'portfolio' --a well-planned selection of investments, with a definite structure and a clear aim.
s.zh: 一位精明的投资者需要一个合理的“投资组合”——即一系列经过精心策划的投资项目，这些投资项目应具有明确的结构和清晰的目标。

s.en: But exactly how does a newcomer to the stock market go about achieving that?
s.zh: 但是，对于一个刚进入股票市场的新人来说，究竟应该如何实现这一目标呢？

s.en: Well, if you go to five reputable stock brokers and ask them what you should do with your money,
s.zh: 那么，如果你去找五家信誉良好的股票经纪公司，询问他们你应该如何处理自己的资金，

s.en: you're likely to get five different answers,
s.zh: 你很可能会得到五个不同的答案。

s.en: --  even if you give all the relevant information about your age, family, finances and what you want from your investments.
s.zh: ——即使你提供了所有关于自己年龄、家庭状况、财务状况以及你对投资的具体期望的相关信息。

s.en: Moral? There is no one 'right' way to structure a portfolio.
s.zh: 结论？其实，并不存在唯一一种“正确”的投资组合构建方式。

s.en: However, there are undoubtedly some wrong ways, and you can be sure that none of our five advisers
s.zh: 不过，错误的做法确实存在；可以肯定，我们的五位顾问中没有一位

s.en: would have suggested sinking all (or perhaps any) of your money into Periwigs.
s.zh: 会建议你把全部资金（甚至可能一分钱）投入 Periwigs 公司。

s.en: So what should you do?
s.zh: 那么你应该怎么做呢？

s.en: We'll assume that you have sorted out the basics--like mortgages, pensions, insurance and access to sufficient cash reserves.
s.zh: 我们假设你已经处理好了所有基本问题，比如抵押贷款、养老金、保险以及确保自己拥有足够的现金储备。

s.en: You should then establish your own individual aims.
s.zh: 然后，你应该确立自己个人的奋斗目标（或目标）。

s.en: These are partly a matter of personal circumstances, partly a matter of psychology.
s.zh: 这部分是由于个人情况造成的，另一部分则是心理因素在起作用。

s.en: For instance, if you are older you have less time to recover from any major losses, and you may well wish to boost your pension income.
s.zh: 例如，如果你年纪较大，那么你从重大损失中恢复过来的时间就会更少，因此你可能会希望增加自己的养老金收入。

s.en: So preserving your capital and generating extra income are your main priorities.
s.zh: 因此，保护你的资本并赚取额外收入是你最主要的优先事项。

s.en: In this case, you'd probably construct a portfolio with some shares (but not high risk ones), along with gilts, cash deposits,
s.zh: 在这种情况下，你可能会构建一个投资组合，其中包含一些股票（但不是高风险股票）、英国国债（gilts）以及现金存款。

s.en: and perhaps convertibles or the income shares of split capital investment trusts.
s.zh: 也许还包括可转换债券，或是分割资本投资信托的收益份额。

s.en: If you are younger, and in a solid financial position,
s.zh: 如果你比较年轻，且财务状况良好，

s.en: you may decide to take an aggressive approach--but only if you're blessed with a sanguine disposition and won't suffer sleepless nights over share prices.
s.zh: 你可以选择采取一种激进的做法——但前提是你必须具备乐观的心态，且不会因为股价的波动而夜不能寐。

s.en: If you recognize yourself in this description,
s.zh: 如果你在这段描述中看到了自己的影子……

s.en: you might include a couple of heady growth stocks in your portfolio, alongside your more pedestrian investments.
s.zh: 你可以在自己的投资组合中，除了那些较为稳健的投资之外，也加入一些高增长性的股票。

s.en: Once you have decided on your investment aims you can then decide where to put your money.
s.zh: 一旦你确定了自己的投资目标，就可以决定将资金投向何处了。

s.en: The golden rule here is spread your risk--if you put all of your money into Periwigs International,
s.zh: 这里的黄金法则是分散风险：如果你把所有的钱都投到 Periwigs International 公司里，

s.en: you're setting yourself up as a hostage to fortune.
s.zh: 你就是在听天由命了。

q: How does the older investor differ in his approach to investment from the younger investor?
年长的投资者在投资方式上与年轻的投资者有何不同？
